## P2 - `addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate` plans migrations by port name only; a destroyed client peer makes apply fail persistently

**Location:** [core/topology&#95;reconcile.go:482-518](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L482-L518)

**Problem:** `addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate` matches a stale bridge-side endpoint to a desired endpoint purely by identical port name under a different `BridgeNS` node and never inspects the client-side peer, even though the `bridgeNSMigration` comment asserts &#34;the client-side endpoint and the veth pair itself stay valid&#34;. Three apply sequences break&#58; &#40;a&#41; rewiring the client link to another interface in the same apply as the bridge move deletes the stale client end in `deleteApplyEndpoints`, which destroys the whole veth pair before `parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts` runs; &#40;b&#41; removing the client node in the same apply lets parking succeed but the container teardown destroys the peer and with it the parked half, so `RestoreBridgePort` fails; &#40;c&#41; removing the old bridge&#39;s parent in the same apply makes `bridgeNSMigParentNode` return &#34;parent container %q not found&#34; because it resolves parents only from the desired `c.Nodes`.

**Trigger:** An apply that simultaneously moves or recreates an in-container bridge and changes the fate of the port&#39;s client side&#58; the client link rewired to another interface or node, the client node removed, or the old parent container removed from the topology.

**Impact:** Every apply step returns early on error before `finalize`/`writeState`, so the failed apply persists nothing; the next apply re-plans the identical migration from the unchanged state and fails identically. The lab is bricked for that port until `destroy`, which destroys exactly the client-side state migration exists to preserve.

**Suggested correction:** Validate candidates at planning time&#58; skip the migration when the old bridge&#39;s parent cannot be resolved from the desired topology &#40;the delete/recreate path handles that case&#41; and require that the old link&#39;s client-side endpoint matches the new link&#39;s client endpoint and is not deleted in this plan. Add a small unit test for the guard; the new robot suite only covers a bridge move with an unchanged client.


## P2 - `UnlinkNamedNetNS` cannot remove a bind-mounted netns, so parking namespaces leak

**Location:** [utils/netlink.go:233-240](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/utils/netlink.go#L233-L240)

**Problem:** The parking netns is created with `netns.NewNamed`, which bind-mounts the namespace onto `/run/netns/<name>`. `UnlinkNamedNetNS` uses `os.Remove`, and unlink on a mount point fails with EBUSY on Linux; this is why the existing machinery uses `netns.DeleteNamed`, which umounts first. Both callers in [`links/migration.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L1-L1) &#40;lines 79 and 178&#41; discard the error with `_ =`, so the cleanup silently does nothing.

**Trigger:** Any bridge-port migration&#58; the success path in `RestoreBridgePort` leaks the netns on every migration, and the park-error path in `ParkBridgePortByOwnership` leaks the freshly created one.

**Impact:** `clab-park-<longName>` entries accumulate in `/run/netns`, remain visible to `ip netns list` after lab `destroy`, and mislead operators. The leak is bounded to one entry per bridge long name but is guaranteed and silent on the success path.

**Suggested correction:** Implement `UnlinkNamedNetNS` with the established umount+unlink pattern &#40;`netns.DeleteNamed`, as in `DefaultNode.cleanupParkingNetNS` and [`nodes/sros/netns.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/nodes/sros/netns.go#L1-L1)&#41; and stop discarding the returned error at both call sites, logging at debug level at minimum.


## P3 - Interrupted bridge-port migration is unrecoverable because parking is not idempotent

**Location:** [links/migration.go:57-81](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L57-L81)

**Problem:** Once `ParkBridgePortByOwnership` has moved a bridge-side end into the parking netns, the port carries the old bridge&#39;s ownership altname and sits in a namespace discovery never scans. If the apply fails after parking but before `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts`, the state file is unchanged, so the next apply re-plans the same migration and `findLinkByOwnershipAltName` fails in the parent&#39;s netns because the port is already parked. If a later apply succeeds without planning the migration, the parked port becomes invisible garbage.

**Trigger:** Any failure between step 2 &#40;`parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts`&#41; and step 8 &#40;`restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts`&#41; of the apply sequence in [`core/apply.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/apply.go#L1-L1), for example an unrelated node deploy error.

**Impact:** A transient failure converts a healthy lab into one where every subsequent apply aborts at the park step, and abandoning the migration silently strands the port with no cleanup path.

**Suggested correction:** Make parking idempotent&#58; before moving the port, check the parking netns of `longName` for an interface carrying the ownership altname and, if found, skip the move and let the existing restore path proceed. This turns an interrupted migration into a resumable one with a small local change.


## P4 - Dead `LinkDeploymentStateSetter`/`SetDeploymentState` and a comment describing a nonexistent mechanism

**Location:** [links/apply.go:79-84](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/apply.go#L79-L84)

**Problem:** This PR introduces the `LinkDeploymentStateSetter` interface and `LinkVEth.SetDeploymentState`, but a repository-wide search finds no call sites. Meanwhile the `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` comment claims &#34;The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed so `deployLinks` skips pair re-creation for it&#34;, which no code does; the actual mechanism is the `plan.addedLinks` filtering a few lines below in the same function.

**Trigger:** Read-only maintenance cost; no runtime trigger.

**Impact:** A dead exported interface invites future callers of an unused abstraction, and the misleading comment sends maintainers hunting for a deployment-state mechanism that does not exist.

**Suggested correction:** Delete `LinkDeploymentStateSetter` and `LinkVEth.SetDeploymentState` &#40;or wire them up if they were intended for a purpose this PR did not land&#41;, and reword the `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` comment to describe the actual `plan.addedLinks` filtering.


## P4 - `enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace` type-asserts `*netlink.Bridge` and can panic

**Location:** [nodes/bridge/bridge.go:308-308](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/nodes/bridge/bridge.go#L308-L308)

**Problem:** `netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName)` is unconditionally type-asserted to `*netlink.Bridge`. If a non-bridge device, such as a leftover veth whose port name collides with the bridge name, currently holds that name, the assertion panics inside the `PostDeploy` hook instead of returning an error.

**Trigger:** A device other than a bridge occupying the bridge&#39;s kernel name in the parent&#39;s netns during `PostDeploy`; an edge case, but a panic aborts the whole apply without diagnostics.

**Impact:** Crash instead of a clean error; low likelihood.

**Suggested correction:** Compare `link.Attrs().MasterIndex != bridgeLink.Attrs().Index` on the `netlink.Link` interface; the type assertion is unnecessary for the master check.

- Tests were not executed &#40;source-only review&#41;; runtime conclusions derive from code semantics including Linux veth pair destruction semantics and `netns.NewNamed` bind-mount behavior.
- The new robot suite covers bridge move with unchanged client, parent drift, add/remove clients, and idempotency; none of the finding-1 variants &#40;client rewire or removal combined with a bridge move, or removed old parent&#41; is exercised.
- Pre-existing issues excluded&#58; the unguarded slicing in bridge `CheckDeploymentConditions` &#40;base [`nodes/bridge/bridge.go:165`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/nodes/bridge/bridge.go#L165-L165)&#41; and the noop `bridge.Delete` leaving a removed in-container bridge behind in the parent both exist in base; the new migration flow depends on the latter but does not worsen it.
- Documentation check&#58; the `BridgeNS` feature and its &#60;bridge&#62;&#124;&#60;parent&#62; naming are already documented in [`docs/manual/kinds/bridge.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/docs/manual/kinds/bridge.md#L1-L1) &#40;unchanged in this PR&#41;; migration is internal apply behavior, so no doc or schema update is required by this PR.
- Verified-correct items&#58; the `rootNamespaceBased` `BridgeNS` grouping in [`core/runtime_state.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/runtime_state.go#L1-L1), the `SetNodesMap` wiring in [`core/config.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/config.go#L1-L1) and [`nodes/node.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/nodes/node.go#L1-L1), the exact cross-netns `PeerIndex` comparison in `linkIntact`, the nil-safety of `ref.node` in `deleteApplyEndpoints`, and the discovery order-independence of `discoverBridgeNSEndpoints`.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

76: diff --git a/core/apply_bridge_migration.go b/core/apply_bridge_migration.go
77: new file mode 100644
78: index 0000000..50dfd7b
79: --- /dev/null
80: +++ b/core/apply_bridge_migration.go
81: @@ -0,0 +1,149 @@
82: +package core
83: +
84: +import (
85: +	"context"
86: +	"fmt"
87: +	"strings"
88: +
89: +	"github.com/charmbracelet/log"
90: +	clablinks "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/links"
91: +	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
92: +)
93: +
94: +// bridgeNSMigParentNode resolves the namespace host of a migrated bridge-side
95: +// endpoint. Stale refs carry either a live bridge node (resolved via the
96: +// topology) or the name-encoded <bridge>|<parent> form of a node that is
97: +// already removed from the desired topology.
98: +func (c *CLab) bridgeNSMigParentNode(ref applyEndpointRef) (clablinks.Node, error) {
99: +	if parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSParentNode(ref.key.node); err == nil {
100: +		return parentNode, nil
101: +	}
102: +	parts := strings.SplitN(ref.key.node, "|", 2)
103: +	if len(parts) != 2 {
104: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot resolve namespace host of bridge %q", ref.key.node)
105: +	}
106: +	node, exists := c.Nodes[parts[1]]
107: +	if !exists {
108: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
109: +			"bridge %q: parent container %q not found",
110: +			ref.key.node,
111: +			parts[1],
112: +		)
113: +	}
114: +	return node, nil
115: +}
116: +
117: +// parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts parks bridge-side veth ends whose owning in-container
118: +// bridge was replaced by a bridge under a different parent (the move case).
119: +// The veth pair stays intact: only the parked half leaves the dying parent's
120: +// namespace, so the client-side end keeps its state untouched.
121: +func (c *CLab) parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts(
122: +	ctx context.Context,
123: +	plan *applyPlan,
124: +) error {
125: +	if plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {
126: +		return nil
127: +	}
128: +
129: +	for i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
130: +		mig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]
131: +
132: +		if mig.relocation != nil {
133: +			continue
134: +		}
135: +
136: +		// The old bridge node may already be deleted from the desired topology
137: +		// (the move case); resolve its namespace host by the name-encoded
138: +		// parent suffix, falling back to the normal resolution.
139: +		parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSMigParentNode(mig.staleRef)
140: +		if err != nil {
141: +			return err
142: +		}
143: +
144: +		newNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]
145: +		if !exists {
146: +			return fmt.Errorf("bridge migration target %q not found", mig.newKey.node)
147: +		}
148: +		longName := newNode.Config().LongName
149: +
150: +		relocation, err := clablinks.ParkBridgePortByOwnership(
151: +			ctx,
152: +			parentNode,
153: +			mig.staleRef.key.node,
154: +			mig.staleRef.key.iface,
155: +			longName,
156: +		)
157: +		if err != nil {
158: +			return err
159: +		}
160: +
161: +		mig.relocation = relocation
162: +	}
163: +
164: +	return nil
165: +}
166: +
167: +// restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts moves parked bridge-side ends into the replacement
168: +// bridge's parent namespace after that container (and the bridge) exist again,
169: +// relabels the ownership altname to the replacement bridge node, and re-enslaves
170: +// the port to the bridge. The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed so
171: +// deployLinks skips pair re-creation for it.
172: +func (c *CLab) restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts(
173: +	ctx context.Context,
174: +	plan *applyPlan,
175: +) error {
176: +	if plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {
177: +		return nil
178: +	}
179: +
180: +	for i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
181: +		mig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]
182: +
183: +		if mig.relocation == nil || plan.plannedLinkSet == nil {
184: +			continue
185: +		}
186: +
187: +		// Restore into the replacement bridge's parent namespace; the bridge
188: +		// node interfaces with the parent's ns through its GetNSPath override.
189: +		bridgeNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]
190: +		if !exists {
191: +			return fmt.Errorf("bridge migration target %q not found", mig.newKey.node)
192: +		}
193: +
194: +		if err := mig.relocation.RestoreBridgePort(
195: +			ctx,
196: +			bridgeNode,
197: +			mig.newKey.node,
198: +			bridgeNSNameInNamespace(mig.newKey.node),
199: +			clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(mig.newKey.iface),
200: +		); err != nil {
201: +			return err
202: +		}
203: +
204: +		// The migrated pair is complete end-to-end (the client-side end was
205: +		// never touched and the parked bridge-side half is restored and
206: +		// enslaved). Filter the corresponding replaced link out of addedLinks
207: +		// so endpoint removal and pair re-creation never touch it.
208: +		kept := plan.addedLinks[:0]
209: +		for _, link := range plan.addedLinks {
210: +			if clablinks.RuntimeEndpointsContainEndpoint(
211: +				link,
212: +				mig.newKey.node,
213: +				mig.newKey.iface,
214: +			) {
215: +				log.Info(
216: +					"Restored migrated bridge port into replacement bridge",
217: +					"bridge",
218: +					mig.newKey.node,
219: +					"port",
220: +					mig.newKey.iface,
221: +				)
222: +				continue
223: +			}
224: +			kept = append(kept, link)
225: +		}
226: +		plan.addedLinks = kept
227: +	}
228: +
229: +	return nil
230: +}

459: +				applyEndpointKey{node: bridgeEndpointPoint[0], iface: bridgeEndpointPoint[1]},

466: +// addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate registers a bridge NS migration when the
467: +// desired topology re-claims the given bridge-side endpoint under a different
468: +// in-container bridge node with the same logical port name.
469: +func (c *CLab) addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate(
470: +	plan *applyPlan,
471: +	staleKey applyEndpointKey,
472: +	staleNode clablinks.Node,
473: +) {
474: +	if staleKey.node == "" || staleKey.iface == "" {
475: +		return
476: +	}
477: +	if _, desired := plan.desiredEndpointSet[staleKey]; desired {
478: +		return
479: +	}
480: +	if c.isBridgeNSMigrationPlanned(plan, staleKey) {
481: +		return
482: +	}
483: +
484: +	for candidate := range plan.desiredEndpointSet {
485: +		if candidate.iface != staleKey.iface || candidate.node == staleKey.node {
486: +			continue
487: +		}
488: +		if !c.isBridgeNSNode(candidate.node) {
489: +			continue
490: +		}
491: +
492: +		plan.bridgeNSMigrations = append(plan.bridgeNSMigrations, bridgeNSMigration{
493: +			staleRef: applyEndpointRef{key: staleKey, node: staleNode},
494: +			newKey:   candidate,
495: +		})
496: +		log.Info(
497: +			"Planning bridge port migration",
498: +			"from",
499: +			staleKey.String(),
500: +			"to",
501: +			candidate.String(),
502: +		)
503: +		return
504: +	}
505: +}

507: +// isBridgeNSMigrationPlanned reports whether the given bridge endpoint is

509: +func (c *CLab) isBridgeNSMigrationPlanned(

514: +		if mig.staleRef.key == key {
515: +			return true
516: +		}
517: +	}
518: +	return false
519: +}

529: +		node.Config().Kind == "bridge" && strings.Contains(nodeName, "|")

877: @@ -0,0 +1,255 @@
878: +package links
879: +
880: +import (
881: +	"context"
882: +	"fmt"
883: +	"strings"
884: +
885: +	"github.com/charmbracelet/log"
886: +	"github.com/containernetworking/plugins/pkg/ns"
887: +	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
888: +	"github.com/vishvananda/netlink"
889: +)
890: +
891: +// NSMigrationNode is the minimal node surface the bridge-port migration
892: +// works with: exec context plus a resolvable namespace path.
893: +type NSMigrationNode interface {
894: +	ExecFunction(ctx context.Context, f func(ns.NetNS) error) error
895: +	GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
896: +	GetShortName() string
897: +}
898: +
899: +// BridgePortRelocation describes a bridge-side veth end parked out of one
900: +// namespace while the in-container bridge hosting it was replaced (a bridge
901: +// parent move). The veth pair stays intact across the namespace hops: the
902: +// client-side end keeps its address and MAC, and the parked half carries its
903: +// device state until it is restored into the replacement namespace.
904: +type BridgePortRelocation struct {
905: +	parkNSPath   string
906: +	KernelName   string // kernel-side name while parked
907: +	OldOwnerName string
908: +	IfaceName    string
909: +	LongName     string // replacement bridge node's long name; exercises the parking netns name
910: +}
911: +
912: +// ParkBridgePortByOwnership finds the interface carrying the ownership altname
913: +// of (ownerName, ifaceName) in src's namespace and parks it into the parking
914: +// netns of longName. The pair survives: only the parked half is relocated.
915: +func ParkBridgePortByOwnership(
916: +	ctx context.Context,
917: +	src Node,
918: +	ownerName string,
919: +	ifaceName string,
920: +	longName string,
921: +) (*BridgePortRelocation, error) {
922: +	parkPath, err := clabutils.CreateOrGetNamedNetNS(clabutils.ParkingNetnsName(longName))
923: +	if err != nil {
924: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create parking netns for migration: %w", err)
925: +	}
926: +
927: +	relocation := &BridgePortRelocation{
928: +		parkNSPath:   parkPath,
929: +		OldOwnerName: ownerName,
930: +		IfaceName:    ifaceName,
931: +		LongName:     longName,
932: +	}
933: +
934: +	parkErr := src.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
935: +		link, err := findLinkByOwnershipAltName(ownerName, ifaceName)
936: +		if err != nil {
937: +			return err
938: +		}
939: +
940: +		relocation.KernelName = link.Attrs().Name
941: +
942: +		if err := netlink.LinkSetDown(link); err != nil {
943: +			log.Debug("failed to bring down interface while parking",
944: +				"iface", link.Attrs().Name, "err", err)
945: +		}
946: +
947: +		parkNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(parkPath)
948: +		if nsErr != nil {
949: +			return nsErr
950: +		}
951: +		defer parkNs.Close()
952: +
953: +		return netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(parkNs.Fd()))
954: +	})
955: +	if parkErr != nil {
956: +		_ = clabutils.UnlinkNamedNetNS(parkPath)
957: +		return nil, parkErr
958: +	}
959: +
960: +	return relocation, nil
961: +}
962: +
963: +// RestoreBridgePort moves the parked half into the replacement bridge's
964: +// namespace, keeps/renames it to the desired kernel name, relabels the
965: +// ownership altname to (newOwnerName, ifaceName) and re-enslaves it to the
966: +// bridge. dst receives a node with both ExecFunction and GetNSPath.
967: +func (r *BridgePortRelocation) RestoreBridgePort(
968: +	ctx context.Context,
969: +	dst NSMigrationNode,
970: +	newOwnerName string,
971: +	bridgeName string,
972: +	desiredKernelName string,
973: +) error {
974: +	parkExecErr := r.execInParkingNS(func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
975: +		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.KernelName)
976: +		if err != nil {
977: +			return fmt.Errorf("parked interface %q not found in parking ns: %w", r.KernelName, err)
978: +		}
979: +
980: +		dstPath, nsErr := dst.GetNSPath(ctx)
981: +		if nsErr != nil {
982: +			return nsErr
983: +		}
984: +		dstNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(dstPath)
985: +		if nsErr != nil {
986: +			return nsErr
987: +		}
988: +		defer dstNs.Close()
989: +
990: +		return netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(dstNs.Fd()))
991: +	})
992: +	if parkExecErr != nil {
993: +		return parkExecErr
994: +	}
995: +
996: +	dstErr := dst.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
997: +		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.KernelName)
998: +		if err != nil {
999: +			return fmt.Errorf("restored interface %q not found in destination ns: %w",
1000: +				r.KernelName, err)
1001: +		}
1002: +
1003: +		if desiredKernelName != "" && link.Attrs().Name != desiredKernelName {
1004: +			if err := netlink.LinkSetName(link, desiredKernelName); err != nil {
1005: +				return err
1006: +			}
1007: +			link.Attrs().Name = desiredKernelName
1008: +		}
1009: +
1010: +		// Strip previous ownership markers and label with the new owner.
1011: +		for _, altName := range link.Attrs().AltNames {
1012: +			if !strings.HasPrefix(altName, ownershipAltNamePrefix) {
1013: +				continue
1014: +			}
1015: +			if delErr := netlink.LinkDelAltName(link, altName); delErr != nil &&
1016: +				!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(delErr) {
1017: +				return fmt.Errorf("failed to drop old ownership altname %q: %w", altName, delErr)
1018: +			}
1019: +		}
1020: +		if addErr := linkAddAltName(
1021: +			link,
1022: +			ownershipAltNameFor(newOwnerName, r.IfaceName),
1023: +		); addErr != nil &&
1024: +			!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(addErr) {
1025: +			return addErr
1026: +		}
1027: +
1028: +		// Re-enslave to the replacement bridge, if present.
1029: +		if bridgeName != "" {
1030: +			if bridgeLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName); err == nil {
1031: +				if link.Attrs().MasterIndex != bridgeLink.Attrs().Index {
1032: +					if err := netlink.LinkSetMaster(link, bridgeLink); err != nil {
1033: +						return fmt.Errorf("failed to enslave %q to %q: %w",
1034: +							link.Attrs().Name, bridgeName, err)
1035: +					}
1036: +					log.Info("Re-enslaved migrated bridge port to replacement bridge",
1037: +						"port", link.Attrs().Name, "bridge", bridgeName)
1038: +				}
1039: +			}
1040: +		}
1041: +
1042: +		if link.Attrs().OperState != netlink.OperUp {
1043: +			if upErr := netlink.LinkSetUp(link); upErr != nil {
1044: +				return fmt.Errorf("failed to bring up %q: %w", link.Attrs().Name, upErr)
1045: +			}
1046: +		}
1047: +
1048: +		return nil
1049: +	})
1050: +	if dstErr != nil {
1051: +		return dstErr
1052: +	}
1053: +
1054: +	// Clean up the now empty parking namespace.
1055: +	_ = clabutils.UnlinkNamedNetNS(r.parkNSPath)
1056: +
1057: +	return nil
1058: +}
1059: +
1060: +func (r *BridgePortRelocation) execInParkingNS(f func(ns.NetNS) error) error {
1061: +	parkNs, err := ns.GetNS(r.parkNSPath)
1062: +	if err != nil {
1063: +		return err
1064: +	}
1065: +	defer parkNs.Close()
1066: +
1067: +	return parkNs.Do(f)
1068: +}
1069: +
1070: +// RelabelOwnershipAltNameFor rewrites the ownership altname of the interface
1071: +// identified by (oldOwner, ifaceName) to (newOwner, ifaceName) inside node's
1072: +// namespace.
1073: +func RelabelOwnershipAltNameFor(
1074: +	ctx context.Context,
1075: +	node Node,
1076: +	oldOwnerName string,
1077: +	ifaceName string,
1078: +	newOwnerName string,
1079: +) error {
1080: +	if newOwnerName == oldOwnerName {
1081: +		return nil
1082: +	}
1083: +
1084: +	return node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
1085: +		link, err := findLinkByOwnershipAltName(oldOwnerName, ifaceName)
1086: +		if err != nil {
1087: +			// Fall back to the sanitized kernel name: short names kept their
1088: +			// kernel name during relocation.
1089: +			link, err = netlink.LinkByName(clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(ifaceName))
1090: +			if err != nil {
1091: +				return fmt.Errorf(
1092: +					"interface to relabel ownership for %q (old owner %q) not found: %w",
1093: +					ifaceName,
1094: +					oldOwnerName,
1095: +					err,
1096: +				)
1097: +			}
1098: +		}
1099: +
1100: +		// Drop all previous ownership markers; ownership is single-valued.
1101: +		for _, altName := range link.Attrs().AltNames {
1102: +			if !strings.HasPrefix(altName, ownershipAltNamePrefix) {
1103: +				continue
1104: +			}
1105: +			if delErr := netlink.LinkDelAltName(link, altName); delErr != nil &&
1106: +				!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(delErr) {
1107: +				return fmt.Errorf("failed to drop old ownership altname %q: %w", altName, delErr)
1108: +			}
1109: +		}
1110: +
1111: +		return linkAddAltName(link, ownershipAltNameFor(newOwnerName, ifaceName))
1112: +	})
1113: +}
1114: +
1115: +// findLinkByOwnershipAltName scans the current namespace for the link carrying
1116: +// the ownership altname of (nodeName, ifaceName).
1117: +func findLinkByOwnershipAltName(nodeName, ifaceName string) (netlink.Link, error) {
1118: +	links, err := netlink.LinkList()
1119: +	if err != nil {
1120: +		return nil, err
1121: +	}
1122: +	for _, link := range links {
1123: +		if HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, nodeName, ifaceName) {
1124: +			return link, nil
1125: +		}

1716: +#   .bridgeParent - which container hosts br01 (bp1 or bp2)
1717: +#   .parentEnv    - env value for the bridge-holding parent, used to trigger
1718: +#                   config drift and force a parent recreation

1720: +
1721: +name: bridge-ns-reconcile
1722: +
1723: +topology:

Potential issues I can spot already:

A. In `core/apply.go` diff, the original code had `if err := c.deleteApplyEndpoints(ctx, plan.staleEndpoints); err != nil` changed to `c.deleteApplyEndpoints(ctx, plan)`. Fine.

B. In `core/apply_bridge_migration.go` restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts: it iterates over `plan.bridgeNSMigrations` and for each migration filters `plan.addedLinks` — note the filtering loop is inside the per-migration loop, and it modifies `plan.addedLinks` in place with `kept := plan.addedLinks[:0]` reusing backing array. This is fine per-iteration. But note: the "mark full-deployed so deployLinks skips pair re-creation" claim — the comment says "The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed" but the code only filters addedLinks. Where is the link marked full-deployed? Need to check `deployLinks` and whether filtering out from addedLinks means the link state stays as-is. Actually filtering it out of addedLinks means deployLinks never touches it, so it's not "marked full-deployed". Let me check the actual code in the head file.

C. In `planBridgeNSMigrations`, scanning `plan.state.Topology.Links` for raw links with "|": it looks for ANY endpoint containing "|" — including client-side endpoints? Actually bridge endpoints are named `<bridge>|<parent>:<iface>`. Wait, no — in the topology, endpoint is "br01|bp1:c1eth1", so `SplitEndpointString` splits at the FIRST ":" giving node="br01|bp1", iface="c1eth1". So point[0] contains "|" identifies bridge endpoints. But what if a regular node name contains "|"? Unlikely. But the check doesn't verify that the link is a bridge kind; it just checks the name contains "|". If a node is named with "|" but isn't a bridge... probably fine since addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate checks isBridgeNSNode for the candidate. But the staleKey would be added as a candidate; if no candidate matches, nothing happens. OK.

However, there's a subtle issue: the deleted-bridge-node recovery iterates ALL links of the old topology, and for links whose bridge node was NOT deleted (still in desired topology under the same name), the endpoint is in desiredEndpointSet so it returns early. Fine.

268: func (c *CLab) checkApplyTopologyDefinition(ctx context.Context) error {
269: 	params := *clablinks.NewVerifyLinkParams()
270: 	if len(c.Endpoints) > 0 {
271: 		runtime := c.globalRuntime()
272: 		if runtime == nil {
273: 			return fmt.Errorf("container runtime is not initialized")
274: 		}
275: 		config := runtime.Config()
276: 		if config.VerifyLinkParams != nil {
277: 			params = *config.VerifyLinkParams
278: 		}
279: 	}
280: 	params.AllowExistingEndpoint = true
281: 	if err := c.verifyLinks(ctx, &params); err != nil {
282: 		return err
283: 	}
284: 
285: 	if err := c.verifyRootNetNSLinks(); err != nil {
286: 		return err
287: 	}
288: 
289: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
290: 		if err := c.Nodes[nodeName].CheckDeploymentConditions(ctx); err != nil {
291: 			return err
292: 		}
293: 	}
294: 
295: 	if err := c.verifyDuplicateAddresses(); err != nil {
296: 		return err
297: 	}
298: 
299: 	return c.verifyTailscaleProxy()
300: }

302: func (c *CLab) prepareApply(
303: 	ctx context.Context,
304: 	addedNodes []string,
305: 	skipLabDirFileACLs bool,
306: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
307: ) error {
308: 	existing := c.collectExistingManagementAddresses(currentNodes)
309: 	if err := c.prepareLabManagementNetwork(ctx, existing...); err != nil {
310: 		return err
311: 	}
312:

314: 		return err
315: 	}
316: 
317: 	for _, nodeName := range addedNodes {
318: 		if err := c.Nodes[nodeName].PullImage(ctx); err != nil {
319: 			return err
320: 		}
321: 	}
322: 
323: 	return nil
324: }

326: func (c *CLab) removeApplyLinkEndpoints(ctx context.Context, links []clablinks.Link) error {
327: 	for _, link := range links {
328: 		for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
329: 			node := ep.GetNode()
330: 
331: 			// For BridgeNS bridge endpoints, use RemoveInterface instead of
332: 			// RemoveOwnedInterface: bridge-attached interfaces are owned by the remote
333: 			// endpoint, so per-node ownership checks would always fail.
334: 			if node.GetLinkEndpointType() == clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS {
335: 				parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSParentNode(node.GetShortName())
336: 				if err != nil {
337: 					return err
338: 				}
339: 				if err := clablinks.RemoveInterface(
340: 					ctx,
341: 					parentNode,
342: 					ep.GetIfaceName(),
343: 				); err != nil {
344: 					return err
345: 				}
346: 				continue
347: 			}
348: 
349: 			if err := clablinks.RemoveOwnedInterface(
350: 				ctx,
351: 				node,
352: 				ep.GetIfaceName(),
353: 			); err != nil {
354: 				return err
355: 			}
356: 		}
357: 	}
358: 
359: 	return nil
360: }

362: // try to preserve the existing addressing instead of reallocation.
363: func (c *CLab) collectExistingManagementAddresses(
364: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
365: ) []clabtypes.ExistingAddress {
366: 	var existing []clabtypes.ExistingAddress
367: 	for name, group := range currentNodes {
368: 		for _, ctr := range group.containers {
369: 			if c.mgmtNetByNetwork(ctr.NetworkName).Network != ctr.NetworkName {
370: 				continue
371: 			}
372: 			for _, value := range []string{ctr.NetworkSettings.IPv4addr, ctr.NetworkSettings.IPv6addr} {
373: 				if ip, err := netip.ParseAddr(value); err == nil {
374: 					existing = append(
375: 						existing,
376: 						clabtypes.ExistingAddress{NodeName: name, ContainerID: ctr.ID, Address: ip},
377: 					)
378: 				}
379: 			}
380: 		}
381: 	}
382: 	return existing
383: }

1: package core

13: // bridgeNSMigParentNode resolves the namespace host of a migrated bridge-side
14: // endpoint. Stale refs carry either a live bridge node (resolved via the
15: // topology) or the name-encoded <bridge>|<parent> form of a node that is
16: // already removed from the desired topology.
17: func (c *CLab) bridgeNSMigParentNode(ref applyEndpointRef) (clablinks.Node, error) {
18: 	if parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSParentNode(ref.key.node); err == nil {
19: 		return parentNode, nil
20: 	}
21: 	parts := strings.SplitN(ref.key.node, "|", 2)
22: 	if len(parts) != 2 {
23: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot resolve namespace host of bridge %q", ref.key.node)
24: 	}
25: 	node, exists := c.Nodes[parts[1]]
26: 	if !exists {
27: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
28: 			"bridge %q: parent container %q not found",
29: 			ref.key.node,
30: 			parts[1],
31: 		)
32: 	}
33: 	return node, nil
34: }
35: 
36: // parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts parks bridge-side veth ends whose owning in-container
37: // bridge was replaced by a bridge under a different parent (the move case).
38: // The veth pair stays intact: only the parked half leaves the dying parent's
39: // namespace, so the client-side end keeps its state untouched.
40: func (c *CLab) parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts(
41: 	ctx context.Context,
42: 	plan *applyPlan,
43: ) error {
44: 	if plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {
45: 		return nil
46: 	}
47: 
48: 	for i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
49: 		mig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]
50: 
51: 		if mig.relocation != nil {
52: 			continue
53: 		}
54: 
55: 		// The old bridge node may already be deleted from the desired topology
56: 		// (the move case); resolve its namespace host by the name-encoded
57: 		// parent suffix, falling back to the normal resolution.
58: 		parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSMigParentNode(mig.staleRef)
59: 		if err != nil {
60: 			return err
61: 		}
62: 
63: 		newNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]
64: 		if !exists {
65: 			return fmt.Errorf("bridge migration target %q not found", mig.newKey.node)
66: 		}
67: 		longName := newNode.Config().LongName
68: 
69: 		relocation, err := clablinks.ParkBridgePortByOwnership(
70: 			ctx,
71: 			parentNode,
72: 			mig.staleRef.key.node,
73: 			mig.staleRef.key.iface,
74: 			longName,
75: 		)
76: 		if err != nil {
77: 			return err
78: 		}
79: 
80: 		mig.relocation = relocation
81: 	}
82: 
83: 	return nil
84: }
85: 
86: // restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts moves parked bridge-side ends into the replacement
87: // bridge's parent namespace after that container (and the bridge) exist again,
88: // relabels the ownership altname to the replacement bridge node, and re-enslaves
89: // the port to the bridge. The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed so
90: // deployLinks skips pair re-creation for it.
91: func (c *CLab) restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts(
92: 	ctx context.Context,
93: 	plan *applyPlan,
94: ) error {
95: 	if plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {
96: 		return nil
97: 	}
98: 
99: 	for i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
100: 		mig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]
101: 
102: 		if mig.relocation == nil || plan.plannedLinkSet == nil {
103: 			continue
104: 		}
105: 
106: 		// Restore into the replacement bridge's parent namespace; the bridge
107: 		// node interfaces with the parent's ns through its GetNSPath override.
108: 		bridgeNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]
109: 		if !exists {
110: 			return fmt.Errorf("bridge migration target %q not found", mig.newKey.node)
111: 		}
112: 
113: 		if err := mig.relocation.RestoreBridgePort(
114: 			ctx,
115: 			bridgeNode,
116: 			mig.newKey.node,
117: 			bridgeNSNameInNamespace(mig.newKey.node),
118: 			clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(mig.newKey.iface),
119: 		); err != nil {
120: 			return err
121: 		}
122: 
123: 		// The migrated pair is complete end-to-end (the client-side end was
124: 		// never touched and the parked bridge-side half is restored and
125: 		// enslaved). Filter the corresponding replaced link out of addedLinks
126: 		// so endpoint removal and pair re-creation never touch it.
127: 		kept := plan.addedLinks[:0]
128: 		for _, link := range plan.addedLinks {
129: 			if clablinks.RuntimeEndpointsContainEndpoint(
130: 				link,
131: 				mig.newKey.node,
132: 				mig.newKey.iface,
133: 			) {
134: 				log.Info(
135: 					"Restored migrated bridge port into replacement bridge",
136: 					"bridge",
137: 					mig.newKey.node,
138: 					"port",
139: 					mig.newKey.iface,
140: 				)
141: 				continue
142: 			}
143: 			kept = append(kept, link)
144: 		}
145: 		plan.addedLinks = kept
146: 	}
147: 
148: 	return nil
149: }

Also the restore happens BEFORE removeApplyLinkEndpoints which removes endpoints of remaining addedLinks — filtering avoids deleting the migrated endpoints (good, since the migrated endpoint was filtered out).

174: // planNetworkModeCascade forces recreation of nodes whose network-mode:

197: 		for _, nodeName := range dependents[target] {
198: 			if _, recreated := plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName]; recreated {
199: 				continue
200: 			}
201: 			if _, added := plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; added {
202: 				continue
203: 			}
204: 
205: 			plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
206: 			delete(plan.restartNodeSet, nodeName)
207: 			delete(plan.linkRestartNodeSet, nodeName)
208: 			plan.nodeChangeReasons[nodeName] = fmt.Sprintf(
209: 				"network-mode target %q recreated", target,
210: 			)
211: 			queue = append(queue, nodeName)
212: 		}
213: 	}
214: }

216: func (c *CLab) planApply(
217: 	ctx context.Context,
218: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
219: ) (*applyPlan, error) {
220: 	state, err := c.LoadState()
221: 	if err != nil {
222: 		log.Warn("Failed to load state file", "error", err)
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	plan := newApplyPlan(currentNodes, state)
226: 
227: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
228: 		if _, exists := currentNodes[nodeName]; !exists {
229: 			status := c.Nodes[nodeName].GetContainerStatus(ctx)
230: 			if status != clabruntime.NotFound {
231: 				return nil, fmt.Errorf(
232: 					"node %q container %q already exists outside the runtime lab state",
233: 					nodeName,
234: 					c.Nodes[nodeName].Config().LongName,
235: 				)
236: 			}
237: 
238: 			plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
239: 			continue
240: 		}
241: 
242: 		if plan.isNewNonContainerNode(nodeName) {
243: 			plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
244: 		}
245: 	}
246: 
247: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedRuntimeNodeGroupNames(currentNodes) {
248: 		if _, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]; !exists {
249: 			plan.deletedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
250: 		}
251: 	}
252: 
253: 	if err := c.checkApplyNetworkModeTargets(plan); err != nil {
254: 		return nil, err
255: 	}
256: 
257: 	if err := c.planNodeReconciliation(ctx, plan); err != nil {
258: 		return nil, err
259: 	}
260: 
261: 	c.planParkedNodes(ctx, plan)
262: 	c.planStoppedNodes(ctx, plan)
263: 
264: 	for _, linkIdx := range sortedLinkIndexes(c.Links) {
265: 		for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(c.Links[linkIdx]) {
266: 			plan.desiredEndpointSet[endpointKeyFromEndpoint(ep)] = struct{}{}
267: 		}
268: 	}
269: 
270: 	if err := c.discoverLiveApplyEndpoints(ctx, plan); err != nil {
271: 		return nil, err
272: 	}
273: 
274: 	if err := c.validateDesiredEndpointOwnership(ctx, plan); err != nil {
275: 		return nil, err
276: 	}
277: 
278: 	c.planDeletedEndpoints(ctx, plan)
279: 
280: 	for _, linkIdx := range sortedLinkIndexes(c.Links) {
281: 		link := c.Links[linkIdx]
282: 		if !plan.linkNeedsDeploy(link) {
283: 			continue
284: 		}
285: 
286: 		plan.addDeployApplyLink(linkIdx, link)
287: 
288: 		for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
289: 			nodeName := ep.GetNode().GetShortName()
290: 			if _, exists := currentNodes[nodeName]; !exists {
291: 				continue
292: 			}
293: 			if _, added := plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; added {
294: 				continue
295: 			}
296: 
297: 			c.planAffectedApplyNode(ctx, plan, nodeName, "added link")
298: 		}
299: 	}
300: 
301: 	// Link reconciliation can request additional recreations. Propagate namespace
302: 	// dependencies only after those decisions, then park every affected live node.
303: 	c.planNetworkModeCascade(plan)
304: 	c.planTailscaleSidecarRecreates(plan)
305: 	c.planParkedNodes(ctx, plan)
306: 	c.planRecreatedNodeLinks(plan)
307: 	for nodeName := range plan.recreatedNodeSet {
308: 		delete(plan.restartNodeSet, nodeName)
309: 		delete(plan.linkRestartNodeSet, nodeName)
310: 		delete(plan.startNodeSet, nodeName)
311: 	}
312: 	if err := c.planNetworkModeRestarts(plan); err != nil {
313: 		return nil, err
314: 	}
315: 
316: 	return plan, nil
317: }

319: func (p *applyPlan) addDeployApplyLink(linkIdx int, link clablinks.Link) {
320: 	if _, planned := p.plannedLinkSet[linkIdx]; planned {
321: 		return
322: 	}
323: 
324: 	p.plannedLinkSet[linkIdx] = struct{}{}
325: 	p.addedLinks = append(p.addedLinks, link)
326: }

328: func (c *CLab) planParkedNodes(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) {
329: 	if plan == nil {
330: 		return
331: 	}
332: 
333: 	for nodeName := range plan.recreatedNodeSet {
334: 		if _, parked := plan.parkedNodeSet[nodeName]; parked {
335: 			continue
336: 		}
337: 		node, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]
338: 		if !exists {
339: 			continue
340: 		}
341: 		if clabruntime.ContainerHasJoinableNetns(node.GetContainerStatus(ctx)) {
342: 			plan.parkedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
343: 		}
344: 	}
345: }

347: func (c *CLab) planStoppedNodes(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) {
348: 	if plan == nil {
349: 		return
350: 	}
351: 
352: 	for nodeName := range plan.currentNodes {
353: 		if plan.isNonContainerNode(nodeName) {
354: 			continue
355: 		}
356: 		node, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]
357: 		if !exists {
358: 			continue
359: 		}
360: 		if _, deleted := plan.deletedNodeSet[nodeName]; deleted {
361: 			continue
362: 		}
363: 		if _, added := plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; added {
364: 			continue
365: 		}
366: 		if _, recreated := plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName]; recreated {
367: 			continue
368: 		}
369: 
370: 		switch node.GetContainerStatus(ctx) {
371: 		case clabruntime.Stopped, clabruntime.Created:
372: 			plan.startNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
373: 		}
374: 	}
375: }

377: func (c *CLab) planRecreatedNodeLinks(plan *applyPlan) {
378: 	if plan == nil || len(plan.recreatedNodeSet) == 0 {
379: 		return
380: 	}
381: 
382: 	rebuildSet := make(map[string]struct{}, len(plan.recreatedNodeSet))
383: 	for nodeName := range plan.recreatedNodeSet {
384: 		if _, parked := plan.parkedNodeSet[nodeName]; parked {
385: 			continue
386: 		}
387: 		rebuildSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
388: 	}
389: 
390: 	for _, linkIdx := range sortedLinkIndexes(c.Links) {
391: 		link := c.Links[linkIdx]
392: 		if !linkTouchesNodeSet(link, rebuildSet) {
393: 			continue
394: 		}
395: 
396: 		plan.addDeployApplyLink(linkIdx, link)
397: 	}
398: }

400: func linkTouchesNodeSet(link clablinks.Link, nodeSet map[string]struct{}) bool {
401: 	if len(nodeSet) == 0 {
402: 		return false
403: 	}
404: 
405: 	for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
406: 		key := endpointKeyFromEndpoint(ep)
407: 		if _, exists := nodeSet[key.node]; exists {
408: 			return true
409: 		}
410: 	}
411: 
412: 	return false
413: }

415: func (c *CLab) planDeletedEndpoints(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) {
416: 	plannedEndpointSet := map[applyEndpointKey]struct{}{}
417: 
418: 	for _, key := range sortedEndpointKeys(plan.liveEndpointSet) {
419: 		if _, exists := plan.desiredEndpointSet[key]; exists {
420: 			continue
421: 		}
422: 		c.addStaleApplyEndpoint(ctx, plan, plannedEndpointSet, key)
423: 	}
424: 
425: 	c.planBridgeNSMigrations(ctx, plan)
426: }
427: 
428: // planBridgeNSMigrations finds stale BridgeNS bridge-side endpoints that the
429: // desired topology re-claims under a different in-container bridge node (the
430: // bridge moved to another parent). Such veth ends are migrated (parked and
431: // restored into the new parent's namespace) instead of deleted, which keeps
432: // the pairwise integrity of the link and the client-side configuration.
433: //
434: // Detection runs on two sources: live-discovered stale endpoints (existing
435: // bridge nodes) and the stored old topology (deleted bridge nodes, whose
436: // ports are not discovered live).
437: func (c *CLab) planBridgeNSMigrations(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) {
438: 	if plan == nil {
439: 		return
440: 	}
441: 
442: 	// Live-discovered stale bridge-side ends (the bridge node still exists).
443: 	for _, ref := range plan.staleEndpoints {
444: 		if ref.node == nil ||
445: 			ref.node.GetLinkEndpointType() != clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS {
446: 			continue
447: 		}
448: 		c.addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate(plan, ref.key, ref.node)
449: 	}
450: 
451: 	// Deleted in-container bridge nodes are absent from the desired topology,
452: 	// so their ports are not discovered live; recover them from the old state.
453: 	if plan.state != nil && plan.state.Topology != nil {
454: 		for _, link := range plan.state.Topology.Links {
455: 			if link == nil || link.Link == nil {
456: 				continue
457: 			}
458: 
459: 			var bridgeEndpointPoint *[2]string
460: 			for _, point := range clablinks.RawLinkEndpoints(link.Link) {
461: 				if strings.Contains(point[0], "|") {
462: 					bridgePoint := point
463: 					bridgeEndpointPoint = &bridgePoint
464: 				}
465: 			}
466: 			if bridgeEndpointPoint == nil {
467: 				continue
468: 			}
469: 
470: 			c.addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate(
471: 				plan,
472: 				applyEndpointKey{node: bridgeEndpointPoint[0], iface: bridgeEndpointPoint[1]},
473: 				nil,
474: 			)
475: 		}
476: 	}
477: }
478: 
479: // addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate registers a bridge NS migration when the
480: // desired topology re-claims the given bridge-side endpoint under a different
481: // in-container bridge node with the same logical port name.
482: func (c *CLab) addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate(
483: 	plan *applyPlan,
484: 	staleKey applyEndpointKey,
485: 	staleNode clablinks.Node,
486: ) {
487: 	if staleKey.node == "" || staleKey.iface == "" {
488: 		return
489: 	}
490: 	if _, desired := plan.desiredEndpointSet[staleKey]; desired {
491: 		return
492: 	}
493: 	if c.isBridgeNSMigrationPlanned(plan, staleKey) {
494: 		return
495: 	}
496: 
497: 	for candidate := range plan.desiredEndpointSet {
498: 		if candidate.iface != staleKey.iface || candidate.node == staleKey.node {
499: 			continue
500: 		}
501: 		if !c.isBridgeNSNode(candidate.node) {
502: 			continue
503: 		}
504: 
505: 		plan.bridgeNSMigrations = append(plan.bridgeNSMigrations, bridgeNSMigration{
506: 			staleRef: applyEndpointRef{key: staleKey, node: staleNode},
507: 			newKey:   candidate,
508: 		})
509: 		log.Info(
510: 			"Planning bridge port migration",
511: 			"from",
512: 			staleKey.String(),
513: 			"to",
514: 			candidate.String(),
515: 		)
516: 		return
517: 	}
518: }
519: 
520: // isBridgeNSMigrationPlanned reports whether the given bridge endpoint is
521: // already covered by a planned migration.
522: func (c *CLab) isBridgeNSMigrationPlanned(
523: 	plan *applyPlan,
524: 	key applyEndpointKey,
525: ) bool {
526: 	for _, mig := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
527: 		if mig.staleRef.key == key {
528: 			return true
529: 		}
530: 	}
531: 	return false
532: }

534: // isBridgeNSNode reports whether the node name refers to an in-container
535: // bridge node of the desired topology.
536: func (c *CLab) isBridgeNSNode(nodeName string) bool {
537: 	node, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]
538: 	if !exists {
539: 		return false
540: 	}
541: 	return node.GetLinkEndpointType() == clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS ||
542: 		node.Config().Kind == "bridge" && strings.Contains(nodeName, "|")
543: }

545: func (c *CLab) addStaleApplyEndpoint(
546: 	ctx context.Context,
547: 	plan *applyPlan,
548: 	plannedEndpointSet map[applyEndpointKey]struct{},
549: 	key applyEndpointKey,
550: ) {
551: 	if key.node == "" || key.iface == "" {
552: 		return
553: 	}
554: 	if _, exists := plannedEndpointSet[key]; exists {
555: 		return
556: 	}
557: 	if _, desired := plan.desiredEndpointSet[key]; desired {
558: 		return
559: 	}
560: 
561: 	node, exists := plan.endpointNode(key.node)
562: 	if !exists {
563: 		node, exists = c.applyLinkNode(key.node)
564: 	}
565: 	if !exists {
566: 		return
567: 	}
568: 
569: 	plannedEndpointSet[key] = struct{}{}
570: 	plan.staleEndpoints = append(plan.staleEndpoints, applyEndpointRef{key: key, node: node})
571: 
572: 	if _, exists := c.Nodes[key.node]; exists {
573: 		if _, added := plan.addedNodeSet[key.node]; !added {
574: 			c.planAffectedApplyNode(ctx, plan, key.node, "deleted endpoint")
575: 		}
576: 	}
577: 
578: 	c.addDerivedHostStaleEndpoints(plan, plannedEndpointSet, key)
579: }

581: func (c *CLab) addDerivedHostStaleEndpoints(
582: 	plan *applyPlan,
583: 	plannedEndpointSet map[applyEndpointKey]struct{},
584: 	key applyEndpointKey,
585: ) {
586: 	if key.node == "host" {
587: 		return
588: 	}
589: 	if _, exists := c.Nodes[key.node]; !exists {
590: 		return
591: 	}
592: 
593: 	hostNode, exists := c.applyLinkNode("host")
594: 	if !exists {
595: 		return
596: 	}
597: 
598: 	for _, iface := range []string{
599: 		fmt.Sprintf("ve-%s_%s", key.node, key.iface),
600: 		fmt.Sprintf("vx-%s_%s", key.node, key.iface),
601: 	} {
602: 		hostKey := applyEndpointKey{node: "host", iface: iface}
603: 		if _, planned := plannedEndpointSet[hostKey]; planned {
604: 			continue
605: 		}
606: 		if _, desired := plan.desiredEndpointSet[hostKey]; desired {
607: 			continue
608: 		}
609: 
610: 		plannedEndpointSet[hostKey] = struct{}{}
611: 		plan.staleEndpoints = append(
612: 			plan.staleEndpoints,
613: 			applyEndpointRef{key: hostKey, node: hostNode, bestEffort: true},
614: 		)
615: 	}
616: }

710: // bridgeNSParentNode resolves the parent container node whose network namespace
711: // hosts the given BridgeNS bridge node. Shared by discovery, validation and
712: // deletion paths touching BridgeNS endpoint lifecycles.
713: func (c *CLab) bridgeNSParentNode(bridgeName string) (clablinks.Node, error) {
714: 	node, exists := c.Nodes[bridgeName]
715: 	if !exists {
716: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("in-container bridge %q not found in topology", bridgeName)
717: 	}
718: 	parentName := networkModeContainerTarget(node.Config().NetworkMode)
719: 	if parentName == "" {
720: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
721: 			"in-container bridge %q has invalid network-mode: %s",
722: 			bridgeName,
723: 			node.Config().NetworkMode,
724: 		)
725: 	}
726: 	parentNode, exists := c.Nodes[parentName]
727: 	if !exists {
728: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
729: 			"in-container bridge %q: parent container %q not found",
730: 			bridgeName,
731: 			parentName,
732: 		)
733: 	}
734: 	return parentNode, nil
735: }

737: // bridgeNSNameInNamespace strips the "<bridge>|<node>" suffix, yielding the
738: // kernel bridge interface name inside the parent container namespace.
739: func bridgeNSNameInNamespace(bridgeName string) string {
740: 	if idx := strings.Index(bridgeName, "|"); idx != -1 {
741: 		return bridgeName[:idx]

743: 	return bridgeName

750: // bridge-attached interfaces (owned but claimed by no desired endpoint) are

756: 	nsNode clablinks.Node,

758: 	desiredNames := make(map[string]struct{})

761: 			desiredNames[key.iface] = struct{}{}
762: 		}
763: 	}

765: 	matched, orphans, err := clablinks.DiscoverEndpointsForBridgeNS(

774: 	}
775: 
776: 	for name, iface := range matched {

778: 		plan.liveEndpointSet[key] = struct{}{}
779: 		plan.liveEndpointInfo[key] = iface
780: 	}
781: 
782: 	for _, iface := range orphans {
783: 		key := applyEndpointKey{node: bridgeName, iface: iface.Name}
784: 		plan.liveEndpointSet[key] = struct{}{}
785: 		plan.liveEndpointInfo[key] = iface
786: 	}

789: }

1032: func (c *CLab) planNodeReconciliation(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) error {
1033: 	if plan == nil || plan.currentNodes == nil {
1034: 		return nil
1035: 	}
1036: 
1037: 	var oldTopo *clabtypes.Topology
1038: 	if plan.state != nil {
1039: 		oldTopo = plan.state.Topology
1040: 	}
1041: 
1042: 	for nodeName := range plan.currentNodes {
1043: 		node, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]
1044: 		if !exists {
1045: 			continue
1046: 		}
1047: 		if _, added := plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; added {
1048: 			continue
1049: 		}
1050: 
1051: 		oldNodeConfig := c.resolveNodeConfigFromTopology(oldTopo, nodeName)
1052: 		newNodeConfig := c.resolveNodeConfigFromTopology(c.Config.Topology, nodeName)
1053: 		diff := node.ComputeDiff(oldNodeConfig, newNodeConfig)
1054: 		plan.nodeDiffs[nodeName] = diff
1055: 
1056: 		result, err := node.GetReconcilePlan(ctx, diff)
1057: 		if err != nil {
1058: 			return fmt.Errorf("reconcile planning failed for node %q: %w", nodeName, err)
1059: 		}
1060: 		if plan.isNonContainerNode(nodeName) && result.Action != clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionNone {
1061: 			return fmt.Errorf(
1062: 				"node %q is externally managed and cannot be %s for %s",
1063: 				nodeName,
1064: 				result.Action,
1065: 				configDriftReason(diff),
1066: 			)
1067: 		}
1068: 
1069: 		switch result.Action {
1070: 		case clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionRestart:
1071: 			plan.restartNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
1072: 			plan.nodeChangeReasons[nodeName] = configDriftReason(diff)
1073: 		case clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionRecreate:
1074: 			plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
1075: 			plan.nodeChangeReasons[nodeName] = configDriftReason(diff)
1076: 		}
1077: 	}
1078: 
1079: 	return nil
1080: }

1140: 			}
1141: 		}

1150: func (p *applyPlan) linkIntact(link clablinks.Link) bool {
1151: 	endpoints := clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link)
1152: 	if len(endpoints) != 2 || len(p.liveEndpointInfo) == 0 {
1153: 		return true
1154: 	}
1155: 
1156: 	left, leftOK := p.liveEndpointInfo[endpointKeyFromEndpoint(endpoints[0])]
1157: 	right, rightOK := p.liveEndpointInfo[endpointKeyFromEndpoint(endpoints[1])]
1158: 	if !leftOK || !rightOK {
1159: 		return false
1160: 	}
1161: 
1162: 	if bridgeMasterMismatch(endpoints[0], left) || bridgeMasterMismatch(endpoints[1], right) {
1163: 		return false
1164: 	}
1165: 
1166: 	return left.PeerIndex != 0 &&
1167: 		right.PeerIndex != 0 &&
1168: 		left.PeerIndex == right.Index &&
1169: 		right.PeerIndex == left.Index
1170: }

1172: // bridgeMasterMismatch reports whether the live interface of a bridge endpoint is
1173: // attached to a bridge other than the one the endpoint resolves to, e.g. after a
1174: // mgmt-net link moved to another management network. mgmt-net endpoints whose
1175: // management network bridge is not resolved are not checked.
1176: func bridgeMasterMismatch(ep clablinks.Endpoint, live clablinks.OwnedInterface) bool {
1177: 	node := ep.GetNode()
1178: 	endpointType := node.GetLinkEndpointType()
1179: 
1180: 	// Handle regular bridge endpoints
1181: 	if endpointType == clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridge {
1182: 		if clablinks.IsUnresolvedMgmtBridgeEndpoint(ep) {
1183: 			return false
1184: 		}
1185: 		return live.MasterName != node.GetShortName()
1186: 	}
1187: 
1188: 	// Handle in-container bridge (BridgeNS) endpoints
1189: 	if endpointType == clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS {
1190: 		// For BridgeNS, the bridge name in the container is the node name without the namespace
1191: 		// suffix
1192: 		bridgeName := node.GetShortName()
1193: 		if idx := strings.Index(bridgeName, "|"); idx != -1 {
1194: 			bridgeName = bridgeName[:idx]
1195: 		}
1196: 		return live.MasterName != bridgeName
1197: 	}
1198: 
1199: 	return false
1200: }

1222: func (c *CLab) deleteApplyEndpoints(
1223: 	ctx context.Context,
1224: 	plan *applyPlan,

1226: 	refs := plan.staleEndpoints

1229: 
1230: 		// For BridgeNS bridges, use RemoveInterface instead of RemoveOwnedInterface.
1231: 		// BridgeNS interfaces are owned by the remote endpoint (the container
1232: 		// connecting to the bridge), not by the bridge itself, so per-node

1250: 				return err
1251: 			}
1252: 			continue

1254: 
1255: 		if err := clablinks.RemoveOwnedInterface(ctx, ref.node, ref.key.iface); err != nil {

1257: 				log.Debugf("skipping best-effort endpoint delete: %v", err)
1258: 				continue
1259: 			}

1261: 		}

55: func (s *bridge) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
56: 	// Init DefaultNode
57: 	s.DefaultNode = *clabnodes.NewDefaultNode(s)
58: 
59: 	s.Cfg = cfg
60: 	for _, o := range opts {
61: 		o(s)
62: 	}
63: 	if s.Cfg.NetworkMode == "" || s.Cfg.NetworkMode == "host" {
64: 		s.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased = true
65: 	} else {
66: 		var err error
67: 		s.containerNs, err = clabutils.ContainerNameFromNetworkMode(s.Config().NetworkMode)
68: 		if err != nil {
69: 			return err
70: 		}
71: 	}
72: 	return nil
73: }
74: 
75: // SetNodesMap implements clabnodes.NamespaceSharerNodesSetter so core can wire
76: // the topology's nodes into the bridge after construction. The bridge keeps
77: // only the parent node hosting its namespace; the rest of the map is not
78: // stored. This makes the parent container resolvable for link deployment and
79: // namespace work even when the bridge node itself is never Deploy()ed (the
80: // reconcile/apply path).
81: func (n *bridge) SetNodesMap(nodes map[string]clabnodes.Node) {
82: 	if n.containerNs == "" {
83: 		return
84: 	}
85: 	if n.parentNode == nil {
86: 		n.parentNode = nodes[n.containerNs]
87: 	}
88: }
89: 
90: // resolveParentNode returns the wired parent node or an error explaining the
91: // missing wiring.
92: func (n *bridge) resolveParentNode() (clabnodes.Node, error) {
93: 	if n.parentNode == nil {
94: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
95: 			"bridge %q: parent container %q not available (nodes not wired)",
96: 			n.GetShortName(),
97: 			n.containerNs,
98: 		)
99: 	}
100: 	return n.parentNode, nil
101: }
102: 
103: // nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix returns the bridge name without the separator suffix
104: // used to distinguish bridges attached to different namespaces in the topology.
105: // For example, if the bridge name is "br0|ns1", it will return "br0".
106: func (n *bridge) nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix() string {
107: 	s := n.GetShortName()
108: 	if idx := strings.Index(s, bridgeNodeSep); idx != -1 {
109: 		return s[:idx]
110: 	}
111: 	return s
112: }
113: 
114: func (n *bridge) Deploy(ctx context.Context, dp *clabnodes.DeployParams) error {
115: 	// Deploy's map is authoritative for wiring the parent node.
116: 	if n.Config().NetworkMode != "" {
117: 		cntName, err := clabutils.ContainerNameFromNetworkMode(n.Config().NetworkMode)
118: 		if err != nil {
119: 			return err
120: 		}
121: 		n.parentNode = dp.Nodes[cntName]
122: 
123: 		if n.parentNode == nil {
124: 			return fmt.Errorf(
125: 				"bridge %q: parent container %q not found in topology",
126: 				n.GetShortName(),
127: 				cntName,
128: 			)
129: 		}
130: 
131: 		// For BridgeNS, wait for parent container to be running before creating bridge
132: 		if err := n.waitForParentContainer(ctx, n.parentNode); err != nil {
133: 			return err
134: 		}
135: 		err = n.parentNode.ExecFunction(ctx, func(nn ns.NetNS) error {
136: 			bridgeName := n.nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix()
137: 			// check if bridge already exists
138: 			existingLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName)
139: 			if err == nil {
140: 				// Bridge already exists, just ensure it's up
141: 				return netlink.LinkSetUp(existingLink)
142: 			}
143: 			// Bridge doesn't exist, create it
144: 			err = netlink.LinkAdd(&netlink.Bridge{
145: 				LinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{
146: 					Name: bridgeName,
147: 				},
148: 			})
149: 			if err != nil {
150: 				return err
151: 			}
152: 			// retrieve link ref
153: 			netlinkLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName)
154: 			if err != nil {
155: 				return err
156: 			}
157: 			// bring the link up
158: 			err = netlink.LinkSetUp(netlinkLink)
159: 			if err != nil {
160: 				return err
161: 			}
162: 			return nil
163: 		})
164: 		if err != nil {
165: 			return err
166: 		}
167: 	}
168: 	n.SetState(clabnodesstate.Deployed)
169: 	return nil
170: }
171: 
172: // waitForParentContainer waits for the parent container to have a joinable network namespace.
173: // This is necessary for BridgeNS bridges which execute operations in the parent container's
174: // namespace.
175: func (n *bridge) waitForParentContainer(ctx context.Context, parentNode clabnodes.Node) error {
176: 	// Poll until parent container has a joinable network namespace or context is cancelled
177: 	ticker := time.NewTicker(100 * time.Millisecond)
178: 	defer ticker.Stop()
179: 
180: 	for {
181: 		select {
182: 		case <-ctx.Done():
183: 			return ctx.Err()
184: 		case <-ticker.C:
185: 			status := parentNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx)
186: 			if clabruntime.ContainerHasJoinableNetns(status) {
187: 				return nil
188: 			}
189: 			if status == clabruntime.NotFound {
190: 				// Parent container doesn't exist yet, keep waiting
191: 				continue
192: 			}
193: 			if status == clabruntime.Stopped {
194: 				return fmt.Errorf(
195: 					"parent container %q has stopped (status=%s)",
196: 					n.containerNs,
197: 					status,
198: 				)
199: 			}
200: 		}
201: 	}
202: }
203: 
204: // ExecFunction executes the given function in the bridge's network namespace.
205: // For BridgeNS bridges (in-container bridges), this executes in the parent container's namespace.
206: // For host bridges, this executes in the host's root namespace.
207: func (b *bridge) ExecFunction(ctx context.Context, f func(ns.NetNS) error) error {
208: 	// For BridgeNS bridges, we need to execute in the parent container's namespace
209: 	if b.containerNs != "" {
210: 		parentNode, err := b.resolveParentNode()
211: 		if err != nil {
212: 			// Without the wired parent there is no namespace to execute in.
213: 			return err
214: 		}
215: 		return parentNode.ExecFunction(ctx, f)
216: 	}
217: 	// For host bridges, execute in the current (host) namespace
218: 	curNs, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
219: 	if err != nil {
220: 		return err
221: 	}
222: 	return curNs.Do(f)
223: }

228: 	return nil
229: }

236: func (b *bridge) PostDeploy(_ context.Context, _ *clabnodes.PostDeployParams) error {
237: 	if b.containerNs != "" {
238: 		return b.enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace()
239: 	}
240: 	return b.installIPTablesBridgeFwdRule()

243: // GetContainerStatus reports the parent container's status for in-container
244: // bridges so lifecycle scheduling (parking, restart ordering) treats the
245: // bridge as alive whenever its namespace host exists.
246: func (b *bridge) GetContainerStatus(ctx context.Context) clabruntime.ContainerStatus {
247: 	if b.containerNs == "" {
248: 		return b.DefaultNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx)
249: 	}
250: 	if parentNode := b.ParentNode(ctx); parentNode != nil {
251: 		return parentNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx)
252: 	}
253: 	return clabruntime.NotFound
254: }

256: // ParentNode resolves the node that hosts this bridge's network namespace.
257: func (b *bridge) ParentNode(_ context.Context) clabnodes.Node {
258: 	if b.containerNs == "" {
259: 		return nil
260: 	}
261: 	return b.parentNode
262: }

264: // ParkEndpoints and RestoreEndpoints are no-ops for in-container bridges: the
265: // bridge-side veth ends live in the parent container's namespace and are
266: // therefore carried through parent recreation by the parent's own park/restore
267: // machinery. Parking them separately would move the same interfaces twice.
268: func (*bridge) ParkEndpoints(_ context.Context) error { return nil }
269: 
270: func (*bridge) RestoreEndpoints(_ context.Context) error { return nil }
271: 
272: // enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace re-enslaves this bridge's tracked endpoint
273: // interfaces (bridge-side veth ends) to the bridge inside the parent's
274: // namespace. Moving interfaces between namespaces (e.g. parking during parent
275: // recreation) clears the master, so restore paths need this fixup. Ports
276: // already enslaved are left untouched; missing ports are skipped and remain
277: // the link deployment path's responsibility.
278: func (b *bridge) enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace() error {
279: 	bridgeName := b.nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix()
280: 	nodeName := b.GetShortName()
281: 
282: 	return b.ExecFunction(context.Background(), func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
283: 		bridgeLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName)
284: 		if err != nil {
285: 			log.Debugf(
286: 				"bridge %q not found while enslaving ports, skipping: %v",
287: 				bridgeName,
288: 				err,
289: 			)
290: 			return nil
291: 		}
292: 
293: 		links, err := netlink.LinkList()
294: 		if err != nil {
295: 			return err
296: 		}
297: 
298: 		for _, ep := range b.GetEndpoints() {
299: 			for _, link := range links {
300: 				if !clablinks.HasOwnershipAltNameFor(
301: 					link,
302: 					nodeName,
303: 					ep.GetIfaceName(),
304: 				) {
305: 					continue
306: 				}
307: 
308: 				if link.Attrs().MasterIndex != bridgeLink.(*netlink.Bridge).Index {
309: 					if err := netlink.LinkSetMaster(link, bridgeLink); err != nil {
310: 						return fmt.Errorf("failed to enslave %q to %q: %w",
311: 							link.Attrs().Name, bridgeName, err)
312: 					}
313: 					log.Info(
314: 						"Re-enslaved restored bridge port to bridge",
315: 						"node",
316: 						nodeName,
317: 						"port",
318: 						link.Attrs().Name,
319: 					)
320: 				}
321: 
322: 				if link.Attrs().OperState != netlink.OperUp {
323: 					if err := netlink.LinkSetUp(link); err != nil {
324: 						return fmt.Errorf("failed to bring up %q: %w",
325: 							link.Attrs().Name, err)
326: 					}
327: 				}
328: 			}
329: 		}
330: 
331: 		return nil
332: 	})
333: }

335: func (b *bridge) GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
336: 	if b.containerNs != "" {

338: 		if err != nil {
339: 			return "", err
340: 		}
341: 		return parentNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
342: 	}
343: 	curns, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
344: 	if err != nil {
345: 		return "", err
346: 	}
347: 	return curns.Path(), nil
348: }

350: func (b *bridge) CheckDeploymentConditions(ctx context.Context) error {
351: 	err := b.VerifyHostRequirements()
352: 	if err != nil {
353: 		return err
354: 	}
355: 
356: 	if strings.HasPrefix(b.Cfg.NetworkMode, "container:") {
357: 		if b.Cfg.NetworkMode[10:] != b.GetShortName()[len(b.nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix())+1:] {
358: 			return fmt.Errorf("container based bridge requires container name as suffix %s != %s",
359: 				b.Cfg.NetworkMode[10:], b.GetShortName()[len(b.nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix())+1:])
360: 		}
361: 	}
362: 
363: 	// check bridge exists only if host ns
364: 	if b.containerNs == "" {
365: 		err = b.ExecFunction(ctx, func(nn ns.NetNS) error {
366: 			// check bridge exists
367: 			_, err = clabutils.BridgeByName(b.nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix())
368: 			if err != nil {
369: 				return err
370: 			}
371: 			return nil
372: 		})
373: 	}
374: 
375: 	return err
376: }

401: func (b *bridge) AddLinkToContainer(
402: 	ctx context.Context,
403: 	link netlink.Link,
404: 	f func(ns.NetNS) error,
405: ) error {
406: 	if b.Cfg.NetworkMode != "" {

412: func (b *bridge) addLinkToContainerNamespace(
413: 	ctx context.Context,
414: 	link netlink.Link,
415: 	f func(ns.NetNS) error,
416: ) error {
417: 	parentNode, err := b.resolveParentNode()
418: 	if err != nil {
419: 		return err
420: 	}
421: 	err = parentNode.AddLinkToContainer(ctx, link, func(nn ns.NetNS) error {
422: 		// get the bridge as netlink.Link
423: 		br, err := netlink.LinkByName(b.nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix())
424: 		if err != nil {
425: 			return err
426: 		}
427: 
428: 		// assign the bridge to the link as master
429: 		err = netlink.LinkSetMaster(link, br)
430: 		if err != nil {
431: 			return err
432: 		}
433: 
434: 		// execute the given function
435: 		return f(nn)
436: 	})
437: 	return err
438: }

440: func (b *bridge) addLinkToContainerHost(
441: 	_ context.Context,

444: ) error {

446: 	curNamespace, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
447: 	if err != nil {
448: 		return err

450: 
451: 	// get the bridge as netlink.Link
452: 	br, err := netlink.LinkByName(b.nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix())
453: 	if err != nil {
454: 		return err
455: 	}
456: 
457: 	// assign the bridge to the link as master
458: 	err = netlink.LinkSetMaster(link, br)
459: 	if err != nil {
460: 		return err
461: 	}
462: 
463: 	// execute the given function
464: 	return curNamespace.Do(f)
465: }

474: // installIPTablesBridgeFwdRule installs `allow` rule for the traffic routed in and out of the
475: // bridge
476: // otherwise, communication over the bridge is not permitted on most systems.
477: func (b *bridge) installIPTablesBridgeFwdRule() (err error) {
478: 	f, err := firewall.NewFirewallClient()
479: 	if err != nil {
480: 		return err
481: 	}
482: 	log.Debugf("setting up bridge firewall rules using %s as the firewall interface", f.Name())
483: 
484: 	r := definitions.FirewallRule{
485: 		Interface: b.nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix(),
486: 		Direction: definitions.InDirection,
487: 		Action:    definitions.AcceptAction,
488: 		Comment:   definitions.ContainerlabComment,
489: 		Table:     definitions.FilterTable,
490: 		Chain:     definitions.ForwardChain,
491: 	}
492: 	err = f.InstallForwardingRules(&r)
493: 	if err != nil {
494: 		return err
495: 	}
496: 
497: 	r = definitions.FirewallRule{
498: 		Interface: b.nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix(),
499: 		Direction: definitions.OutDirection,
500: 		Action:    definitions.AcceptAction,
501: 		Comment:   definitions.ContainerlabComment,
502: 		Table:     definitions.FilterTable,
503: 		Chain:     definitions.ForwardChain,
504: 	}
505: 
506: 	return f.InstallForwardingRules(&r)
507: }
