1: package links
2: 
3: import (
4: 	"context"
5: 	"fmt"
6: 	"strings"
7: 
8: 	"github.com/charmbracelet/log"
9: 	"github.com/containernetworking/plugins/pkg/ns"
10: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
11: 	"github.com/vishvananda/netlink"
12: )
13: 
14: // NSMigrationNode is the minimal node surface the bridge-port migration
15: // works with: exec context plus a resolvable namespace path.
16: type NSMigrationNode interface {
17: 	ExecFunction(ctx context.Context, f func(ns.NetNS) error) error
18: 	GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
19: 	GetShortName() string
20: }
21: 
22: // BridgePortRelocation describes a bridge-side veth end parked out of one
23: // namespace while the in-container bridge hosting it was replaced (a bridge
24: // parent move). The veth pair stays intact across the namespace hops: the
25: // client-side end keeps its address and MAC, and the parked half carries its
26: // device state until it is restored into the replacement namespace.
27: type BridgePortRelocation struct {
28: 	parkNSPath   string
29: 	KernelName   string // kernel-side name while parked
30: 	OldOwnerName string
31: 	IfaceName    string
32: 	LongName     string // replacement bridge node's long name; exercises the parking netns name
33: }
34: 
35: // ParkBridgePortByOwnership finds the interface carrying the ownership altname
36: // of (ownerName, ifaceName) in src's namespace and parks it into the parking
37: // netns of longName. The pair survives: only the parked half is relocated.
38: func ParkBridgePortByOwnership(
39: 	ctx context.Context,
40: 	src Node,
41: 	ownerName string,
42: 	ifaceName string,
43: 	longName string,
44: ) (*BridgePortRelocation, error) {
45: 	parkPath, err := clabutils.CreateOrGetNamedNetNS(clabutils.ParkingNetnsName(longName))
46: 	if err != nil {
47: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create parking netns for migration: %w", err)
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	relocation := &BridgePortRelocation{
51: 		parkNSPath:   parkPath,
52: 		OldOwnerName: ownerName,
53: 		IfaceName:    ifaceName,
54: 		LongName:     longName,
55: 	}
56: 
57: 	parkErr := src.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
58: 		link, err := findLinkByOwnershipAltName(ownerName, ifaceName)
59: 		if err != nil {
60: 			return err
61: 		}
62: 
63: 		relocation.KernelName = link.Attrs().Name
64: 
65: 		if err := netlink.LinkSetDown(link); err != nil {
66: 			log.Debug("failed to bring down interface while parking",
67: 				"iface", link.Attrs().Name, "err", err)
68: 		}
69: 
70: 		parkNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(parkPath)
71: 		if nsErr != nil {
72: 			return nsErr
73: 		}
74: 		defer parkNs.Close()
75: 
76: 		return netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(parkNs.Fd()))
77: 	})
78: 	if parkErr != nil {
79: 		_ = clabutils.UnlinkNamedNetNS(parkPath)
80: 		return nil, parkErr
81: 	}
82: 
83: 	return relocation, nil
84: }
85: 
86: // RestoreBridgePort moves the parked half into the replacement bridge's
87: // namespace, keeps/renames it to the desired kernel name, relabels the
88: // ownership altname to (newOwnerName, ifaceName) and re-enslaves it to the
89: // bridge. dst receives a node with both ExecFunction and GetNSPath.
90: func (r *BridgePortRelocation) RestoreBridgePort(
91: 	ctx context.Context,
92: 	dst NSMigrationNode,
93: 	newOwnerName string,
94: 	bridgeName string,
95: 	desiredKernelName string,
96: ) error {
97: 	parkExecErr := r.execInParkingNS(func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
98: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.KernelName)
99: 		if err != nil {
100: 			return fmt.Errorf("parked interface %q not found in parking ns: %w", r.KernelName, err)
101: 		}
102: 
103: 		dstPath, nsErr := dst.GetNSPath(ctx)
104: 		if nsErr != nil {
105: 			return nsErr
106: 		}
107: 		dstNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(dstPath)
108: 		if nsErr != nil {
109: 			return nsErr
110: 		}
111: 		defer dstNs.Close()
112: 
113: 		return netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(dstNs.Fd()))
114: 	})
115: 	if parkExecErr != nil {
116: 		return parkExecErr
117: 	}
118: 
119: 	dstErr := dst.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
120: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.KernelName)
121: 		if err != nil {
122: 			return fmt.Errorf("restored interface %q not found in destination ns: %w",
123: 				r.KernelName, err)
124: 		}
125: 
126: 		if desiredKernelName != "" && link.Attrs().Name != desiredKernelName {
127: 			if err := netlink.LinkSetName(link, desiredKernelName); err != nil {
128: 				return err
129: 			}
130: 			link.Attrs().Name = desiredKernelName
131: 		}
132: 
133: 		// Strip previous ownership markers and label with the new owner.
134: 		for _, altName := range link.Attrs().AltNames {
135: 			if !strings.HasPrefix(altName, ownershipAltNamePrefix) {
136: 				continue
137: 			}
138: 			if delErr := netlink.LinkDelAltName(link, altName); delErr != nil &&
139: 				!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(delErr) {
140: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to drop old ownership altname %q: %w", altName, delErr)
141: 			}
142: 		}
143: 		if addErr := linkAddAltName(
144: 			link,
145: 			ownershipAltNameFor(newOwnerName, r.IfaceName),
146: 		); addErr != nil &&
147: 			!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(addErr) {
148: 			return addErr
149: 		}
150: 
151: 		// Re-enslave to the replacement bridge, if present.
152: 		if bridgeName != "" {
153: 			if bridgeLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName); err == nil {
154: 				if link.Attrs().MasterIndex != bridgeLink.Attrs().Index {
155: 					if err := netlink.LinkSetMaster(link, bridgeLink); err != nil {
156: 						return fmt.Errorf("failed to enslave %q to %q: %w",
157: 							link.Attrs().Name, bridgeName, err)
158: 					}
159: 					log.Info("Re-enslaved migrated bridge port to replacement bridge",
160: 						"port", link.Attrs().Name, "bridge", bridgeName)
161: 				}
162: 			}
163: 		}
164: 
165: 		if link.Attrs().OperState != netlink.OperUp {
166: 			if upErr := netlink.LinkSetUp(link); upErr != nil {
167: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to bring up %q: %w", link.Attrs().Name, upErr)
168: 			}
169: 		}
170: 
171: 		return nil
172: 	})
173: 	if dstErr != nil {
174: 		return dstErr
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	// Clean up the now empty parking namespace.
178: 	_ = clabutils.UnlinkNamedNetNS(r.parkNSPath)
179: 
180: 	return nil
181: }
182: 
183: func (r *BridgePortRelocation) execInParkingNS(f func(ns.NetNS) error) error {
184: 	parkNs, err := ns.GetNS(r.parkNSPath)
185: 	if err != nil {
186: 		return err
187: 	}
188: 	defer parkNs.Close()
189: 
190: 	return parkNs.Do(f)
191: }
192: 
193: // RelabelOwnershipAltNameFor rewrites the ownership altname of the interface
194: // identified by (oldOwner, ifaceName) to (newOwner, ifaceName) inside node's
195: // namespace.
196: func RelabelOwnershipAltNameFor(
197: 	ctx context.Context,
198: 	node Node,
199: 	oldOwnerName string,
200: 	ifaceName string,
201: 	newOwnerName string,
202: ) error {
203: 	if newOwnerName == oldOwnerName {
204: 		return nil
205: 	}
206: 
207: 	return node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
208: 		link, err := findLinkByOwnershipAltName(oldOwnerName, ifaceName)
209: 		if err != nil {
210: 			// Fall back to the sanitized kernel name: short names kept their
211: 			// kernel name during relocation.
212: 			link, err = netlink.LinkByName(clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(ifaceName))
213: 			if err != nil {
214: 				return fmt.Errorf(
215: 					"interface to relabel ownership for %q (old owner %q) not found: %w",
216: 					ifaceName,
217: 					oldOwnerName,
218: 					err,
219: 				)
220: 			}
221: 		}
222: 
223: 		// Drop all previous ownership markers; ownership is single-valued.
224: 		for _, altName := range link.Attrs().AltNames {
225: 			if !strings.HasPrefix(altName, ownershipAltNamePrefix) {
226: 				continue
227: 			}
228: 			if delErr := netlink.LinkDelAltName(link, altName); delErr != nil &&
229: 				!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(delErr) {
230: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to drop old ownership altname %q: %w", altName, delErr)
231: 			}
232: 		}
233: 
234: 		return linkAddAltName(link, ownershipAltNameFor(newOwnerName, ifaceName))
235: 	})
236: }
237: 
238: // findLinkByOwnershipAltName scans the current namespace for the link carrying
239: // the ownership altname of (nodeName, ifaceName).
240: func findLinkByOwnershipAltName(nodeName, ifaceName string) (netlink.Link, error) {
241: 	links, err := netlink.LinkList()
242: 	if err != nil {
243: 		return nil, err
244: 	}
245: 	for _, link := range links {
246: 		if HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, nodeName, ifaceName) {
247: 			return link, nil
248: 		}
249: 	}
250: 	return nil, fmt.Errorf(
251: 		"no interface carries the ownership marker of %q for %q",
252: 		nodeName,
253: 		ifaceName,
254: 	)
255: }

(End of file - total 255 lines)

The pair survives: only the parked half is relocated.\nfunc ParkBridgePortByOwnership(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tsrc Node,\n\townerName string,\n\tifaceName string,\n\tlongName string,\n) (*BridgePortRelocation, error) {\n\tparkPath, err := clabutils.CreateOrGetNamedNetNS(clabutils.ParkingNetnsName(longName))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"failed to create parking netns for migration: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\trelocation := &BridgePortRelocation{\n\t\tparkNSPath:   parkPath,\n\t\tOldOwnerName: ownerName,\n\t\tIfaceName:    ifaceName,\n\t\tLongName:     longName,\n\t}\n\n\tparkErr := src.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {\n\t\tlink, err := findLinkByOwnershipAltName(ownerName, ifaceName)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\trelocation.KernelName = link.Attrs().Name\n\n\t\tif err := netlink.LinkSetDown(link); err != nil {\n\t\t\tlog.Debug(\"failed to bring down interface while parking\",\n\t\t\t\t\"iface\", link.Attrs().Name, \"err\", err)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tparkNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(parkPath)\n\t\tif nsErr != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nsErr\n\t\t}\n\t\tdefer parkNs.Close()\n\n\t\treturn netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(parkNs.Fd()))\n\t})\n\tif parkErr != nil {\n\t\t_ = clabutils.UnlinkNamedNetNS(parkPath)\n\t\treturn nil, parkErr\n\t}\n\n\treturn relocation, nil\n}\n\n// RestoreBridgePort moves the parked half into the replacement bridge's\n// namespace, keeps/renames it to the desired kernel name, relabels the\n// ownership altname to (newOwnerName, ifaceName) and re-enslaves it to the\n// bridge. dst receives a node with both ExecFunction and GetNSPath.\nfunc (r *BridgePortRelocation) RestoreBridgePort(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tdst NSMigrationNode,\n\tnewOwnerName string,\n\tbridgeName string,\n\tdesiredKernelName string,\n) error {\n\tparkExecErr := r.execInParkingNS(func(_ ns.NetNS) error {\n\t\tlink, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.KernelName)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"parked interface %q not found in parking ns: %w\", r.KernelName, err)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tdstPath, nsErr := dst.GetNSPath(ctx)\n\t\tif nsErr != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nsErr\n\t\t}\n\t\tdstNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(dstPath)\n\t\tif nsErr != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nsErr\n\t\t}\n\t\tdefer dstNs.Close()\n\n\t\treturn netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(dstNs.Fd()))\n\t})\n\tif parkExecErr != nil {\n\t\treturn parkExecErr\n\t}\n\n\tdstErr := dst.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {\n\t\tlink, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.KernelName)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"restored interface %q not found in destination ns: %w\",\n\t\t\t\tr.KernelName, err)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif desiredKernelName != \"\" && link.Attrs().Name != desiredKernelName {\n\t\t\tif err := netlink.LinkSetName(link, desiredKernelName); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tlink.Attrs().Name = desiredKernelName\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Strip previous ownership markers and label with the new owner.\n\t\tfor _, altName := range link.Attrs().AltNames {\n\t\t\tif !strings.HasPrefix(altName, ownershipAltNamePrefix) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif delErr := netlink.LinkDelAltName(link, altName); delErr != nil &&\n\t\t\t\t!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(delErr) {\n\t\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to drop old ownership altname %q: %w\", altName, delErr)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif addErr := linkAddAltName(\n\t\t\tlink,\n\t\t\townershipAltNameFor(newOwnerName, r.IfaceName),\n\t\t); addErr != nil &&\n\t\t\t!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(addErr) {\n\t\t\treturn addErr\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Re-enslave to the replacement bridge, if present.\n\t\tif bridgeName != \"\" {\n\t\t\tif bridgeLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName); err == nil {\n\t\t\t\tif link.Attrs().MasterIndex != bridgeLink.Attrs().Index {\n\t\t\t\t\tif err := netlink.LinkSetMaster(link, bridgeLink); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to enslave %q to %q: %w\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tlink.Attrs().Name, bridgeName, err)\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tlog.Info(\"Re-enslaved migrated bridge port to replacement bridge\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\"port\", link.Attrs().Name, \"bridge\", bridgeName)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif link.Attrs().OperState != netlink.OperUp {\n\t\t\tif upErr := netlink.LinkSetUp(link); upErr != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to bring up %q: %w\", link.Attrs().Name, upErr)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\treturn nil\n\t})\n\tif dstErr != nil {\n\t\treturn dstErr\n\t}\n\n\t// Clean up the now empty parking namespace.\n\t_ = clabutils.UnlinkNamedNetNS(r.parkNSPath)\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *BridgePortRelocation) execInParkingNS(f func(ns.NetNS) error) error {\n\tparkNs, err := ns.GetNS(r.parkNSPath)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tdefer parkNs.Close()\n\n\treturn parkNs.Do(f)\n}\n\n// RelabelOwnershipAltNameFor rewrites the ownership altname of the interface\n// identified by (oldOwner, ifaceName) to (newOwner, ifaceName) inside node's\n// namespace.\nfunc RelabelOwnershipAltNameFor(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tnode Node,\n\toldOwnerName string,\n\tifaceName string,\n\tnewOwnerName string,\n) error {\n\tif newOwnerName == oldOwnerName {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\treturn node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {\n\t\tlink, err := findLinkByOwnershipAltName(oldOwnerName, ifaceName)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t// Fall back to the sanitized kernel name: short names kept their\n\t\t\t// kernel name during relocation.\n\t\t\tlink, err = netlink.LinkByName(clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(ifaceName))\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\t\"interface to relabel ownership for %q (old owner %q) not found: %w\",\n\t\t\t\t\tifaceName,\n\t\t\t\t\toldOwnerName,\n\t\t\t\t\terr,\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Drop all previous ownership markers; ownership is single-valued.\n\t\tfor _, altName := range link.Attrs().AltNames {\n\t\t\tif !strings.HasPrefix(altName, ownershipAltNamePrefix) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif delErr := netlink.LinkDelAltName(link, altName); delErr != nil &&\n\t\t\t\t!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(delErr) {\n\t\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to drop old ownership altname %q: %w\", altName, delErr)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\treturn linkAddAltName(link, ownershipAltNameFor(newOwnerName, ifaceName))\n\t})\n}\n\n// findLinkByOwnershipAltName scans the current namespace for the link carrying\n// the ownership altname of (nodeName, ifaceName).\nfunc findLinkByOwnershipAltName(nodeName, ifaceName string) (netlink.Link, error) {\n\tlinks, err := netlink.LinkList()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tfor _, link := range links {\n\t\tif HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, nodeName, ifaceName) {\n\t\t\treturn link, nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\"no interface carries the ownership marker of %q for %q\",\n\t\tnodeName,\n\t\tifaceName,\n\t)\n}",

142: func DiscoverEndpointsForBridgeNS(

170: 			if !hasOwnershipAltName(link) {

172: 			}
173: 
174: 			// Match against the desired logical endpoint names
175: 			// recorded in this interface's ownership altname.
176: 			logical, found := matchOwnedInterface(link, ownerName, desiredNames)
177: 
178: 			info := OwnedInterface{
179: 				Name:        name,
180: 				Index:       link.Attrs().Index,
181: 				MasterIndex: link.Attrs().MasterIndex,
182: 				Type:        link.Type(),
183: 			}

186: 				if masterErr != nil {
187: 					return fmt.Errorf("failed to discover master for %q: %w", name, masterErr)

191: 			if info.Type == "veth" {

193: 				if !ok {
194: 					veth = &netlink.Veth{LinkAttrs: *link.Attrs()}
195: 				}

332: // bridgePortDeleter removes a bridge port that can outlive its netdev. OVS ports created for an
333: // interface name Linux will not accept are named after the random netdev, so deleting the veth
334: // from the container side leaves the port behind.

339: func removeBridgePort(node Node, ifaceName string) error {

341: 		return nil
342: 	}

346: 		return nil

349: 	// Best-effort, matching ovs.Delete. A missing bridge or a down ovsdb must not abort
350: 	// destroy or reconcile and leave the container running.
351: 	if err := cleaner.DeleteBridgePort(ifaceName); err != nil {
352: 		log.Errorf(

354: 			ifaceName,

359:

361: }

365: // releases carry a marker for the bridge name of the mgmt-net link node instead
366: // of the stable mgmt-net owner name, and are accepted as well.
367: func isOwnedBy(link netlink.Link, node Node, ownerName, ifaceName string) bool {

369: 		return true

372: 	if _, ok := node.(*mgmtBridgeLinkNode); ok && ownerName == mgmtNetOwnerName {
373: 		return HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, node.GetShortName(), ifaceName)
374: 	}

1: package core

3: import (

13: // bridgeNSMigParentNode resolves the namespace host of a migrated bridge-side
14: // endpoint. Stale refs carry either a live bridge node (resolved via the
15: // topology) or the name-encoded <bridge>|<parent> form of a node that is
16: // already removed from the desired topology.
17: func (c *CLab) bridgeNSMigParentNode(ref applyEndpointRef) (clablinks.Node, error) {
18: 	if parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSParentNode(ref.key.node); err == nil {
19: 		return parentNode, nil
20: 	}
21: 	parts := strings.SplitN(ref.key.node, "|", 2)
22: 	if len(parts) != 2 {
23: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot resolve namespace host of bridge %q", ref.key.node)
24: 	}
25: 	node, exists := c.Nodes[parts[1]]
26: 	if !exists {
27: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
28: 			"bridge %q: parent container %q not found",
29: 			ref.key.node,
30: 			parts[1],
31: 		)
32: 	}
33: 	return node, nil
34: }
35: 
36: // parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts parks bridge-side veth ends whose owning in-container
37: // bridge was replaced by a bridge under a different parent (the move case).
38: // The veth pair stays intact: only the parked half leaves the dying parent's
39: // namespace, so the client-side end keeps its state untouched.
40: func (c *CLab) parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts(
41: 	ctx context.Context,
42: 	plan *applyPlan,
43: ) error {
44: 	if plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {
45: 		return nil
46: 	}
47: 
48: 	for i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
49: 		mig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]
50: 
51: 		if mig.relocation != nil {
52: 			continue
53: 		}
54: 
55: 		// The old bridge node may already be deleted from the desired topology
56: 		// (the move case); resolve its namespace host by the name-encoded
57: 		// parent suffix, falling back to the normal resolution.
58: 		parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSMigParentNode(mig.staleRef)
59: 		if err != nil {
60: 			return err
61: 		}
62: 
63: 		newNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]
64: 		if !exists {
65: 			return fmt.Errorf("bridge migration target %q not found", mig.newKey.node)
66: 		}
67: 		longName := newNode.Config().LongName
68: 
69: 		relocation, err := clablinks.ParkBridgePortByOwnership(
70: 			ctx,
71: 			parentNode,
72: 			mig.staleRef.key.node,
73: 			mig.staleRef.key.iface,
74: 			longName,
75: 		)
76: 		if err != nil {
77: 			return err
78: 		}
79: 
80: 		mig.relocation = relocation
81: 	}
82: 
83: 	return nil
84: }
85: 
86: // restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts moves parked bridge-side ends into the replacement
87: // bridge's parent namespace after that container (and the bridge) exist again,
88: // relabels the ownership altname to the replacement bridge node, and re-enslaves
89: // the port to the bridge. The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed so
90: // deployLinks skips pair re-creation for it.
91: func (c *CLab) restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts(
92: 	ctx context.Context,
93: 	plan *applyPlan,
94: ) error {
95: 	if plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {
96: 		return nil
97: 	}
98: 
99: 	for i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
100: 		mig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]
101: 
102: 		if mig.relocation == nil || plan.plannedLinkSet == nil {
103: 			continue
104: 		}
105: 
106: 		// Restore into the replacement bridge's parent namespace; the bridge
107: 		// node interfaces with the parent's ns through its GetNSPath override.
108: 		bridgeNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]
109: 		if !exists {
110: 			return fmt.Errorf("bridge migration target %q not found", mig.newKey.node)
111: 		}
112: 
113: 		if err := mig.relocation.RestoreBridgePort(
114: 			ctx,
115: 			bridgeNode,
116: 			mig.newKey.node,
117: 			bridgeNSNameInNamespace(mig.newKey.node),
118: 			clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(mig.newKey.iface),
119: 		); err != nil {
120: 			return err
121: 		}
122: 
123: 		// The migrated pair is complete end-to-end (the client-side end was
124: 		// never touched and the parked bridge-side half is restored and
125: 		// enslaved). Filter the corresponding replaced link out of addedLinks
126: 		// so endpoint removal and pair re-creation never touch it.
127: 		kept := plan.addedLinks[:0]
128: 		for _, link := range plan.addedLinks {
129: 			if clablinks.RuntimeEndpointsContainEndpoint(
130: 				link,
131: 				mig.newKey.node,
132: 				mig.newKey.iface,
133: 			) {
134: 				log.Info(
135: 					"Restored migrated bridge port into replacement bridge",
136: 					"bridge",
137: 					mig.newKey.node,
138: 					"port",
139: 					mig.newKey.iface,
140: 				)
141: 				continue
142: 			}
143: 			kept = append(kept, link)
144: 		}
145: 		plan.addedLinks = kept
146: 	}
147: 
148: 	return nil
149: }

err == nil {\n\t\treturn parentNode, nil\n\t}\n\tparts := strings.SplitN(ref.key.node, \"|\", 2)\n\tif len(parts) != 2 {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"cannot resolve namespace host of bridge %q\", ref.key.node)\n\t}\n\tnode, exists := c.Nodes[parts[1]]\n\tif !exists {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\"bridge %q: parent container %q not found\",\n\t\t\tref.key.node,\n\t\t\tparts[1],\n\t\t)\n\t}\n\treturn node, nil\n}\n\n// parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts parks bridge-side veth ends whose owning in-container\n// bridge was replaced by a bridge under a different parent (the move case).\n// The veth pair stays intact: only the parked half leaves the dying parent's\n// namespace, so the client-side end keeps its state untouched.\nfunc (c *CLab) parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tplan *applyPlan,\n) error {\n\tif plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {\n\t\tmig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]\n\n\t\tif mig.relocation != nil {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// The old bridge node may already be deleted from the desired topology\n\t\t// (the move case); resolve its namespace host by the name-encoded\n\t\t// parent suffix, falling back to the normal resolution.\n\t\tparentNode, err := c.bridgeNSMigParentNode(mig.staleRef)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tnewNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]\n\t\tif !exists {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"bridge migration target %q not found\", mig.newKey.node)\n\t\t}\n\t\tlongName := newNode.Config().LongName\n\n\t\trelocation, err := clablinks.ParkBridgePortByOwnership(\n\t\t\tctx,\n\t\t\tparentNode,\n\t\t\tmig.staleRef.key.node,\n\t\t\tmig.staleRef.key.iface,\n\t\t\tlongName,\n\t\t)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tmig.relocation = relocation\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts moves parked bridge-side ends into the replacement\n// bridge's parent namespace after that container (and the bridge) exist again,\n// relabels the ownership altname to the replacement bridge node, and re-enslaves\n// the port to the bridge. The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed so\n// deployLinks skips pair re-creation for it.\nfunc (c *CLab) restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tplan *applyPlan,\n) error {\n\tif plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {\n\t\tmig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]\n\n\t\tif mig.relocation == nil || plan.plannedLinkSet == nil {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Restore into the replacement bridge's parent namespace; the bridge\n\t\t// node interfaces with the parent's ns through its GetNSPath override.\n\t\tbridgeNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]\n\t\tif !exists {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"bridge migration target %q not found\", mig.newKey.node)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif err := mig.relocation.RestoreBridgePort(\n\t\t\tctx,\n\t\t\tbridgeNode,\n\t\t\tmig.newKey.node,\n\t\t\tbridgeNSNameInNamespace(mig.newKey.node),\n\t\t\tclabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(mig.newKey.iface),\n\t\t); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// The migrated pair is complete end-to-end (the client-side end was\n\t\t// never touched and the parked bridge-side half is restored and\n\t\t// enslaved). Filter the corresponding replaced link out of addedLinks\n\t\t// so endpoint removal and pair re-creation never touch it.\n\t\tkept := plan.addedLinks[:0]\n\t\tfor _, link := range plan.addedLinks {\n\t\t\tif clablinks.RuntimeEndpointsContainEndpoint(\n\t\t\t\tlink,\n\t\t\t\tmig.newKey.node,\n\t\t\t\tmig.newKey.iface,\n\t\t\t) {\n\t\t\t\tlog.Info(\n\t\t\t\t\t\"Restored migrated bridge port into replacement bridge\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\"bridge\",\n\t\t\t\t\tmig.newKey.node,\n\t\t\t\t\t\"port\",\n\t\t\t\t\tmig.newKey.iface,\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tkept = append(kept, link)\n\t\t}\n\t\tplan.addedLinks = kept\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}",

23: func (c *CLab) runtimeNodeGroups(
24: 	ctx context.Context,
25: ) (map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup, error) {
26: 	containers, err := c.ListContainers(ctx, WithListLabName(c.Config.Name))
27: 	if err != nil {
28: 		return nil, err
29: 	}
30: 
31: 	result := make(map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup)
32: 	var duplicates []string
33:

36: 			continue
37: 		}

39: 		nodeName := ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]

41: 			continue
42: 		}
43:

45: 		distributed := groupName != ""
46: 		if groupName == "" {
47: 			groupName = nodeName
48: 		}
49: 
50: 		group, exists := result[groupName]
51: 		if !exists {
52: 			group = &runtimeNodeGroup{
53: 				name:        groupName,
54: 				distributed: distributed,
55: 			}
56: 			result[groupName] = group
57: 		}
58: 		group.containers = append(group.containers, ctr)
59: 		group.distributed = group.distributed || distributed
60: 
61: 		if !group.distributed && len(group.containers) > 1 {
62: 			duplicates = append(duplicates, nodeName)
63: 			continue
64: 		}
65: 	}
66: 
67: 	// Pre-existing resources have no containerlab labels, but still participate in apply.
68: 	for nodeName, node := range c.Nodes {
69: 		cfg := node.Config()
70: 		if cfg == nil {
71: 			continue
72: 		}
73: 		if _, exists := result[nodeName]; exists {
74: 			continue
75: 		}
76: 		if cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased {
77: 			result[nodeName] = &runtimeNodeGroup{
78: 				name:               nodeName,
79: 				rootNamespaceBased: true,
80: 			}
81: 			continue
82: 		}
83: 		// BridgeNS bridges (in-container bridges) don't have their own containers,
84: 		// but they do represent real resources. Check if parent container exists.
85: 		//
86: 		// Trade-off: We only check parent container existence, not the actual bridge
87: 		// interface inside the parent. This is fast and simple, but may show the bridge
88: 		// as "current" when the bridge interface is missing (e.g., after container
89: 		// recreation). The detailed bridge existence check is handled during
90: 		// reconciliation by linkIntact() and bridgeMasterMismatch().
91: 		if cfg.Kind == "bridge" && cfg.NetworkMode != "" && cfg.NetworkMode != "host" {
92: 			if parentName, err := clabutils.ContainerNameFromNetworkMode(
93: 				cfg.NetworkMode,
94: 			); err == nil {
95: 				if _, parentExists := result[parentName]; parentExists {
96: 					result[nodeName] = &runtimeNodeGroup{
97: 						name:               nodeName,
98: 						rootNamespaceBased: true,
99: 					}
100: 				}
101: 			}
102: 			continue
103: 		}
104: 		if !cfg.SkipUniquenessCheck || node.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.NotFound {
105: 			continue
106: 		}
107: 		result[nodeName] = &runtimeNodeGroup{name: nodeName, external: true}
108: 	}
109: 
110: 	if len(duplicates) > 0 {
111: 		sort.Strings(duplicates)
112: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
113: 			"apply supports only single-container nodes, found multiple containers for nodes: %s",
114: 			strings.Join(duplicates, ", "),
115: 		)
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	for _, group := range result {
119: 		sort.Slice(group.containers, func(i, j int) bool {
120: 			return runtimeContainerLess(group.containers[i], group.containers[j])
121: 		})
122: 	}
123: 
124: 	return result, nil
125: }

127: // NeedsInitialDeploy reports whether the lab has no runtime state yet, i.e. whether

129: func (c *CLab) NeedsInitialDeploy(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) {
130: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
131: 		checker, ok := c.LabRuntime.(clablabruntime.LabExistenceChecker)
132: 		if !ok {
133: 			return false, fmt.Errorf(
134: 				"lab runtime %q cannot determine whether the lab already exists",
135: 				c.globalRuntimeName,
136: 			)
137: 		}

140: 			Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
141: 		})
142: 
143: 		return !exists, err
144: 	}
145: 
146: 	currentNodes, err := c.runtimeNodeGroups(ctx)
147: 	if err != nil {
148: 		return false, err
149: 	}
150: 
151: 	return c.needsInitialDeploy(currentNodes)
152: }

154: func (c *CLab) needsInitialDeploy(currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup) (bool, error) {
155: 	if len(currentNodes) == 0 {
156: 		return true, nil
157: 	}
158: 	for _, node := range currentNodes {
159: 		if !node.external && !node.rootNamespaceBased {
160: 			return false, nil
161: 		}
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	state, err := c.LoadState()
165: 	return state == nil, err
166: }

168: func (c *CLab) setMgmtBridgeFromRuntime(
169: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
170: ) error {
171: 	if c.Config.Mgmt.Bridge != "" {
172: 		return nil
173: 	}
174: 
175: 	var bridge string
176: 	for _, runtimeNode := range currentNodes {
177: 		for _, ctr := range runtimeNode.containers {
178: 			// only containers attached to the default management network, or
179: 			// without a runtime network, carry the default network's bridge
180: 			// label. Unknown networks, e.g. ones dropped from the mgmt list,
181: 			// must not contribute their bridge.
182: 			switch ctr.NetworkName {
183: 			case "", c.Config.Mgmt.Network:
184: 			default:
185: 				continue
186: 			}
187: 			ctrBridge := ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeMgmtNetBr]
188: 			if ctrBridge == "" {
189: 				continue
190: 			}
191: 			if bridge == "" {
192: 				bridge = ctrBridge
193: 				continue
194: 			}
195: 			if bridge != ctrBridge {
196: 				return fmt.Errorf(
197: 					"runtime lab has conflicting management bridge labels: %q and %q",
198: 					bridge,
199: 					ctrBridge,
200: 				)
201: 			}
202: 		}
203: 	}
204: 
205: 	if bridge != "" {
206: 		c.Config.Mgmt.Bridge = bridge
207: 	}
208: 
209: 	return nil
210: }

212: func (c *CLab) updateRuntimeInfoForExistingNodes(ctx context.Context) error {
213: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
214: 		node := c.Nodes[nodeName]
215: 		if node.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.NotFound {
216: 			continue
217: 		}
218: 		if err := node.UpdateConfigWithRuntimeInfo(ctx); err != nil {
219: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to update runtime info for node %q: %w", nodeName, err)
220: 		}
221: 	}
222: 
223: 	return nil
224: }
225: 
226: func sortedRuntimeNodeGroupNames(nodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup) []string {
227: 	names := make([]string, 0, len(nodes))
228: 	for name := range nodes {
229: 		names = append(names, name)
230: 	}
231: 	sort.Strings(names)
232: 	return names
233: }
234: 
235: func runtimeContainerNodeName(ctr clabruntime.GenericContainer) string {
236: 	if name := ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]; name != "" {
237: 		return name
238: 	}
239: 	if len(ctr.Names) > 0 {
240: 		return ctr.Names[0]
241: 	}
242: 	return ctr.ID
243: }
244: 
245: func runtimeContainerLess(a, b clabruntime.GenericContainer) bool {
246: 	// internal holders own the network namespace of the other containers in the group,
247: 	// so they sort first to be deleted last.
248: 	aInternal := a.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true"
249: 	bInternal := b.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true"
250: 	if aInternal != bInternal {
251: 		return aInternal
252: 	}
253: 
254: 	aName := runtimeContainerNodeName(a)
255: 	bName := runtimeContainerNodeName(b)
256: 
257: 	aOrder := runtimeComponentSortOrder(aName)
258: 	bOrder := runtimeComponentSortOrder(bName)
259: 	if aOrder != bOrder {
260: 		return aOrder < bOrder
261: 	}
262: 
263: 	return aName < bName
264: }
265: 
266: func runtimeComponentSortOrder(name string) int {
267: 	idx := strings.LastIndex(name, "-")
268: 	if idx < 0 || idx == len(name)-1 {
269: 		return 0
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	slot := strings.ToUpper(name[idx+1:])
273: 	if len(slot) == 1 && slot[0] >= 'A' && slot[0] <= 'Z' {
274: 		return 100 - int(slot[0])
275: 	}
276: 
277: 	var n int
278: 	for _, r := range slot {
279: 		if r < '0' || r > '9' {
280: 			return 0
281: 		}
282: 		n = n*10 + int(r-'0')
283: 	}
284: 
285: 	return n
286: }

268: func (c *CLab) checkApplyTopologyDefinition(ctx context.Context) error {
269: 	params := *clablinks.NewVerifyLinkParams()
270: 	if len(c.Endpoints) > 0 {
271: 		runtime := c.globalRuntime()
272: 		if runtime == nil {
273: 			return fmt.Errorf("container runtime is not initialized")
274: 		}
275: 		config := runtime.Config()
276: 		if config.VerifyLinkParams != nil {
277: 			params = *config.VerifyLinkParams
278: 		}
279: 	}
280: 	params.AllowExistingEndpoint = true
281: 	if err := c.verifyLinks(ctx, &params); err != nil {
282: 		return err
283: 	}
284: 
285: 	if err := c.verifyRootNetNSLinks(); err != nil {
286: 		return err
287: 	}
288: 
289: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
290: 		if err := c.Nodes[nodeName].CheckDeploymentConditions(ctx); err != nil {
291: 			return err
292: 		}
293: 	}
294: 
295: 	if err := c.verifyDuplicateAddresses(); err != nil {
296: 		return err
297: 	}
298: 
299: 	return c.verifyTailscaleProxy()
300: }

302: func (c *CLab) prepareApply(
303: 	ctx context.Context,
304: 	addedNodes []string,
305: 	skipLabDirFileACLs bool,
306: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
307: ) error {
308: 	existing := c.collectExistingManagementAddresses(currentNodes)
309: 	if err := c.prepareLabManagementNetwork(ctx, existing...); err != nil {
310: 		return err

314: 		return err
315: 	}
316:

318: 		if err := c.Nodes[nodeName].PullImage(ctx); err != nil {
319: 			return err
320: 		}

322: 
323: 	return nil
324: }

326: func (c *CLab) removeApplyLinkEndpoints(ctx context.Context, links []clablinks.Link) error {
327: 	for _, link := range links {
328: 		for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
329: 			node := ep.GetNode()
330: 
331: 			// For BridgeNS bridge endpoints, use RemoveInterface instead of
332: 			// RemoveOwnedInterface: bridge-attached interfaces are owned by the remote
333: 			// endpoint, so per-node ownership checks would always fail.
334: 			if node.GetLinkEndpointType() == clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS {
335: 				parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSParentNode(node.GetShortName())
336: 				if err != nil {
337: 					return err
338: 				}
339: 				if err := clablinks.RemoveInterface(
340: 					ctx,
341: 					parentNode,
342: 					ep.GetIfaceName(),
343: 				); err != nil {
344: 					return err
345: 				}
346: 				continue
347: 			}
348: 
349: 			if err := clablinks.RemoveOwnedInterface(
350: 				ctx,
351: 				node,
352: 				ep.GetIfaceName(),
353: 			); err != nil {
354: 				return err
355: 			}
356: 		}
357: 	}
358: 
359: 	return nil
360: }

362: // try to preserve the existing addressing instead of reallocation.
363: func (c *CLab) collectExistingManagementAddresses(
364: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
365: ) []clabtypes.ExistingAddress {
366: 	var existing []clabtypes.ExistingAddress
367: 	for name, group := range currentNodes {
368: 		for _, ctr := range group.containers {
369: 			if c.mgmtNetByNetwork(ctr.NetworkName).Network != ctr.NetworkName {
370: 				continue
371: 			}
372: 			for _, value := range []string{ctr.NetworkSettings.IPv4addr, ctr.NetworkSettings.IPv6addr} {
373: 				if ip, err := netip.ParseAddr(value); err == nil {
374: 					existing = append(
375: 						existing,
376: 						clabtypes.ExistingAddress{NodeName: name, ContainerID: ctr.ID, Address: ip},
377: 					)
378: 				}
379: 			}
380: 		}
381: 	}
382: 	return existing
383: }

5: package utils
6: 
7: import (
8: 	"crypto/rand"
9: 	"crypto/sha1"
10: 	"encoding/hex"
11: 	"fmt"
12: 	"net"
13: 	"net/netip"
14: 	"os"
15: 	"path/filepath"
16: 	goruntime "runtime"
17: 	"strings"
18: 
19: 	"github.com/charmbracelet/log"
20: 	"github.com/jsimonetti/rtnetlink/rtnl"
21: 	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
22: 	"github.com/vishvananda/netlink"
23: 	"github.com/vishvananda/netns"
24: )
25: 
26: func netlinkFamily(ip netip.Addr) int {
27: 	if ip.Is4() {
28: 		return netlink.FAMILY_V4
29: 	}
30: 	if ip.Is6() {
31: 		return netlink.FAMILY_V6
32: 	}
33: 	return netlink.FAMILY_ALL
34: }
35: 
36: const (
37: 	parkingNetnsPrefix = "clab-park-"
38: 	// Be conservative and keep the name comfortably within Linux NAME_MAX (255 bytes).
39: 	maxParkingNetnsNameLen = 200
40: )
41: 
42: // BridgeByName returns a *netlink.Bridge referenced by its name.
43: func BridgeByName(name string) (*netlink.Bridge, error) {
44: 	l, err := netlink.LinkByName(name)
45: 	if err != nil {
46: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("could not lookup %q: %v", name, err)
47: 	}
48: 	br, ok := l.(*netlink.Bridge)
49: 	if !ok {
50: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q already exists but is not a bridge", name)
51: 	}
52: 	return br, nil
53: }
54: 
55: // LinkContainerNS creates a symlink for containers network namespace
56: // so that it can be managed by iproute2 utility.
57: func LinkContainerNS(nspath, containerName string) error {
58: 	CreateDirectory("/run/netns/", clabconstants.PermissionsDirDefault)
59: 	dst := "/run/netns/" + containerName
60: 	if _, err := os.Lstat(dst); err == nil {
61: 		os.Remove(dst)
62: 	}
63: 	err := os.Symlink(nspath, dst)
64: 	if err != nil {
65: 		return err
66: 	}
67: 	return nil
68: }
69: 
70: // GenMac generates a random MAC address for a given OUI.
71: func GenMac(oui string) (net.HardwareAddr, error) {
72: 	buf := make([]byte, 3)
73: 	_, _ = rand.Read(buf)
74: 
75: 	hwa, err := net.ParseMAC(fmt.Sprintf("%s:%02x:%02x:%02x", oui, buf[0], buf[1], buf[2]))
76: 	return hwa, err
77: }
78: 
79: // DeleteNetnsSymlink deletes a network namespace and removes the symlink created by LinkContainerNS
80: // func.
81: func DeleteNetnsSymlink(n string) error {
82: 	log.Debug("Deleting netns symlink: ", n)
83: 	sl := fmt.Sprintf("/run/netns/%s", n)
84: 	err := os.Remove(sl)
85: 	if err != nil {
86: 		log.Debug("Failed to delete netns symlink by path:", sl)
87: 	}
88: 	return nil
89: }
90: 
91: // ParkingNetnsName returns the deterministic named-netns identifier used to park
92: // a container's dataplane interfaces while the container is stopped.
93: func ParkingNetnsName(containerName string) string {
94: 	name := parkingNetnsPrefix + containerName
95: 	if len(name) <= maxParkingNetnsNameLen {
96: 		return name
97: 	}
98: 
99: 	sum := sha1.Sum([]byte(containerName))
100: 	suffix := hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])[:10]
101: 
102: 	// leave room for "-" + suffix
103: 	maxBaseLen := maxParkingNetnsNameLen - 1 - len(suffix)
104: 	if maxBaseLen < 1 {
105: 		return suffix
106: 	}
107: 
108: 	return name[:maxBaseLen] + "-" + suffix
109: }
110: 
111: // LinkIPs returns IPv4/IPv6 addresses assigned to a link referred by its name.
112: func LinkIPs(ln string) (v4addrs, v6addrs []netlink.Addr, err error) {
113: 	l, err := netlink.LinkByName(ln)
114: 	if err != nil {
115: 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to lookup link %q: %w", ln, err)
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	v4addrs, err = netlink.AddrList(l, netlink.FAMILY_V4)
119: 	if err != nil {
120: 		return nil, nil, err
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	v6addrs, err = netlink.AddrList(l, netlink.FAMILY_V6)
124: 	if err != nil {
125: 		return nil, nil, err
126: 	}
127: 
128: 	return
129: }
130: 
131: // FirstLinkIPs returns string representation of the first IPv4/v6 address
132: // found for a link referenced by name.
133: func FirstLinkIPs(ln string) (v4, v6 string, err error) {
134: 	v4addrs, v6addrs, err := LinkIPs(ln)
135: 	if err != nil {
136: 		return
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	if len(v4addrs) != 0 {
140: 		v4 = v4addrs[0].IP.String()
141: 	}
142: 
143: 	if len(v6addrs) != 0 {
144: 		v6 = v6addrs[0].IP.String()
145: 	}
146: 
147: 	return v4, v6, err
148: }
149: 
150: // GetLinksByNamePrefix returns a list of links whose name matches a prefix.
151: func GetLinksByNamePrefix(prefix string) ([]netlink.Link, error) {
152: 	// filtered list of interfaces
153: 	if prefix == "" {
154: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("prefix is not specified")
155: 	}
156: 	var fls []netlink.Link
157: 
158: 	ls, err := netlink.LinkList()
159: 	if err != nil {
160: 		return nil, err
161: 	}
162: 	for _, l := range ls {
163: 		if strings.HasPrefix(l.Attrs().Name, prefix) {
164: 			fls = append(fls, l)
165: 		}
166: 	}
167: 	if len(fls) == 0 {
168: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no links found by specified prefix %s", prefix)
169: 	}
170: 	return fls, nil
171: }
172: 
173: func GetRouteForIP(ip net.IP) (*rtnl.Route, error) {
174: 	conn, err := rtnl.Dial(nil)
175: 	if err != nil {
176: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("can't establish netlink connection: %s", err)
177: 	}
178: 	defer conn.Close()
179: 
180: 	r, err := conn.RouteGet(ip)
181: 
182: 	return r, err
183: }
184: 
185: func CreateNamedNetNS(name string) (string, error) {
186: 	nsPath := filepath.Join("/run/netns", name)
187: 
188: 	goruntime.LockOSThread()
189: 	defer goruntime.UnlockOSThread()
190: 
191: 	currentNS, err := netns.Get()
192: 	if err != nil {
193: 		return "", err
194: 	}
195: 	defer currentNS.Close()
196: 
197: 	defer func() {
198: 		_ = netns.Set(currentNS)
199: 	}()
200: 
201: 	newNS, err := netns.NewNamed(name)
202: 	if err != nil {
203: 		if os.IsExist(err) && FileOrDirExists(nsPath) {
204: 			return nsPath, nil
205: 		}
206: 		return "", err
207: 	}
208: 
209: 	newNS.Close()
210: 
211: 	return nsPath, nil
212: }
213: 
214: // create a new netns or return the nspath if it exists.
215: func CreateOrGetNamedNetNS(name string) (string, error) {
216: 	if nsPath, err := GetNamedNetNS(name); err == nil {
217: 		return nsPath, nil
218: 	}
219: 
220: 	return CreateNamedNetNS(name)
221: }
222: 
223: // GetNamedNetNS returns the nspath of the named netns, if it exists.
224: func GetNamedNetNS(name string) (string, error) {
225: 	nsPath := filepath.Join("/run/netns", name)
226: 	if !FileOrDirExists(nsPath) {
227: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("named netns %q does not exist", name)
228: 	}
229: 
230: 	return nsPath, nil
231: }
232: 
233: // UnlinkNamedNetNS removes the named netns symlink/mount, best effort.
234: func UnlinkNamedNetNS(nsPath string) error {
235: 	if !FileOrDirExists(nsPath) {
236: 		return nil
237: 	}
238: 
239: 	return os.Remove(nsPath)
240: }
241: 
242: // SanitizeInterfaceName sanitizes the interface name by replacing '/' and ' ' with '-'.
243: // Making it suitable to write as AltName for the interface.
244: func SanitizeInterfaceName(ifaceName string) string {
245: 	var sb strings.Builder
246: 	sb.Grow(len(ifaceName))
247: 
248: 	for _, char := range ifaceName {
249: 		switch char {
250: 		case '/', ' ':
251: 			sb.WriteRune('-')
252: 		default:
253: 			sb.WriteRune(char)
254: 		}
255: 	}
256: 
257: 	return sb.String()
258: }

Reasoning
Now I have the utils/netlink.go details. Important facts:

- `CreateNamedNetNS` uses `netns.NewNamed(name)` which creates a **bind mount** at `/run/netns/<name>` (it's a mount point, not a symlink). So `UnlinkNamedNetNS` uses `os.Remove(nsPath)` — `os.Remove` on a mounted file... Actually for bind mounts, `os.Remove` (unlink syscall) on a mount point returns EBUSY. `ip netns del` uses `umount2` first then `unlink`. So `UnlinkNamedNetNS` will fail with EBUSY for a real mounted netns → the parking netns leaks. Wait — but is `netns.NewNamed` a bind mount? Yes, vishvananda/netns NewNamed creates a new netns and bind-mounts it to /run/netns/<name>. Unlinking requires umount first. So `UnlinkNamedNetNS` returns EBUSY error, and both call sites (`_ = UnlinkNamedNetNS(parkPath)` in migration.go lines 79, 178) ignore the error → the parking netns remains on disk forever (leak in /run/netns). Hmm wait — but do the regular park/restore paths also use CreateOrGetNamedNetNS and rely on deleting it? Let me check how the pre-existing park machinery cleans up the parking netns. Let me grep for ParkingNetnsName usage and UnlinkNamedNetNS usage across the repo.

Also check: after LinkSetNsFd moves the interface out of the parking ns, the netns has no interfaces, but the ns is still mounted. `os.Remove` on a bind mount → EBUSY. Unless... Actually, let me think: os.Remove calls unlinkat. For a mount point, unlink returns EBUSY. Yes.

But wait — maybe the existing parking machinery deletes the netns elsewhere with proper umount? Let me grep.

70: func (p *applyPlan) empty() bool {
71: 	return len(p.addedNodeSet) == 0 &&
72: 		len(p.deletedNodeSet) == 0 &&
73: 		len(p.recreatedNodeSet) == 0 &&
74: 		len(p.startNodeSet) == 0 &&
75: 		len(p.restartNodeSet) == 0 &&
76: 		len(p.linkRestartNodeSet) == 0 &&
77: 		len(p.addedLinks) == 0 &&
78: 		len(p.staleEndpoints) == 0

81: func newApplyPlan(currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup, state *LabState) *applyPlan {
82: 	return &applyPlan{
83: 		currentNodes:       currentNodes,
84: 		addedNodeSet:       map[string]struct{}{},
85: 		deletedNodeSet:     map[string]struct{}{},
86: 		recreatedNodeSet:   map[string]struct{}{},
87: 		parkedNodeSet:      map[string]struct{}{},
88: 		startNodeSet:       map[string]struct{}{},
89: 		restartNodeSet:     map[string]struct{}{},
90: 		linkRestartNodeSet: map[string]struct{}{},
91: 		nodeDiffs:          map[string]*clabtypes.TopologyDiff{},
92: 		plannedLinkSet:     map[int]struct{}{},
93: 		desiredEndpointSet: map[applyEndpointKey]struct{}{},
94: 		liveEndpointSet:    map[applyEndpointKey]struct{}{},
95: 		liveEndpointInfo:   map[applyEndpointKey]clablinks.OwnedInterface{},
96: 		endpointNodes:      map[string]clablinks.Node{},
97: 		state:              state,
98: 		nodeChangeReasons:  map[string]string{},
99: 	}
100: }

102: func (p *applyPlan) isExternallyManaged(nodeName string) bool {
103: 	if p == nil {
104: 		return false
105: 	}
106: 	node := p.currentNodes[nodeName]
107: 	return node != nil && node.external
108: }
109: 
110: func (p *applyPlan) isRootNamespaceNode(nodeName string) bool {
111: 	if p == nil {
112: 		return false
113: 	}
114: 	node := p.currentNodes[nodeName]
115: 	return node != nil && node.rootNamespaceBased
116: }
117: 
118: func (p *applyPlan) isNonContainerNode(nodeName string) bool {
119: 	return p.isExternallyManaged(nodeName) || p.isRootNamespaceNode(nodeName)
120: }
121: 
122: // isNewNonContainerNode reports whether a non-container node (bridge, host,
123: // ext-container) is absent from the previously deployed topology. Such nodes
124: // exist outside the lab, so they are always listed as current nodes, even
125: // when the topology has just added them.
126: func (p *applyPlan) isNewNonContainerNode(nodeName string) bool {
127: 	if !p.isNonContainerNode(nodeName) || p.state == nil || p.state.Topology == nil {
128: 		return false
129: 	}
130: 	_, exists := p.state.Topology.Nodes[nodeName]
131: 	return !exists
132: }
133: 
134: // networkModeContainerTarget returns the referenced node name for a
135: // "network-mode: container:<name>" config, or "" if networkMode does not
136: // share another container's network namespace.
137: func networkModeContainerTarget(networkMode string) string {
138: 	if target, shared := strings.CutPrefix(networkMode, "container:"); shared {
139: 		return target
140: 	}
141: 	return ""
142: }
143: 
144: // checkApplyNetworkModeTargets rejects apply when a node's network-mode:
145: // container:<target> target is being removed from the topology while the
146: // dependent node stays desired. Deleting the target would leave the
147: // dependent silently attached to a defunct network namespace.
148: func (c *CLab) checkApplyNetworkModeTargets(plan *applyPlan) error {
149: 	if plan == nil {
150: 		return nil
151: 	}
152: 
153: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
154: 		networkMode := c.Nodes[nodeName].Config().NetworkMode
155: 		target := networkModeContainerTarget(networkMode)
156: 		if target == "" {
157: 			continue
158: 		}
159: 		if _, deleted := plan.deletedNodeSet[target]; deleted {
160: 			return fmt.Errorf(
161: 				"node %q has network-mode %q, but %q is being removed from the topology; "+
162: 					"remove or retarget %q as well",
163: 				nodeName,
164: 				networkMode,
165: 				target,
166: 				nodeName,
167: 			)
168: 		}
169: 	}
170: 
171: 	return nil
172: }
173: 
174: // planNetworkModeCascade forces recreation of nodes whose network-mode:
175: // container:<target> target is itself being recreated. Docker binds
176: // NetworkMode to the target container's ID at creation time, so a plain
177: // restart of the dependent cannot rebind it to the target's new container;
178: // only recreating the dependent does. A reverse dependency graph visits each
179: // node and dependency at most once, including long namespace-sharing chains.
180: func (c *CLab) planNetworkModeCascade(plan *applyPlan) {
181: 	if plan == nil || len(plan.recreatedNodeSet) == 0 {
182: 		return
183: 	}
184: 
185: 	dependents := make(map[string][]string)
186: 	for name, node := range c.Nodes {
187: 		if target := networkModeContainerTarget(node.Config().NetworkMode); target != "" {
188: 			dependents[target] = append(dependents[target], name)
189: 		}
190: 	}
191: 	queue := make([]string, 0, len(c.Nodes))
192: 	for name := range plan.recreatedNodeSet {
193: 		queue = append(queue, name)
194: 	}
195: 	for i := 0; i < len(queue); i++ {
196: 		target := queue[i]
197: 		for _, nodeName := range dependents[target] {
198: 			if _, recreated := plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName]; recreated {
199: 				continue
200: 			}
201: 			if _, added := plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; added {
202: 				continue
203: 			}
204: 
205: 			plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
206: 			delete(plan.restartNodeSet, nodeName)
207: 			delete(plan.linkRestartNodeSet, nodeName)
208: 			plan.nodeChangeReasons[nodeName] = fmt.Sprintf(
209: 				"network-mode target %q recreated", target,
210: 			)
211: 			queue = append(queue, nodeName)
212: 		}
213: 	}
214: }

216: func (c *CLab) planApply(
217: 	ctx context.Context,
218: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
219: ) (*applyPlan, error) {
220: 	state, err := c.LoadState()
221: 	if err != nil {
222: 		log.Warn("Failed to load state file", "error", err)
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	plan := newApplyPlan(currentNodes, state)
226: 
227: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
228: 		if _, exists := currentNodes[nodeName]; !exists {
229: 			status := c.Nodes[nodeName].GetContainerStatus(ctx)
230: 			if status != clabruntime.NotFound {
231: 				return nil, fmt.Errorf(
232: 					"node %q container %q already exists outside the runtime lab state",
233: 					nodeName,
234: 					c.Nodes[nodeName].Config().LongName,
235: 				)
236: 			}
237: 
238: 			plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
239: 			continue
240: 		}
241: 
242: 		if plan.isNewNonContainerNode(nodeName) {
243: 			plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
244: 		}
245: 	}
246: 
247: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedRuntimeNodeGroupNames(currentNodes) {
248: 		if _, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]; !exists {
249: 			plan.deletedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
250: 		}
251: 	}
252: 
253: 	if err := c.checkApplyNetworkModeTargets(plan); err != nil {
254: 		return nil, err
255: 	}
256: 
257: 	if err := c.planNodeReconciliation(ctx, plan); err != nil {
258: 		return nil, err
259: 	}
260: 
261: 	c.planParkedNodes(ctx, plan)
262: 	c.planStoppedNodes(ctx, plan)
263: 
264: 	for _, linkIdx := range sortedLinkIndexes(c.Links) {
265: 		for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(c.Links[linkIdx]) {
266: 			plan.desiredEndpointSet[endpointKeyFromEndpoint(ep)] = struct{}{}
267: 		}
268: 	}
269: 
270: 	if err := c.discoverLiveApplyEndpoints(ctx, plan); err != nil {
271: 		return nil, err
272: 	}
273: 
274: 	if err := c.validateDesiredEndpointOwnership(ctx, plan); err != nil {
275: 		return nil, err
276: 	}
277: 
278: 	c.planDeletedEndpoints(ctx, plan)
279: 
280: 	for _, linkIdx := range sortedLinkIndexes(c.Links) {
281: 		link := c.Links[linkIdx]
282: 		if !plan.linkNeedsDeploy(link) {
283: 			continue
284: 		}
285: 
286: 		plan.addDeployApplyLink(linkIdx, link)
287: 
288: 		for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
289: 			nodeName := ep.GetNode().GetShortName()
290: 			if _, exists := currentNodes[nodeName]; !exists {
291: 				continue
292: 			}
293: 			if _, added := plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; added {
294: 				continue
295: 			}
296: 
297: 			c.planAffectedApplyNode(ctx, plan, nodeName, "added link")
298: 		}
299: 	}
300: 
301: 	// Link reconciliation can request additional recreations. Propagate namespace
302: 	// dependencies only after those decisions, then park every affected live node.
303: 	c.planNetworkModeCascade(plan)
304: 	c.planTailscaleSidecarRecreates(plan)
305: 	c.planParkedNodes(ctx, plan)
306: 	c.planRecreatedNodeLinks(plan)
307: 	for nodeName := range plan.recreatedNodeSet {
308: 		delete(plan.restartNodeSet, nodeName)
309: 		delete(plan.linkRestartNodeSet, nodeName)
310: 		delete(plan.startNodeSet, nodeName)
311: 	}
312: 	if err := c.planNetworkModeRestarts(plan); err != nil {
313: 		return nil, err
314: 	}
315: 
316: 	return plan, nil
317: }

416: 	plannedEndpointSet := map[applyEndpointKey]struct{}{}
417: 
418: 	for _, key := range sortedEndpointKeys(plan.liveEndpointSet) {

428: // planBridgeNSMigrations finds stale BridgeNS bridge-side endpoints that the
429: // desired topology re-claims under a different in-container bridge node (the
430: // bridge moved to another parent). Such veth ends are migrated (parked and
431: // restored into the new parent's namespace) instead of deleted, which keeps
432: // the pairwise integrity of the link and the client-side configuration.
433: //
434: // Detection runs on two sources: live-discovered stale endpoints (existing
435: // bridge nodes) and the stored old topology (deleted bridge nodes, whose
436: // ports are not discovered live).
437: func (c *CLab) planBridgeNSMigrations(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) {
438: 	if plan == nil {
439: 		return
440: 	}
441: 
442: 	// Live-discovered stale bridge-side ends (the bridge node still exists).
443: 	for _, ref := range plan.staleEndpoints {
444: 		if ref.node == nil ||
445: 			ref.node.GetLinkEndpointType() != clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS {
446: 			continue
447: 		}
448: 		c.addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate(plan, ref.key, ref.node)
449: 	}
450: 
451: 	// Deleted in-container bridge nodes are absent from the desired topology,
452: 	// so their ports are not discovered live; recover them from the old state.
453: 	if plan.state != nil && plan.state.Topology != nil {
454: 		for _, link := range plan.state.Topology.Links {
455: 			if link == nil || link.Link == nil {
456: 				continue
457: 			}
458: 
459: 			var bridgeEndpointPoint *[2]string
460: 			for _, point := range clablinks.RawLinkEndpoints(link.Link) {
461: 				if strings.Contains(point[0], "|") {
462: 					bridgePoint := point
463: 					bridgeEndpointPoint = &bridgePoint
464: 				}
465: 			}
466: 			if bridgeEndpointPoint == nil {
467: 				continue
468: 			}
469: 
470: 			c.addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate(
471: 				plan,
472: 				applyEndpointKey{node: bridgeEndpointPoint[0], iface: bridgeEndpointPoint[1]},
473: 				nil,
474: 			)
475: 		}
476: 	}
477: }

479: // addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate registers a bridge NS migration when the
480: // desired topology re-claims the given bridge-side endpoint under a different
481: // in-container bridge node with the same logical port name.
482: func (c *CLab) addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate(
483: 	plan *applyPlan,
484: 	staleKey applyEndpointKey,
485: 	staleNode clablinks.Node,
486: ) {
487: 	if staleKey.node == "" || staleKey.iface == "" {
488: 		return
489: 	}
490: 	if _, desired := plan.desiredEndpointSet[staleKey]; desired {
491: 		return
492: 	}
493: 	if c.isBridgeNSMigrationPlanned(plan, staleKey) {
494: 		return
495: 	}
496: 
497: 	for candidate := range plan.desiredEndpointSet {
498: 		if candidate.iface != staleKey.iface || candidate.node == staleKey.node {
499: 			continue
500: 		}
501: 		if !c.isBridgeNSNode(candidate.node) {
502: 			continue
503: 		}
504: 
505: 		plan.bridgeNSMigrations = append(plan.bridgeNSMigrations, bridgeNSMigration{
506: 			staleRef: applyEndpointRef{key: staleKey, node: staleNode},
507: 			newKey:   candidate,
508: 		})
509: 		log.Info(
510: 			"Planning bridge port migration",
511: 			"from",
512: 			staleKey.String(),
513: 			"to",
514: 			candidate.String(),
515: 		)
516: 		return
517: 	}
518: }

522: func (c *CLab) isBridgeNSMigrationPlanned(
523: 	plan *applyPlan,
524: 	key applyEndpointKey,
525: ) bool {

527: 		if mig.staleRef.key == key {
528: 			return true
529: 		}
530: 	}
531: 	return false
532: }

539: 		return false
540: 	}

542: 		node.Config().Kind == "bridge" && strings.Contains(nodeName, "|")
543: }

575: 		}
576: 	}

710: // bridgeNSParentNode resolves the parent container node whose network namespace
711: // hosts the given BridgeNS bridge node. Shared by discovery, validation and

713: func (c *CLab) bridgeNSParentNode(bridgeName string) (clablinks.Node, error) {
714: 	node, exists := c.Nodes[bridgeName]
715: 	if !exists {
716: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("in-container bridge %q not found in topology", bridgeName)
717: 	}
718: 	parentName := networkModeContainerTarget(node.Config().NetworkMode)
719: 	if parentName == "" {
720: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
721: 			"in-container bridge %q has invalid network-mode: %s",
722: 			bridgeName,
723: 			node.Config().NetworkMode,
724: 		)
725: 	}
726: 	parentNode, exists := c.Nodes[parentName]
727: 	if !exists {
728: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
729: 			"in-container bridge %q: parent container %q not found",
730: 			bridgeName,
731: 			parentName,
732: 		)
733: 	}
734: 	return parentNode, nil

737: // bridgeNSNameInNamespace strips the "<bridge>|<node>" suffix, yielding the
738: // kernel bridge interface name inside the parent container namespace.
739: func bridgeNSNameInNamespace(bridgeName string) string {
740: 	if idx := strings.Index(bridgeName, "|"); idx != -1 {
741: 		return bridgeName[:idx]

743: 	return bridgeName

773: 		return err

776: 	for name, iface := range matched {

782: 	for _, iface := range orphans {
783: 		key := applyEndpointKey{node: bridgeName, iface: iface.Name}
784: 		plan.liveEndpointSet[key] = struct{}{}
785: 		plan.liveEndpointInfo[key] = iface

788: 	return nil
789: }

1150: func (p *applyPlan) linkIntact(link clablinks.Link) bool {

1152: 	if len(endpoints) != 2 || len(p.liveEndpointInfo) == 0 {
1153: 		return true

1156: 	left, leftOK := p.liveEndpointInfo[endpointKeyFromEndpoint(endpoints[0])]
1157: 	right, rightOK := p.liveEndpointInfo[endpointKeyFromEndpoint(endpoints[1])]
1158: 	if !leftOK || !rightOK {
1159: 		return false
1160: 	}
1161: 
1162: 	if bridgeMasterMismatch(endpoints[0], left) || bridgeMasterMismatch(endpoints[1], right) {
1163: 		return false
1164: 	}
1165: 
1166: 	return left.PeerIndex != 0 &&
1167: 		right.PeerIndex != 0 &&
1168: 		left.PeerIndex == right.Index &&

1175: // management network bridge is not resolved are not checked.

1183: 			return false
1184: 		}
1185: 		return live.MasterName != node.GetShortName()
1186: 	}
1187: 
1188: 	// Handle in-container bridge (BridgeNS) endpoints
1189: 	if endpointType == clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS {
1190: 		// For BridgeNS, the bridge name in the container is the node name without the namespace
1191: 		// suffix
1192: 		bridgeName := node.GetShortName()
1193: 		if idx := strings.Index(bridgeName, "|"); idx != -1 {
1194: 			bridgeName = bridgeName[:idx]
1195: 		}
1196: 		return live.MasterName != bridgeName
1197: 	}
1198: 
1199: 	return false

171: func (l *LinkVEth) deployAEnd(ctx context.Context, idx int) error {
172: 	ep := l.Endpoints[idx]
173: 	// the peer Endpoint is the other of the two endpoints in the
174: 	// Endpoints slice. So do a +1 on the index and modulo operation
175: 	// to take care of the wrap around.
176: 	peerIdx := (idx + 1) % 2
177: 	peerEp := l.Endpoints[peerIdx]
178: 
179: 	log.Debugf("Creating Endpoint: %s ( --> %s )", ep, peerEp)
180: 
181: 	// build the netlink.Veth struct for the link provisioning
182: 	linkA := &netlink.Veth{
183: 		LinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{
184: 			Name: ep.GetRandIfaceName(),
185: 			MTU:  l.MTU,
186: 			// Mac address is set later on
187: 		},
188: 		PeerName: peerEp.GetRandIfaceName(),
189: 		// PeerMac address is set later on
190: 	}
191: 
192: 	// add the link
193: 	err := netlink.LinkAdd(linkA)
194: 	if err != nil {
195: 		return err
196: 	}
197: 
198: 	// cleanup is a helper that removes the veth pair if a subsequent step fails
199: 	// after LinkAdd succeeded, preventing orphaned interfaces from blocking retries.
200: 	cleanup := func(err error) error {
201: 		if delErr := netlink.LinkDel(linkA); delErr != nil {
202: 			log.Debugf(
203: 				"failed to cleanup veth pair %s after error: %v",
204: 				ep.GetRandIfaceName(),
205: 				delErr,
206: 			)
207: 		}
208: 		return err
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	// disable TXOffloading
212: 	if err := clabutils.EthtoolTXOff(ep.GetRandIfaceName()); err != nil {
213: 		return cleanup(err)
214: 	}
215: 
216: 	// the link needs to be moved to the relevant network namespace
217: 	// and enabled (up). This is done via linkSetupFunc.
218: 	// based on the endpoint type the link setup function is different.
219: 	// linkSetupFunc is executed in a netns of a node.
220: 	// if the node is a regular namespace node
221: 	// add link to node, rename, set mac and Up
222: 	err = ep.GetNode().AddLinkToContainer(ctx, linkA,
223: 		SetNameMACAndUpInterface(linkA, ep))
224: 	if err != nil {
225: 		return cleanup(err)
226: 	}
227: 
228: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateHalfDeployed
229: 
230: 	// e.g. host endpoints are nodeless, and therefore the B end of the veth link should
231: 	// be deployed right after the A end is deployed.
232: 	if peerEp.IsNodeless() {
233: 		return l.deployBEnd(ctx, peerIdx)
234: 	}
235: 
236: 	return nil
237: }

Reasoning
Confirmed: the existing park machinery uses `netns.DeleteNamed(...)` (which does umount + unlink properly), while the NEW `UnlinkNamedNetNS` (utils/netlink.go:234-240) uses `os.Remove` — which fails with EBUSY on a bind-mounted named netns created by `netns.NewNamed`. So the migration's parking netns is created via `CreateOrGetNamedNetNS` (bind mount) and "cleaned" via `UnlinkNamedNetNS` → EBUSY → ignored (`_ =`) → the netns leaks permanently in `/run/netns/` on every bridge migration, holding a reference to a network namespace. Also, `GetNamedNetNS`/`FileOrDirExists` would then find it next time and reuse it (mild), but the leak accumulates: each migration with a distinct longName (e.g., lab recreate with different names) leaves a mount. Also leaked netns mounts keep kernel resources alive.

Wait — one nuance: could the migration reuse an existing parking netns name that also belongs to a node's regular parking? `ParkingNetnsName(longName)` where longName = the NEW BRIDGE node's LongName. Bridge nodes have no container, so their parking ns name is unique to the bridge. But the restore path in the normal machinery: for the bridge node itself, ParkEndpoints is a noop. So `clab-park-<bridgeLongName>` is only created by the migration → leaked every time.

Fix: use `netns.DeleteNamed` (like `cleanupParkingNetNS`) instead of `os.Remove`, or better: extend `UnlinkNamedNetNS` to umount+unlink. This is a P2 (resource leak on every migration; persistent mount in /run/netns keeps a dead netns alive; also may cause `GetNamedNetNS` reuse confusion). Actually let me double-check that `netns.NewNamed` really bind-mounts. From vishvananda/netns source (netns.go):

```go
// NewNamed creates a new named network namespace and returns a handle to it
func NewNamed(name string) (NetNS, error) {
	if err := createNamedNetNS(name); err != nil { ... }
	...
}
```

Actually the real implementation:

```go
func NewNamed(name string) (NetNS, error) {
	if name == "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("ns name required")
	}
	ns, err := New()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer ns.Close()

	nsPath := filepath.Join(defaultNetNSPath, name)
	if err = mount(netnsPath, nsPath); err != nil { ... }
```

Yes — it bind-mounts `/proc/self/ns/net` (netnsPath) onto `/run/netns/<name>`. So the path is a mount point. `os.Remove` on a mount point → EBUSY. Confirmed. Note the failure is silently ignored (`_ =`), which is exactly the "silently leak" pattern. P2.

Also `createNamedNetNS`... fine.

Next: check `planParkedNodes` (lines 328-345) and the BridgeNS handling there, then the restore flow, then look at nodes/node.go WireNodesMapToNodes and core/config.go, then links/link_veth.go endpointBridgeNS deployment (deployBEnd for bridge ns?), then check `Endpoint` types for BridgeNS endpoints — how is `GetRandIfaceName` etc. handled for bridge endpoints. Also check `deployLinks` to see how bridge endpoints are deployed and whether removeApplyLinkEndpoints with RemoveInterface... Actually I read removeApplyLinkEndpoints in core/apply.go already: for BridgeNS endpoints it calls bridgeNSParentNode + RemoveInterface — note: RemoveInterface(parentNode, ifaceName) — it removes by kernel name SanitizeInterfaceName(ifaceName). For a planned new link (not migrated), removing the bridge endpoint before deploy. OK.

But wait — there's a subtle issue in removeApplyLinkEndpoints: it's called with plan.addedLinks AFTER restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts filtered migrated links. But if the migration restore FAILED to enslave... errors propagate. Fine.

Another important check: `removeApplyLinkEndpoints` for a BridgeNS endpoint calls `c.bridgeNSParentNode(node.GetShortName())`. Fine.

Now — the bridge-side endpoint in deployLinks: let me read the BridgeNS endpoint deploy logic in links (endpoint_bridge_ns.go?) and the link_veth deployBEnd to see how the veth gets into the parent ns and the altname labeling. Let me grep for endpoint types with BridgeNS.

If the new parent (bp2) is being recreated in the same apply (move + drift on bp2), the bridge node br01|bp2 is ADDED (not recreated — cascade only applies to nodes in c.Nodes... wait, planNetworkModeCascade iterates c.Nodes dependents: br01|bp2's target is bp2; if bp2 ∈ recreatedNodeSet → br01|bp2 gets recreatedNodeSet. But br01|bp2 was in addedNodeSet → cascade skips added nodes (line 201-203). Good — added nodes stay added, deployed by deployApplyNodes after bp2. Order: deployApplyNodes (223) — deploys in what order? deployNodeNames sorted alphabetically: bp1... bp2, br01|bp2 — alphabetical: "bp2" < "br01|bp2"? "bp2" vs "br01|bp2": 'p' (0x70) vs 'r' (0x72) → bp2 first. Lucky. But is there a guarantee that the parent deploys before the bridge? deployApplyNodes — need to check if it's concurrent with maxWorkers (options.maxWorkers). If workers > 1, br01|bp2's Deploy may run before bp2's Deploy completes → waitForParentContainer polls GetContainerStatus until joinable — it waits, good. But SetNodesMap wiring: dp.Nodes includes all nodes regardless of deployment state. waitForParentContainer waits for the parent container to be running. OK — handled.

  - **P2 (defect):** `bridgeNSMigParentNode` (core/apply_bridge_migration.go:17-34) fails when the old bridge's parent was also removed from topology: fallback looks up `c.Nodes[parts[1]]`, absent → apply aborts mid-way (after `deleteApplyEndpoints`) with confusing error; re-running hits same failure. Fix: skip planning migration when old parent ∈ `plan.deletedNodeSet` (normal delete/recreate path handles it).
  - **P2 (defect):** `addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate` (core/topology_reconcile.go:482+) matches candidates purely by same bridge-side iface name under a different bridge node, never verifying the client-side peer matches. Scenario: old link `c1:eth1–br01|bp1:c1eth1`, new link `c2:eth1–br02|bp1:c1eth1` → migration planned; if c1 node removed from topology (c1:eth1 not discovered/deleted at endpoint stage), parking succeeds but peer is destroyed when c1 container is deleted → one-ended zombie veth enslaved to br02, and the new link is filtered from `addedLinks` so `c2:eth1` is NEVER created — silent broken wiring, no error.
  - **P2 (leak):** `UnlinkNamedNetNS` (utils/netlink.go:234-240) uses `os.Remove`, but `netns.NewNamed` (called by `CreateOrGetNamedNetNS`) bind-mounts `/run/netns/<name>` → `os.Remove` returns EBUSY → error silently ignored (`_ =` at links/migration.go:79 and :178) → parking netns (`clab-park-<bridgeLongName>`) leaks permanently on every migration. Existing machinery uses `netns.DeleteNamed` (nodes/default_node.go:464-469, nodes/sros/netns.go:74-80) which umounts properly — fix is to use `netns.DeleteNamed`/umount+unlink.
  - **Dead code / misleading comment:** `LinkVEth.SetDeploymentState` (links/link_veth.go:156-159) and `LinkDeploymentStateSetter` (links/apply.go:82-84) have NO callers anywhere in head. Comment in `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` claiming "The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed" is inaccurate — the code only filters the link from `plan.addedLinks` (which is the actual working mechanism).
  - **Panic-risk candidates (must check base for pre-existing):** `enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace` type-asserts `bridgeLink.(*netlink.Bridge)` (nodes/bridge/bridge.go ~308) — panics if a non-bridge link with same name exists; `CheckDeploymentConditions` (bridge.go ~356-360) does `b.Cfg.NetworkMode[10:] != b.GetShortName()[len(nameWithoutSeparatorSuffix())+1:]` — panics (slice out of range) if shortname has no `|` and NetworkMode has `container:` prefix.
  - Verified-safe items: `deleteApplyEndpoints` `ref.node.GetLinkEndpointType()` deref is safe (`addStaleApplyEndpoint` returns early if node not in `c.Nodes`); cross-netns `linkIntact` PeerIndex comparison is exact (veth ifindex preserved across ns moves); bridge `br01|bp2` in move case lands in `addedNodeSet` via `isNewNonContainerNode` (not an "already exists" error, thanks to new `rootNamespaceBased` branch in `core/runtime_state.go`); orphan kernel-name discovery → stale → migration works; `checkApplyNetworkModeTargets` guards deleted network-mode targets; `planParkedNodes` only iterates `recreatedNodeSet` (core/topology_reconcile.go:328-345); derived host stale endpoints for BridgeNS are best-effort noise (pre-existing mechanism, harmless).
  - Wiring: `SetNodesMap`/`WireNodesMapToNodes` called at core/config.go:182 and :294; bridge.go:81 implements `NamespaceSharerNodesSetter`.
  - `LinkApplyMode` defaults: linux kind → `LinkApplyModeLive` (nodes/linux/linux.go:43), so client nodes are not restarted on migrated links.

119: 		); err != nil {

126: 		// so endpoint removal and pair re-creation never touch it.

133: 			) {

139: 					mig.newKey.iface,
140: 				)
