1: package links
2: 
3: import (
4: 	"context"
5: 	"fmt"
6: 	"strings"
7: 
8: 	"github.com/charmbracelet/log"
9: 	"github.com/containernetworking/plugins/pkg/ns"
10: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
11: 	"github.com/vishvananda/netlink"
12: )
13: 
14: // NSMigrationNode is the minimal node surface the bridge-port migration
15: // works with: exec context plus a resolvable namespace path.
16: type NSMigrationNode interface {
17: 	ExecFunction(ctx context.Context, f func(ns.NetNS) error) error
18: 	GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
19: 	GetShortName() string
20: }
21: 
22: // BridgePortRelocation describes a bridge-side veth end parked out of one
23: // namespace while the in-container bridge hosting it was replaced (a bridge
24: // parent move). The veth pair stays intact across the namespace hops: the
25: // client-side end keeps its address and MAC, and the parked half carries its
26: // device state until it is restored into the replacement namespace.
27: type BridgePortRelocation struct {
28: 	parkNSPath   string
29: 	KernelName   string // kernel-side name while parked
30: 	OldOwnerName string
31: 	IfaceName    string
32: 	LongName     string // replacement bridge node's long name; exercises the parking netns name
33: }
34: 
35: // ParkBridgePortByOwnership finds the interface carrying the ownership altname
36: // of (ownerName, ifaceName) in src's namespace and parks it into the parking
37: // netns of longName. The pair survives: only the parked half is relocated.
38: func ParkBridgePortByOwnership(
39: 	ctx context.Context,
40: 	src Node,
41: 	ownerName string,
42: 	ifaceName string,
43: 	longName string,
44: ) (*BridgePortRelocation, error) {
45: 	parkPath, err := clabutils.CreateOrGetNamedNetNS(clabutils.ParkingNetnsName(longName))
46: 	if err != nil {
47: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create parking netns for migration: %w", err)
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	relocation := &BridgePortRelocation{
51: 		parkNSPath:   parkPath,
52: 		OldOwnerName: ownerName,
53: 		IfaceName:    ifaceName,
54: 		LongName:     longName,
55: 	}
56: 
57: 	parkErr := src.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
58: 		link, err := findLinkByOwnershipAltName(ownerName, ifaceName)
59: 		if err != nil {
60: 			return err
61: 		}
62: 
63: 		relocation.KernelName = link.Attrs().Name
64: 
65: 		if err := netlink.LinkSetDown(link); err != nil {
66: 			log.Debug("failed to bring down interface while parking",
67: 				"iface", link.Attrs().Name, "err", err)
68: 		}
69: 
70: 		parkNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(parkPath)
71: 		if nsErr != nil {
72: 			return nsErr
73: 		}
74: 		defer parkNs.Close()
75: 
76: 		return netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(parkNs.Fd()))
77: 	})
78: 	if parkErr != nil {
79: 		_ = clabutils.UnlinkNamedNetNS(parkPath)
80: 		return nil, parkErr
81: 	}
82: 
83: 	return relocation, nil
84: }
85: 
86: // RestoreBridgePort moves the parked half into the replacement bridge's
87: // namespace, keeps/renames it to the desired kernel name, relabels the
88: // ownership altname to (newOwnerName, ifaceName) and re-enslaves it to the
89: // bridge. dst receives a node with both ExecFunction and GetNSPath.
90: func (r *BridgePortRelocation) RestoreBridgePort(
91: 	ctx context.Context,
92: 	dst NSMigrationNode,
93: 	newOwnerName string,
94: 	bridgeName string,
95: 	desiredKernelName string,
96: ) error {
97: 	parkExecErr := r.execInParkingNS(func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
98: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.KernelName)
99: 		if err != nil {
100: 			return fmt.Errorf("parked interface %q not found in parking ns: %w", r.KernelName, err)
101: 		}
102: 
103: 		dstPath, nsErr := dst.GetNSPath(ctx)
104: 		if nsErr != nil {
105: 			return nsErr
106: 		}
107: 		dstNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(dstPath)
108: 		if nsErr != nil {
109: 			return nsErr
110: 		}
111: 		defer dstNs.Close()
112: 
113: 		return netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(dstNs.Fd()))
114: 	})
115: 	if parkExecErr != nil {
116: 		return parkExecErr
117: 	}
118: 
119: 	dstErr := dst.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
120: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.KernelName)
121: 		if err != nil {
122: 			return fmt.Errorf("restored interface %q not found in destination ns: %w",
123: 				r.KernelName, err)
124: 		}
125: 
126: 		if desiredKernelName != "" && link.Attrs().Name != desiredKernelName {
127: 			if err := netlink.LinkSetName(link, desiredKernelName); err != nil {
128: 				return err
129: 			}
130: 			link.Attrs().Name = desiredKernelName
131: 		}
132: 
133: 		// Strip previous ownership markers and label with the new owner.
134: 		for _, altName := range link.Attrs().AltNames {
135: 			if !strings.HasPrefix(altName, ownershipAltNamePrefix) {
136: 				continue
137: 			}
138: 			if delErr := netlink.LinkDelAltName(link, altName); delErr != nil &&
139: 				!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(delErr) {
140: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to drop old ownership altname %q: %w", altName, delErr)
141: 			}
142: 		}
143: 		if addErr := linkAddAltName(
144: 			link,
145: 			ownershipAltNameFor(newOwnerName, r.IfaceName),
146: 		); addErr != nil &&
147: 			!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(addErr) {
148: 			return addErr
149: 		}
150: 
151: 		// Re-enslave to the replacement bridge, if present.
152: 		if bridgeName != "" {
153: 			if bridgeLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName); err == nil {
154: 				if link.Attrs().MasterIndex != bridgeLink.Attrs().Index {
155: 					if err := netlink.LinkSetMaster(link, bridgeLink); err != nil {
156: 						return fmt.Errorf("failed to enslave %q to %q: %w",
157: 							link.Attrs().Name, bridgeName, err)
158: 					}
159: 					log.Info("Re-enslaved migrated bridge port to replacement bridge",
160: 						"port", link.Attrs().Name, "bridge", bridgeName)
161: 				}
162: 			}
163: 		}
164: 
165: 		if link.Attrs().OperState != netlink.OperUp {
166: 			if upErr := netlink.LinkSetUp(link); upErr != nil {
167: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to bring up %q: %w", link.Attrs().Name, upErr)
168: 			}
169: 		}
170: 
171: 		return nil
172: 	})
173: 	if dstErr != nil {
174: 		return dstErr
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	// Clean up the now empty parking namespace.
178: 	_ = clabutils.UnlinkNamedNetNS(r.parkNSPath)
179: 
180: 	return nil
181: }
182: 
183: func (r *BridgePortRelocation) execInParkingNS(f func(ns.NetNS) error) error {
184: 	parkNs, err := ns.GetNS(r.parkNSPath)
185: 	if err != nil {
186: 		return err
187: 	}
188: 	defer parkNs.Close()
189: 
190: 	return parkNs.Do(f)
191: }
192: 
193: // RelabelOwnershipAltNameFor rewrites the ownership altname of the interface
194: // identified by (oldOwner, ifaceName) to (newOwner, ifaceName) inside node's
195: // namespace.
196: func RelabelOwnershipAltNameFor(
197: 	ctx context.Context,
198: 	node Node,
199: 	oldOwnerName string,
200: 	ifaceName string,
201: 	newOwnerName string,
202: ) error {
203: 	if newOwnerName == oldOwnerName {
204: 		return nil
205: 	}
206: 
207: 	return node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
208: 		link, err := findLinkByOwnershipAltName(oldOwnerName, ifaceName)
209: 		if err != nil {
210: 			// Fall back to the sanitized kernel name: short names kept their
211: 			// kernel name during relocation.
212: 			link, err = netlink.LinkByName(clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(ifaceName))
213: 			if err != nil {
214: 				return fmt.Errorf(
215: 					"interface to relabel ownership for %q (old owner %q) not found: %w",
216: 					ifaceName,
217: 					oldOwnerName,
218: 					err,
219: 				)
220: 			}
221: 		}
222: 
223: 		// Drop all previous ownership markers; ownership is single-valued.
224: 		for _, altName := range link.Attrs().AltNames {
225: 			if !strings.HasPrefix(altName, ownershipAltNamePrefix) {
226: 				continue
227: 			}
228: 			if delErr := netlink.LinkDelAltName(link, altName); delErr != nil &&
229: 				!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(delErr) {
230: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to drop old ownership altname %q: %w", altName, delErr)
231: 			}
232: 		}
233: 
234: 		return linkAddAltName(link, ownershipAltNameFor(newOwnerName, ifaceName))
235: 	})
236: }
237: 
238: // findLinkByOwnershipAltName scans the current namespace for the link carrying
239: // the ownership altname of (nodeName, ifaceName).
240: func findLinkByOwnershipAltName(nodeName, ifaceName string) (netlink.Link, error) {
241: 	links, err := netlink.LinkList()
242: 	if err != nil {
243: 		return nil, err
244: 	}
245: 	for _, link := range links {
246: 		if HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, nodeName, ifaceName) {
247: 			return link, nil
248: 		}
249: 	}
250: 	return nil, fmt.Errorf(
251: 		"no interface carries the ownership marker of %q for %q",
252: 		nodeName,
253: 		ifaceName,
254: 	)
255: }

428: // planBridgeNSMigrations finds stale BridgeNS bridge-side endpoints that the
429: // desired topology re-claims under a different in-container bridge node (the
430: // bridge moved to another parent). Such veth ends are migrated (parked and
431: // restored into the new parent's namespace) instead of deleted, which keeps
432: // the pairwise integrity of the link and the client-side configuration.
433: //
434: // Detection runs on two sources: live-discovered stale endpoints (existing
435: // bridge nodes) and the stored old topology (deleted bridge nodes, whose
436: // ports are not discovered live).
437: func (c *CLab) planBridgeNSMigrations(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) {
438: 	if plan == nil {
439: 		return
440: 	}
441: 
442: 	// Live-discovered stale bridge-side ends (the bridge node still exists).
443: 	for _, ref := range plan.staleEndpoints {
444: 		if ref.node == nil ||
445: 			ref.node.GetLinkEndpointType() != clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS {
446: 			continue
447: 		}
448: 		c.addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate(plan, ref.key, ref.node)
449: 	}
450: 
451: 	// Deleted in-container bridge nodes are absent from the desired topology,
452: 	// so their ports are not discovered live; recover them from the old state.
453: 	if plan.state != nil && plan.state.Topology != nil {
454: 		for _, link := range plan.state.Topology.Links {
455: 			if link == nil || link.Link == nil {
456: 				continue
457: 			}
458: 
459: 			var bridgeEndpointPoint *[2]string
460: 			for _, point := range clablinks.RawLinkEndpoints(link.Link) {
461: 				if strings.Contains(point[0], "|") {
462: 					bridgePoint := point
463: 					bridgeEndpointPoint = &bridgePoint
464: 				}
465: 			}
466: 			if bridgeEndpointPoint == nil {
467: 				continue
468: 			}
469: 
470: 			c.addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate(
471: 				plan,
472: 				applyEndpointKey{node: bridgeEndpointPoint[0], iface: bridgeEndpointPoint[1]},
473: 				nil,
474: 			)
475: 		}
476: 	}
477: }
478: 
479: // addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate registers a bridge NS migration when the
480: // desired topology re-claims the given bridge-side endpoint under a different
481: // in-container bridge node with the same logical port name.
482: func (c *CLab) addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate(
483: 	plan *applyPlan,
484: 	staleKey applyEndpointKey,
485: 	staleNode clablinks.Node,
486: ) {
487: 	if staleKey.node == "" || staleKey.iface == "" {
488: 		return
489: 	}
490: 	if _, desired := plan.desiredEndpointSet[staleKey]; desired {
491: 		return
492: 	}
493: 	if c.isBridgeNSMigrationPlanned(plan, staleKey) {
494: 		return
495: 	}
496: 
497: 	for candidate := range plan.desiredEndpointSet {
498: 		if candidate.iface != staleKey.iface || candidate.node == staleKey.node {
499: 			continue
500: 		}
501: 		if !c.isBridgeNSNode(candidate.node) {

503: 		}
504: 
505: 		plan.bridgeNSMigrations = append(plan.bridgeNSMigrations, bridgeNSMigration{
506: 			staleRef: applyEndpointRef{key: staleKey, node: staleNode},
507: 			newKey:   candidate,
508: 		})
509: 		log.Info(
510: 			"Planning bridge port migration",
511: 			"from",
512: 			staleKey.String(),
513: 			"to",
514: 			candidate.String(),
515: 		)
516: 		return
517: 	}
518: }

- `UnlinkNamedNetNS` uses `os.Remove` and both call sites in `links/migration.go` (79, 178) ignore the error. The named netns created via `netns.NewNamed` is a bind mount → `os.Remove` fails with EBUSY → parking netns leaks. Existing pattern `netns.DeleteNamed` (default_node.go:469, sros/netns.go:80) umounts properly. P2 leak. Also `UnlinkNamedNetNS` is only used by migration code — introduced in this PR.

- `LinkDeploymentStateSetter` (links/apply.go:79-84) and `LinkVEth.SetDeploymentState` (link_veth.go:156-159): who calls SetDeploymentState? Grep shows call sites... `SetDeploymentState(` — need to grep for callers specifically. The matches above are declarations and internal DeploymentState field sets. Let me grep for `\.SetDeploymentState\(` to find callers.

Also check the misleading comment: restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts comment says "The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed so deployLinks skips pair re-creation for it." — but the code filters the link from plan.addedLinks. Is there any other mechanism that marks a LinkVEth full-deployed? Possibly `link.linkVEth.DeploymentState` set somewhere in restoreRecreatedNodes path? The summary said dead code with no callers. Let me verify with a grep for SetDeploymentState callers.

Reasoning
The type assert at line 308: `bridgeLink.(*netlink.Bridge)`. `netlink.LinkByName` on a bridge device returns `*netlink.Bridge` (LinkByName decodes by kind) — so the assert should hold for an actual bridge. Could `LinkByName` return a non-Bridge for a name that matches? Only if another device with the same name exists — but LinkByName found `bridgeName` which is the bridge's name. If it were a veth named br01, the assert would panic. Edge: a leftover veth with the bridge's name (e.g., from a partially failed previous apply where the bridge was replaced by a migrated port? unlikely). This is a hardening nit — P4 at most. Also: was `enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace` added in this PR? Yes (new function). The assert panic risk is speculative; mention as P4 or coverage note. I'll include as P4 only if I'm confident it's actionable. A cleaner alternative: `netlink.LinkSetMaster(link, bridgeLink)` doesn't need the Index comparison via type assert — could compare `link.Attrs().MasterIndex != bridgeLink.Attrs().Index` (works on the Link interface). That's a small correction removing the panic risk entirely. P4, fine.

Also check the restore path: what happens when `bridgeLink` is not a Bridge? OK, P4.

Now, the P2 nil-deref in deleteApplyEndpoints line 1234 `ref.node.GetLinkEndpointType()` — stale refs always have non-nil node (addStaleApplyEndpoint early-returns). But wait — are there other places that append to plan.staleEndpoints with nil node? planBridgeNSMigrations only appends to bridgeNSMigrations. Let me check addDerivedHostStaleEndpoints and other addStale... Also check checkApplyNetworkModeTargets. And I should double check `plan.staleEndpoints` population sites: grep "staleEndpoints = append".

710: // bridgeNSParentNode resolves the parent container node whose network namespace
711: // hosts the given BridgeNS bridge node. Shared by discovery, validation and
712: // deletion paths touching BridgeNS endpoint lifecycles.
713: func (c *CLab) bridgeNSParentNode(bridgeName string) (clablinks.Node, error) {
714: 	node, exists := c.Nodes[bridgeName]
715: 	if !exists {
716: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("in-container bridge %q not found in topology", bridgeName)
717: 	}
718: 	parentName := networkModeContainerTarget(node.Config().NetworkMode)
719: 	if parentName == "" {
720: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
721: 			"in-container bridge %q has invalid network-mode: %s",
722: 			bridgeName,
723: 			node.Config().NetworkMode,
724: 		)
725: 	}
726: 	parentNode, exists := c.Nodes[parentName]
727: 	if !exists {
728: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
729: 			"in-container bridge %q: parent container %q not found",
730: 			bridgeName,
731: 			parentName,
732: 		)
733: 	}
734: 	return parentNode, nil
735: }

737: // bridgeNSNameInNamespace strips the "<bridge>|<node>" suffix, yielding the
738: // kernel bridge interface name inside the parent container namespace.
739: func bridgeNSNameInNamespace(bridgeName string) string {
740: 	if idx := strings.Index(bridgeName, "|"); idx != -1 {
741: 		return bridgeName[:idx]
742: 	}
743: 	return bridgeName
744: }

746: // discoverBridgeNSEndpoints discovers interfaces attached to an in-container
747: // bridge. Interfaces are discovered in the parent container's namespace and
748: // mapped to their logical endpoint names via ownership altnames, so no ordering
749: // dependency with the remote endpoints' discovery exists. Orphaned
750: // bridge-attached interfaces (owned but claimed by no desired endpoint) are
751: // keyed by their kernel names so stale-clean up can remove them.

104: 		return nil, err
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	sort.Slice(interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
108: 		return interfaces[i].Name < interfaces[j].Name
109: 	})
110: 
111: 	return interfaces, nil
112: }
113: 
114: func DiscoverOwnedInterfaceNames(
115: 	ctx context.Context,
116: 	node Node,
117: 	knownIfaceNames map[string]struct{},
118: ) ([]string, error) {
119: 	interfaces, err := DiscoverOwnedInterfaces(ctx, node, knownIfaceNames)
120: 	if err != nil {
121: 		return nil, err
122: 	}
123: 
124: 	ifaceNames := make([]string, 0, len(interfaces))
125: 	for _, iface := range interfaces {
126: 		ifaceNames = append(ifaceNames, iface.Name)
127: 	}
128: 	sort.Strings(ifaceNames)
129: 
130: 	return ifaceNames, nil
131: }
132: 
133: // DiscoverEndpointsForBridgeNS discovers interfaces attached to an in-container
134: // bridge in node's namespace and maps each to its logical endpoint name via the
135: // ownership altname marker (hash of ownerName and logical iface name). This has
136: // no dependency on discovery order of the remote endpoints.
137: // desiredNames holds the logical endpoint iface names of the topology defined on
138: // this bridge. Interfaces carrying an ownership marker for an entry of
139: // desiredNames are returned in matched; any other containerlab-owned
140: // bridge-attached interface is returned in orphans (stale candidates).
141: // matched: key = logical endpoint iface name. orphans key = kernel iface name.
142: func DiscoverEndpointsForBridgeNS(
143: 	ctx context.Context,
144: 	node Node,
145: 	ownerName string,
146: 	bridgeName string,
147: 	desiredNames map[string]struct{},
148: ) (matched map[string]OwnedInterface, orphans []OwnedInterface, err error) {
149: 	matched = make(map[string]OwnedInterface, len(desiredNames))
150: 
151: 	err = node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
152: 		// Bridge absent is fine: there is nothing attached to discover.
153: 		bridge, bridgeErr := netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName)
154: 		if bridgeErr != nil {
155: 			return nil
156: 		}
157: 		bridgeIndex := bridge.Attrs().Index
158: 
159: 		links, err := netlink.LinkList()
160: 		if err != nil {
161: 			return err
162: 		}
163: 
164: 		for _, link := range links {
165: 			name := link.Attrs().Name
166: 			if name == "lo" || name == "eth0" || name == bridgeName {
167: 				continue
168: 			}
169: 
170: 			if !hasOwnershipAltName(link) {
171: 				continue
172: 			}
173: 
174: 			// Match against the desired logical endpoint names
175: 			// recorded in this interface's ownership altname.
176: 			logical, found := matchOwnedInterface(link, ownerName, desiredNames)
177: 
178: 			info := OwnedInterface{
179: 				Name:        name,
180: 				Index:       link.Attrs().Index,
181: 				MasterIndex: link.Attrs().MasterIndex,
182: 				Type:        link.Type(),
183: 			}
184: 			if info.MasterIndex != 0 {
185: 				master, masterErr := netlink.LinkByIndex(info.MasterIndex)
186: 				if masterErr != nil {
187: 					return fmt.Errorf("failed to discover master for %q: %w", name, masterErr)
188: 				}
189: 				info.MasterName = master.Attrs().Name
190: 			}
191: 			if info.Type == "veth" {
192: 				veth, ok := link.(*netlink.Veth)
193: 				if !ok {
194: 					veth = &netlink.Veth{LinkAttrs: *link.Attrs()}
195: 				}
196: 				peerIndex, peerErr := netlink.VethPeerIndex(veth)
197: 				if peerErr != nil {
198: 					return fmt.Errorf("failed to discover veth peer for %q: %w", name, peerErr)
199: 				}
200: 				info.PeerIndex = peerIndex
201: 			}
202: 
203: 			if found {
204: 				matched[logical] = info
205: 			} else if info.MasterIndex == bridgeIndex {
206: 				// Owned, attached to this bridge, but no desired endpoint claims it:
207: 				// a stale/orphan candidate that must be visible to stale cleanup.
208: 				orphans = append(orphans, info)
209: 			}
210: 		}
211: 
212: 		return nil
213: 	})
214: 	if err != nil {
215: 		return nil, nil, err
216: 	}
217: 
218: 	sort.Slice(orphans, func(i, j int) bool {
219: 		return orphans[i].Name < orphans[j].Name
220: 	})
221: 
222: 	return matched, orphans, nil
223: }
224: 
225: // matchOwnedInterface finds which desired logical endpoint name claims this
226: // interface by comparing ownership altname hashes.
227: func matchOwnedInterface(
228: 	link netlink.Link,
229: 	ownerName string,
230: 	desiredNames map[string]struct{},
231: ) (string, bool) {
232: 	for name := range desiredNames {
233: 		if HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, ownerName, name) {
234: 			return name, true
235: 		}
236: 	}
237: 	return "", false
238: }
239: 
240: // ValidateOwnedInterface returns an error when an existing interface is not
241: // owned by the requested logical endpoint. Missing interfaces are valid.
242: func ValidateOwnedInterface(ctx context.Context, node Node, ifaceName string) error {
243: 	return ValidateOwnedInterfaceFor(ctx, node, ownershipName(node), ifaceName)
244: }
245: 
246: // ValidateOwnedInterfaceFor validates an interface in node's namespace against
247: // a possibly different logical owner. Parking nodes use this when the
248: // interface remains owned by the original node.
249: func ValidateOwnedInterfaceFor(
250: 	ctx context.Context,
251: 	node Node,
252: 	ownerName string,
253: 	ifaceName string,
254: ) error {
255: 	return node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
256: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(ifaceName)
257: 		if _, notfound := err.(netlink.LinkNotFoundError); notfound {
258: 			return nil
259: 		}
260: 		if err != nil {
261: 			return err
262: 		}
263: 		if isOwnedBy(link, node, ownerName, ifaceName) {
264: 			return nil
265: 		}
266: 		return fmt.Errorf(
267: 			"interface %q on node %q exists but is not containerlab-owned",
268: 			ifaceName,
269: 			node.GetShortName(),
270: 		)
271: 	})
272: }
273: 
274: // RemoveOwnedInterface removes an interface only when it carries the ownership
275: // marker of the given node's logical endpoint.
276: func RemoveOwnedInterface(ctx context.Context, node Node, ifaceName string) error {
277: 	return removeOwnedInterfaceStrict(ctx, node, ifaceName, true)
278: }
279: 
280: // RemoveInterface removes an interface without per-node ownership checks, only
281: // requiring a containerlab ownership marker. Needed for BridgeNS bridges, where
282: // the bridge-attached interface's ownership marker refers to the bridge endpoint
283: // owner, not to the parent container this call executes in.
284: func RemoveInterface(ctx context.Context, node Node, ifaceName string) error {
285: 	return removeOwnedInterfaceStrict(ctx, node, ifaceName, false)
286: }
287: 
288: func removeOwnedInterfaceStrict(
289: 	ctx context.Context,
290: 	node Node,
291: 	ifaceName string,
292: 	requireNodeOwnership bool,
293: ) error {
294: 	if node == nil || ifaceName == "" {
295: 		return nil
296: 	}
297: 
298: 	return node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
299: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(ifaceName))
300: 		if _, notfound := err.(netlink.LinkNotFoundError); notfound {
301: 			return removeBridgePort(node, ifaceName)
302: 		}
303: 		if err != nil {
304: 			return err
305: 		}
306: 
307: 		if requireNodeOwnership && !isOwnedBy(link, node, ownershipName(node), ifaceName) {
308: 			return fmt.Errorf(
309: 				"%w: interface %q on node %q",
310: 				ErrInterfaceUnowned,
311: 				ifaceName,
312: 				node.GetShortName(),
313: 			)
314: 		}
315: 		if !requireNodeOwnership && !hasOwnershipAltName(link) {
316: 			return fmt.Errorf(
317: 				"%w: interface %q on node %q is not containerlab-owned",
318: 				ErrInterfaceUnowned,
319: 				ifaceName,
320: 				node.GetShortName(),
321: 			)
322: 		}
323: 
324: 		if err = netlink.LinkDel(link); err != nil {
325: 			return err
326: 		}
327: 
328: 		return removeBridgePort(node, ifaceName)
329: 	})
330: }
331: 
332: // bridgePortDeleter removes a bridge port that can outlive its netdev. OVS ports created for an
333: // interface name Linux will not accept are named after the random netdev, so deleting the veth
334: // from the container side leaves the port behind.
335: type bridgePortDeleter interface {
336: 	DeleteBridgePort(string) error
337: }
338: 
339: func removeBridgePort(node Node, ifaceName string) error {
340: 	if node == nil || ifaceName == "" {
341: 		return nil
342: 	}
343: 
344: 	cleaner, ok := node.(bridgePortDeleter)
345: 	if !ok {
346: 		return nil
347: 	}
348: 
349: 	// Best-effort, matching ovs.Delete. A missing bridge or a down ovsdb must not abort
350: 	// destroy or reconcile and leave the container running.
351: 	if err := cleaner.DeleteBridgePort(ifaceName); err != nil {
352: 		log.Errorf(
353: 			"Could not remove bridge port %q on node %q: %v",
354: 			ifaceName,
355: 			node.GetShortName(),
356: 			err,
357: 		)
358: 	}
359: 
360: 	return nil
361: }
362: 
363: // isOwnedBy reports whether link carries the ownership marker of the logical
364: // endpoint ownerName:ifaceName. Interfaces of mgmt-net links deployed by earlier
365: // releases carry a marker for the bridge name of the mgmt-net link node instead
366: // of the stable mgmt-net owner name, and are accepted as well.
367: func isOwnedBy(link netlink.Link, node Node, ownerName, ifaceName string) bool {
368: 	if HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, ownerName, ifaceName) {
369: 		return true
370: 	}
371: 
372: 	if _, ok := node.(*mgmtBridgeLinkNode); ok && ownerName == mgmtNetOwnerName {
373: 		return HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, node.GetShortName(), ifaceName)
374: 	}
375: 
376: 	return false
377: }

# PR Review: BridgeNS migration and reconcile support

## Summary

This PR adds migration support for in-container bridges (`bridge` kind with `network-mode: container:<parent>`, "BridgeNS") to the `apply` reconcile flow: bridge-side veth ends are parked into a dedicated named netns while the parent/bridge is replaced, then restored and re-enslaved into the replacement bridge. It also wires the nodes map into namespace-sharing nodes, groups BridgeNS bridges as `rootNamespaceBased` in runtime state so they can be planned as added nodes, and adds a full robot suite covering move, drift, add, and remove scenarios.

The core happy paths traced correctly (move with unchanged client, parent recreation, add/remove clients). Three defects were found in the new migration machinery: migrations are planned without validating that the client-side peer survives the apply (leading to a **persistent** apply failure, since failed applies never persist state), the new `UnlinkNamedNetNS` helper cannot delete a bind-mounted netns and silently leaks parking namespaces, and an interrupted migration cannot be resumed by a later apply. Two P4 maintainability items round out the review (dead code plus a comment describing a nonexistent mechanism, and a type assertion that can panic).

## Findings

| # | Priority | Title | Location |
|---|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | P2 | Migration planned by port name only; destroyed client peer makes apply fail persistently | `core/topology_reconcile.go` |
| 2 | P2 | `UnlinkNamedNetNS` cannot remove a bind-mounted netns, so parking namespaces leak | `utils/netlink.go` |
| 3 | P3 | Interrupted bridge-port migration is unrecoverable; parking is not idempotent | `links/migration.go` |
| 4 | P4 | Dead `LinkDeploymentStateSetter`/`SetDeploymentState` and a comment describing a nonexistent mechanism | `links/apply.go`, `links/link_veth.go`, `core/apply_bridge_migration.go` |
| 5 | P4 | `enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace` type-asserts `*netlink.Bridge` and can panic | `nodes/bridge/bridge.go` |

### 1. Migration planned by port name only; destroyed client peer makes apply fail persistently — P2

Location: [core/topology_reconcile.go#L482-L518](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L482-L518) (`addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate`), with the failure surfacing in [core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L17-L34](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L17-L34) and [links/migration.go#L90-L124](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L90-L124).

`addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate` matches a stale bridge-side endpoint to a desired endpoint purely by identical port name under a different BridgeNS node (`candidate.iface != staleKey.iface || candidate.node == staleKey.node`). It never inspects the *client-side* peer of the old port and never checks that the migration is feasible — yet the struct's own comment asserts "the client-side endpoint and the veth pair itself stay valid" ([core/topology_reconcile.go#L35-L40](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L35-L40)). Three concrete breaks follow:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[apply: migration planned by port name] --> B{old client end fate}
    B -->|rewired to eth2, c1 stays| C[deleteApplyEndpoints deletes c1:eth1<br/>veth pair destroyed]
    B -->|c1 node removed| D[park succeeds<br/>c1 container deleted<br/>peer destroyed, parked half destroyed too]
    B -->|bp1 removed from topology| E[bridgeNSMigParentNode: parent not found]
    C --> F[park fails: ownership altname not found]
    D --> G[restore fails: parked iface not found]
    F --> H[apply aborts, state not persisted]
    E --> H
    G --> H
    H --> I[next apply re-plans same migration from stale state<br/>fails identically - lab bricked until destroy]
```

**Triggers.** (a) The client link is rewired to another interface in the same apply as the bridge move (e.g. old `c1:eth1–br01|bp1:c1eth1` becomes `c1:eth2–br02|bp1:c1eth1`): since `applyKnownEndpointNames` returns `nil` for regular nodes ([core/topology_reconcile.go#L854-L870](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L854-L870)), the old `c1:eth1` is still discovered, becomes a stale endpoint, and `deleteApplyEndpoints` deletes it at step 1 — destroying the whole veth pair — before `parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts` runs at step 2. (b) The client node is removed from the topology in the same apply: parking succeeds (step 2 runs before node deletion), but deleting the client container destroys its netns, which destroys the veth peer and with it the parked half, so `RestoreBridgePort` fails with "parked interface not found in parking ns". (c) The old bridge's parent is also removed from the topology in the same apply (bridge moved from `br01|bp1` to `br02|bp2`): `bridgeNSMigParentNode` resolves parents only from `c.Nodes` (desired topology) and returns "parent container not found", aborting at step 2.

**Impact.** Because every apply step returns early on error before `finalize`/`writeState` ([core/apply.go#L207-L241](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/apply.go#L207-L241)), the failed apply persists nothing; the next apply re-plans the identical migration from the unchanged state and fails identically. The lab is bricked for that port until `destroy` — which destroys exactly the client-side state migration exists to preserve. Even variant (c), which mutates nothing, is persistent and fails with a confusing error.

**Correction.** Validate candidates at planning time: skip a migration when the old bridge's parent cannot be resolved from the desired topology (the normal delete/recreate path already handles that case correctly), and require that the old link's client-side endpoint matches the new link's client endpoint and is not deleted/replaced in this plan. A unit test asserting the guard on `addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate` would be the smallest useful check; the new robot suite only covers the move with an unchanged client, so none of these variants is currently exercised.

### 2. `UnlinkNamedNetNS` cannot remove a bind-mounted netns, so parking namespaces leak — P2

Location: [utils/netlink.go#L233-L240](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/utils/netlink.go#L233-L240), callers [links/migration.go#L79](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L79) and [links/migration.go#L178](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L178).

The parking netns is created with `netns.NewNamed` ([utils/netlink.go#L201](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/utils/netlink.go#L201)), which bind-mounts the network namespace onto `/run/netns/<name>`. `os.Remove` (unlink) on a mount point fails with `EBUSY` on Linux — this is precisely why the existing machinery uses `netns.DeleteNamed`, which umounts first ([nodes/default_node.go#L463-L470](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/nodes/default_node.go#L463-L470), [nodes/sros/netns.go#L74-L80](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/nodes/sros/netns.go#L74-L80)). Both call sites discard the error (`_ =`), so the cleanup silently does nothing.

**Trigger.** Any bridge-port migration: the success path at `RestoreBridgePort` (line 178) leaks the netns on every migration, and the park-error path (line 79) leaks the freshly created one. `CreateOrGetNamedNetNS` reuses a name, so the leak is one entry per distinct bridge long name, but the entries persist after lab destroy.

**Impact.** `clab-park-<longName>` entries accumulate in `/run/netns`, visible to `ip netns list` and other tooling, survive lab destroy, and mislead operators into thinking a netns is in use. The leaked netns is empty in the common case, so it is a hygiene leak rather than data loss — but the failure is silent and guaranteed on the success path.

**Correction.** Replace `UnlinkNamedNetNS`'s body with the established pattern (`netns.DeleteNamed`/umount+unlink, matching `cleanupParkingNetNS`), and handle the returned error instead of `_ =`, at minimum logging at debug level.

### 3. Interrupted bridge-port migration is unrecoverable; parking is not idempotent — P3

Location: [links/migration.go#L57-L77](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L57-L77), planning in [core/topology_reconcile.go#L437-L477](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L437-L477).

Once `ParkBridgePortByOwnership` has moved a bridge-side end into the parking netns, the port carries the *old* bridge's ownership altname and sits in a namespace discovery never scans. If the apply then fails before `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` (for example, a later node deploy error unrelated to the migration), the state file is unchanged, so the next apply re-plans the same migration — and `findLinkByOwnershipAltName` now fails in the parent's netns because the port is already parked. Conversely, if a later apply succeeds for other reasons and no migration is planned, the parked port becomes invisible garbage forever.

**Trigger.** Any failure between step 2 (`parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts`) and step 8 (`restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts`) of the apply sequence in [core/apply.go#L207-L241](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/apply.go#L207-L241).

**Impact.** A transient failure converts a healthy lab into one where every subsequent apply aborts at the park step, and where abandoning the migration silently strands the port.

**Correction.** Make parking idempotent: before moving the port, check the parking netns of `longName` for an interface with the ownership altname and, if found, skip the move and proceed with restore. This turns an interrupted migration into a resumable one with a small, local change.

### 4. Dead `LinkDeploymentStateSetter`/`SetDeploymentState` and a comment describing a nonexistent mechanism — P4

Location: [links/apply.go#L79-L84](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/apply.go#L79-L84), [links/link_veth.go#L156-L159](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/link_veth.go#L156-L159), [core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L86-L90](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L86-L90).

This PR introduces the `LinkDeploymentStateSetter` interface and `LinkVEth.SetDeploymentState`, but a repository-wide search finds no call sites (all other `DeploymentState` mutations are internal to each link type). Meanwhile the `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` comment claims "The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed so deployLinks skips pair re-creation for it" — no such marking exists; the actual mechanism is the `plan.addedLinks` filtering four lines below. The comment would send the next maintainer hunting for a mechanism that does not exist.

**Trigger/impact.** Read-only maintenance cost; dead exported interface and misleading documentation of the restore path.

**Correction.** Delete the interface and method, or wire them up if they were intended for something; reword the comment to describe the actual `plan.addedLinks` filtering.

### 5. `enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace` type-asserts `*netlink.Bridge` and can panic — P4

Location: [nodes/bridge/bridge.go#L308](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/nodes/bridge/bridge.go#L308).

`netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName)` is type-asserted to `*netlink.Bridge`. `LinkByName` decodes by kernel kind, so if any other device (for example a leftover veth whose port name collides with the bridge name) currently holds `bridgeName`, the assertion panics inside the PostDeploy hook rather than producing an error.

**Trigger.** A device other than a bridge occupying the bridge's name in the parent's netns during `PostDeploy` — an edge case, but a panic aborts the whole apply with no diagnostics.

**Impact.** Crash instead of a clean error; low likelihood.

**Correction.** Compare `link.Attrs().MasterIndex != bridgeLink.Attrs().Index` on the `netlink.Link` interface — the assertion is not needed for the master check at all.

- `checkApplyNetworkModeTargets` guard behavior, the `rootNamespaceBased` BridgeNS grouping in `core/runtime_state.go`, and the `SetNodesMap` wiring in `core/config.go` were verified and are correct; no findings there.

## Important Details

- PR subject: BridgeNS (in-container bridge via `network-mode: container:<parent>`) migration/reconciliation during `apply`. Bridge nodes named `<bridge>|<parent>`; ownership via netlink altnames; parking netns moves veth ends between parent namespaces.
- All 21 changed paths confirmed (manifest tail resolved, nothing truncated): `core/{apply.go, apply_bridge_migration.go, apply_test.go, config.go, network_mode_test.go, runtime_state.go, topology_reconcile.go}`, `links/{apply.go, link_veth.go, migration.go, ownership.go}`, `nodes/{bridge/bridge.go, node.go}`, `utils/netlink.go`, `tests/01-smoke/34-bridge-ns-reconcile.{clab.yml, robot}` + 5 `.vars.*.yml`.
- Apply order confirmed (head `core/apply.go:207-243`): `deleteApplyEndpoints` → `parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts` → `parkRecreatedNodes` → `deleteApplyNodes` → `deployApplyNodes` → `restoreRecreatedNodes` → `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` → `removeApplyLinkEndpoints(plan.addedLinks)` → `deployLinks` → bridge PostDeploy (`enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace`). Any step error returns before `finalize`/`writeState`, so failed applies never persist new state → failed plans repeat identically on retry.
- **Consolidated findings (final candidates for report):**
  - **P2 (root cause single):** `addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate` (core/topology_reconcile.go:482-518) plans migrations purely by bridge-side port-name matching under a different bridge node, without validating feasibility. Manifestations, all causing **persistent, unrecoverable apply failure** (state never written → same failing plan repeats until `destroy`):
    1. Rewire during bridge move (e.g. `c1:eth1–br01|bp1:c1eth1` → `c1:eth2–br02|bp1:c1eth1`): `applyKnownEndpointNames` returns nil for regular nodes (topology_reconcile.go:854-870), so old client end `c1:eth1` IS discovered (ownership altname set on both veth ends via `addOwnershipAltName` in `SetNameMACAndUpInterface`, links/link.go:609) → deleted at step 1 → veth pair destroyed → parking at step 2 fails (`findLinkByOwnershipAltName` not found).
    2. Client removed during bridge move (e.g. `c1` removed, port reused by new link `c2:eth1–br02|bp1:c1eth1`): parking succeeds (runs before node deletion), then c1 container teardown destroys the peer → parked end destroyed (veth pair semantics) → restore fails with parked interface not found.
    3. Old parent removed in same apply (`br01|bp1`→`br02|bp2`, bp1 deleted): `bridgeNSMigParentNode` (core/apply_bridge_migration.go:17-34) fails — `c.Nodes[parts[1]]` only holds desired nodes → park stage aborts with confusing `parent container %q not found`; lab otherwise intact. Fix: skip migration planning when old parent not resolvable from desired topology (delete+recreate path handles it correctly).
    - Supporting evidence: `bridgeNSMigration` doc comment (topology_reconcile.go:375-379) asserts "client-side endpoint and the veth pair itself stay valid" — exactly what's violated.
  - **P2 (leak):** `UnlinkNamedNetNS` (utils/netlink.go:233-240) uses `os.Remove`, but `CreateNamedNetNS` uses `netns.NewNamed` (utils/netlink.go:185-212) which bind-mounts `/run/netns/<name>` → `os.Remove` returns EBUSY → error silently ignored (`_ =` at links/migration.go:79 error path and :178 success path) → parking netns (`clab-park-<bridgeLongName>`) leaks on every migration. Fix: use `netns.DeleteNamed` (umount+unlink) as in nodes/default_node.go:469, nodes/sros/netns.go:80.
  - **P4 (dead code):** `LinkVEth.SetDeploymentState` (links/link_veth.go:156-159, added in this PR) and `LinkDeploymentStateSetter` interface (links/apply.go:79-84) have zero call sites (`grep "\.SetDeploymentState\("` → none).
  - **P4 (misleading comment):** `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` comment (core/apply_bridge_migration.go:~89-90) claims "The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed so deployLinks skips pair re-creation" — actual mechanism is filtering the link from `plan.addedLinks`.
  - **P4 (panic-risk hardening, new in PR):** `enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace` type-asserts `bridgeLink.(*netlink.Bridge)` (nodes/bridge/bridge.go:308) — could panic if a non-bridge link holds the bridge name; cleaner: compare `link.Attrs().MasterIndex != bridgeLink.Attrs().Index` on the Link interface.
- Verified-safe / classification items:
  - `CheckDeploymentConditions` slicing (`b.Cfg.NetworkMode[10:]` vs `GetShortName()[len(...)+1:]`, head bridge.go:356-360) is **pre-existing** (identical in base bridge.go:164-167) → not a PR finding.
  - `deleteApplyEndpoints` `ref.node.GetLinkEndpointType()` deref (topology_reconcile.go:1234) is safe — all `plan.staleEndpoints` entries have non-nil node (only populated via `addStaleApplyEndpoint` :545-570 and `addDerivedHostStaleEndpoints` :581-616; deleted-node candidates go only to `bridgeNSMigrations`).
  - `deleteApplyEndpoints` BridgeNS branch skips migration-planned endpoints ("Preserving bridge port for migration", :1235-1240).
  - `bridgeNSParentNode` (topology_reconcile.go:713-735); orphan discovery keys under the CURRENT desired bridge node; ports of a removed bridge with old-owner altname are invisible (orphan requires MasterIndex == desired bridge index) — leftover bridge ifaces in surviving parents are never removed because `bridge.Delete` is a noop (head bridge.go:225-229, same in base) → pre-existing behavior → coverage note, not a finding.
  - `deleteApplyNodes` skips `rootNamespaceBased` nodes (core/destroy.go:582-583).
  - Robot test suite (`34-bridge-ns-reconcile`) covers initial deploy, add-c3, remove-c2, move-bridge, drift-parent — but NOT any changed-client or removed-parent migration scenario → recommend smallest useful check: unit test on the planning guard in `addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate`.
  - Prior verified-safe items stand: cross-netns `linkIntact` PeerIndex exact; `br01|bp2` added-node planning via `rootNamespaceBased` branch in core/runtime_state.go; `checkApplyNetworkModeTargets` guards deleted network-mode targets; `planParkedNodes` only iterates `recreatedNodeSet`; `SetNodesMap`/`WireNodesMapToNodes` wired at core/config.go:182 and :294, bridge.go implements `NamespaceSharerNodesSetter`; `LinkApplyMode` default `LinkApplyModeLive` for linux kind (nodes/linux/linux.go:43).
- Tool note: read of `/source` root dir listing denied; `read /source/<file>` works.
- Link endpoint types confirmed: `LinkEndpointTypeVeth/Bridge/BridgeNS/Host` (links/link.go:560-565).

36: // of (ownerName, ifaceName) in src's namespace and parks it into the parking

38: func ParkBridgePortByOwnership(
39: 	ctx context.Context,
40: 	src Node,
41: 	ownerName string,
42: 	ifaceName string,
43: 	longName string,
44: ) (*BridgePortRelocation, error) {
45: 	parkPath, err := clabutils.CreateOrGetNamedNetNS(clabutils.ParkingNetnsName(longName))
46: 	if err != nil {
47: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create parking netns for migration: %w", err)
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	relocation := &BridgePortRelocation{

52: 		OldOwnerName: ownerName,
53: 		IfaceName:    ifaceName,
54: 		LongName:     longName,

59: 		if err != nil {
60: 			return err
61: 		}
62: 
63: 		relocation.KernelName = link.Attrs().Name
64: 
65: 		if err := netlink.LinkSetDown(link); err != nil {
66: 			log.Debug("failed to bring down interface while parking",

70: 		parkNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(parkPath)
71: 		if nsErr != nil {
72: 			return nsErr
73: 		}

75:

88: // ownership altname to (newOwnerName, ifaceName) and re-enslaves it to the
89: // bridge. dst receives a node with both ExecFunction and GetNSPath.
90: func (r *BridgePortRelocation) RestoreBridgePort(
91: 	ctx context.Context,
92: 	dst NSMigrationNode,
93: 	newOwnerName string,
94: 	bridgeName string,
95: 	desiredKernelName string,
96: ) error {

98: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.KernelName)
99: 		if err != nil {
100: 			return fmt.Errorf("parked interface %q not found in parking ns: %w", r.KernelName, err)
101: 		}
102: 
103: 		dstPath, nsErr := dst.GetNSPath(ctx)
104: 		if nsErr != nil {
105: 			return nsErr
106: 		}
107: 		dstNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(dstPath)
108: 		if nsErr != nil {
109: 			return nsErr
110: 		}
111: 		defer dstNs.Close()
112: 
113: 		return netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(dstNs.Fd()))
114: 	})
115: 	if parkExecErr != nil {
116: 		return parkExecErr
117: 	}
118: 
119: 	dstErr := dst.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
120: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.KernelName)
121: 		if err != nil {
122: 			return fmt.Errorf("restored interface %q not found in destination ns: %w",
123: 				r.KernelName, err)
124: 		}
125: 
126: 		if desiredKernelName != "" && link.Attrs().Name != desiredKernelName {
127: 			if err := netlink.LinkSetName(link, desiredKernelName); err != nil {
128: 				return err
129: 			}
130: 			link.Attrs().Name = desiredKernelName
131: 		}
132: 
133: 		// Strip previous ownership markers and label with the new owner.
134: 		for _, altName := range link.Attrs().AltNames {
135: 			if !strings.HasPrefix(altName, ownershipAltNamePrefix) {
136: 				continue
137: 			}
138: 			if delErr := netlink.LinkDelAltName(link, altName); delErr != nil &&
139: 				!isAltNameNotSupportedErr(delErr) {
140: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to drop old ownership altname %q: %w", altName, delErr)
141: 			}
142: 		}
143: 		if addErr := linkAddAltName(
144: 			link,
145: 			ownershipAltNameFor(newOwnerName, r.IfaceName),
146: 		); addErr != nil &&

13: // bridgeNSMigParentNode resolves the namespace host of a migrated bridge-side
14: // endpoint. Stale refs carry either a live bridge node (resolved via the
15: // topology) or the name-encoded <bridge>|<parent> form of a node that is
16: // already removed from the desired topology.
17: func (c *CLab) bridgeNSMigParentNode(ref applyEndpointRef) (clablinks.Node, error) {
18: 	if parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSParentNode(ref.key.node); err == nil {
19: 		return parentNode, nil
20: 	}
21: 	parts := strings.SplitN(ref.key.node, "|", 2)
22: 	if len(parts) != 2 {
23: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot resolve namespace host of bridge %q", ref.key.node)
24: 	}
25: 	node, exists := c.Nodes[parts[1]]
26: 	if !exists {
27: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
28: 			"bridge %q: parent container %q not found",
29: 			ref.key.node,
30: 			parts[1],
31: 		)
32: 	}
33: 	return node, nil
34: }
35: 
36: // parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts parks bridge-side veth ends whose owning in-container
37: // bridge was replaced by a bridge under a different parent (the move case).
38: // The veth pair stays intact: only the parked half leaves the dying parent's
39: // namespace, so the client-side end keeps its state untouched.
40: func (c *CLab) parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts(
41: 	ctx context.Context,
42: 	plan *applyPlan,
43: ) error {
44: 	if plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {
45: 		return nil
46: 	}
47: 
48: 	for i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
49: 		mig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]
50: 
51: 		if mig.relocation != nil {
52: 			continue
53: 		}
54: 
55: 		// The old bridge node may already be deleted from the desired topology
56: 		// (the move case); resolve its namespace host by the name-encoded
57: 		// parent suffix, falling back to the normal resolution.
58: 		parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSMigParentNode(mig.staleRef)
59: 		if err != nil {
60: 			return err
61: 		}
62: 
63: 		newNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]
64: 		if !exists {
65: 			return fmt.Errorf("bridge migration target %q not found", mig.newKey.node)
66: 		}
67: 		longName := newNode.Config().LongName
68: 
69: 		relocation, err := clablinks.ParkBridgePortByOwnership(
70: 			ctx,
71: 			parentNode,
72: 			mig.staleRef.key.node,
73: 			mig.staleRef.key.iface,
74: 			longName,
75: 		)
76: 		if err != nil {
77: 			return err
78: 		}
79: 
80: 		mig.relocation = relocation
81: 	}
82: 
83: 	return nil
84: }

86: // restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts moves parked bridge-side ends into the replacement
87: // bridge's parent namespace after that container (and the bridge) exist again,
88: // relabels the ownership altname to the replacement bridge node, and re-enslaves
89: // the port to the bridge. The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed so
90: // deployLinks skips pair re-creation for it.
91: func (c *CLab) restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts(
92: 	ctx context.Context,
93: 	plan *applyPlan,
94: ) error {
95: 	if plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {
96: 		return nil
97: 	}
98: 
99: 	for i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
100: 		mig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]
101: 
102: 		if mig.relocation == nil || plan.plannedLinkSet == nil {
103: 			continue
104: 		}
105: 
106: 		// Restore into the replacement bridge's parent namespace; the bridge
107: 		// node interfaces with the parent's ns through its GetNSPath override.
108: 		bridgeNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]
109: 		if !exists {
110: 			return fmt.Errorf("bridge migration target %q not found", mig.newKey.node)
111: 		}
112: 
113: 		if err := mig.relocation.RestoreBridgePort(
114: 			ctx,

# PR Review: BridgeNS migration and reconcile support

## Summary

This PR adds migration support for in-container bridges (`bridge` kind with `network-mode: container:<parent>`, "BridgeNS") to the `apply` reconcile flow: bridge-side veth ends are parked into a dedicated named netns while the parent/bridge is replaced, then restored and re-enslaved into the replacement bridge. It also wires the nodes map into namespace-sharing nodes, groups BridgeNS bridges as `rootNamespaceBased` in runtime state so they can be planned as added nodes, and adds a full robot suite covering move, drift, add, and remove scenarios.

The core happy paths traced correctly (move with unchanged client, parent recreation, add/remove clients). Three defects were found in the new migration machinery: migrations are planned without validating that the client-side peer survives the apply (leading to a **persistent** apply failure, since failed applies never persist state), the new `UnlinkNamedNetNS` helper cannot delete a bind-mounted netns and silently leaks parking namespaces, and an interrupted migration cannot be resumed by a later apply. Two P4 maintainability items round out the review (dead code plus a comment describing a nonexistent mechanism, and a type assertion that can panic).

## Findings

| # | Priority | Title | Location |
|---|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | P2 | Migration planned by port name only; destroyed client peer makes apply fail persistently | `core/topology_reconcile.go` |
| 2 | P2 | `UnlinkNamedNetNS` cannot remove a bind-mounted netns, so parking namespaces leak | `utils/netlink.go` |
| 3 | P3 | Interrupted bridge-port migration is unrecoverable; parking is not idempotent | `links/migration.go` |
| 4 | P4 | Dead `LinkDeploymentStateSetter`/`SetDeploymentState` and a comment describing a nonexistent mechanism | `links/apply.go`, `links/link_veth.go`, `core/apply_bridge_migration.go` |
| 5 | P4 | `enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace` type-asserts `*netlink.Bridge` and can panic | `nodes/bridge/bridge.go` |

### 1. Migration planned by port name only; destroyed client peer makes apply fail persistently — P2

Location: [core/topology_reconcile.go#L482-L518](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L482-L518) (`addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate`), with the assumption stated at [core/topology_reconcile.go#L35-L40](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L35-L40) and failures surfacing in [core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L17-L34](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L17-L34) and [links/migration.go#L97-L101](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L97-L101).

`addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate` matches a stale bridge-side endpoint to a desired endpoint purely by identical port name under a different BridgeNS node ([core/topology_reconcile.go#L497-L503](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L497-L503)). It never inspects the *client-side* peer of the old port and never checks that the migration is feasible — yet the struct's own comment asserts "the client-side endpoint and the veth pair itself stay valid" ([core/topology_reconcile.go#L35-L40](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L35-L40)). Three concrete breaks follow:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[apply: migration planned by port name] --> B{old client end fate}
    B -->|rewired to eth2, c1 stays| C[deleteApplyEndpoints deletes c1:eth1<br/>veth pair destroyed]
    B -->|c1 node removed| D[park succeeds<br/>c1 container deleted<br/>peer destroyed, parked half destroyed too]
    B -->|bp1 removed from topology| E[bridgeNSMigParentNode: parent not found]
    C --> F[park fails: ownership altname not found]
    D --> G[restore fails: parked iface not found]
    F --> H[apply aborts, state not persisted]
    E --> H
    G --> H
    H --> I[next apply re-plans same migration from stale state<br/>fails identically - lab bricked until destroy]
```

**Triggers.** (a) The client link is rewired to another interface in the same apply as the bridge move (e.g. old `c1:eth1–br01|bp1:c1eth1` becomes `c1:eth2–br02|bp1:c1eth1`): since `applyKnownEndpointNames` returns `nil` for regular nodes ([core/topology_reconcile.go#L854-L870](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L854-L870)), the old `c1:eth1` is still discovered, becomes a stale endpoint, and `deleteApplyEndpoints` deletes it at step 1 — destroying the whole veth pair — before `parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts` runs at step 2. (b) The client node is removed from the topology in the same apply: parking succeeds (step 2 runs before node deletion), but deleting the client container destroys its netns, which destroys the veth peer and with it the parked half, so `RestoreBridgePort` fails with "parked interface %q not found in parking ns" ([links/migration.go#L97-L101](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L97-L101)). (c) The old bridge's parent is also removed from the topology in the same apply (bridge moved from `br01|bp1` to `br02|bp2`): `bridgeNSMigParentNode` resolves parents only from `c.Nodes` (desired topology) and returns "parent container %q not found", aborting at step 2.

**Impact.** Because every apply step returns early on error before `finalize`/`writeState` ([core/apply.go#L207-L241](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/apply.go#L207-L241)), the failed apply persists nothing; the next apply re-plans the identical migration from the unchanged state and fails identically. The lab is bricked for that port until `destroy` — which destroys exactly the client-side state migration exists to preserve. Even variant (c), which mutates nothing, is persistent and fails with a confusing error.

**Correction.** Validate candidates at planning time: skip a migration when the old bridge's parent cannot be resolved from the desired topology (the normal delete/recreate path already handles that case correctly), and require that the old link's client-side endpoint matches the new link's client endpoint and is not deleted/replaced in this plan. A unit test asserting the guard on `addBridgeNSMigrationCandidate` would be the smallest useful check; the new robot suite only covers the move with an unchanged client, so none of these variants is currently exercised.

### 2. `UnlinkNamedNetNS` cannot remove a bind-mounted netns, so parking namespaces leak — P2

Location: [utils/netlink.go#L233-L240](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/utils/netlink.go#L233-L240), callers [links/migration.go#L79](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L79) and [links/migration.go#L178](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L178).

The parking netns is created with `netns.NewNamed` ([utils/netlink.go#L201](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/utils/netlink.go#L201)), which bind-mounts the network namespace onto `/run/netns/<name>`. `os.Remove` (unlink) on a mount point fails with `EBUSY` on Linux — this is precisely why the existing machinery uses `netns.DeleteNamed`, which umounts first ([nodes/default_node.go#L463-L470](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/nodes/default_node.go#L463-L470), [nodes/sros/netns.go#L74-L80](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/nodes/sros/netns.go#L74-L80)). Both call sites discard the error (`_ =`), so the cleanup silently does nothing.

**Trigger.** Any bridge-port migration: the success path at `RestoreBridgePort` (line 178) leaks the netns on every migration, and the park-error path (line 79) leaks the freshly created one. `CreateOrGetNamedNetNS` reuses a name, so the leak is one entry per distinct bridge long name, but the entries persist after lab destroy.

**Impact.** `clab-park-<longName>` entries accumulate in `/run/netns`, visible to `ip netns list` and other tooling, survive lab destroy, and mislead operators into thinking a netns is in use. The leaked netns is empty in the common case, so it is a hygiene leak rather than data loss — but the failure is silent and guaranteed on the success path.

**Correction.** Replace `UnlinkNamedNetNS`'s body with the established pattern (`netns.DeleteNamed`/umount+unlink, matching `cleanupParkingNetNS`), and handle the returned error instead of `_ =`, at minimum logging at debug level.

### 3. Interrupted bridge-port migration is unrecoverable; parking is not idempotent — P3

Location: [links/migration.go#L57-L81](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/migration.go#L57-L81), planning in [core/topology_reconcile.go#L437-L477](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/topology_reconcile.go#L437-L477).

Once `ParkBridgePortByOwnership` has moved a bridge-side end into the parking netns, the port carries the *old* bridge's ownership altname and sits in a namespace discovery never scans. If the apply then fails before `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` (for example, a later node deploy error unrelated to the migration), the state file is unchanged, so the next apply re-plans the same migration — and `findLinkByOwnershipAltName` now fails in the parent's netns because the port is already parked. Conversely, if a later apply succeeds for other reasons and no migration is planned, the parked port becomes invisible garbage forever.

**Trigger.** Any failure between step 2 (`parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts`) and step 8 (`restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts`) of the apply sequence in [core/apply.go#L207-L241](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/apply.go#L207-L241).

**Impact.** A transient failure converts a healthy lab into one where every subsequent apply aborts at the park step, and where abandoning the migration silently strands the port.

**Correction.** Make parking idempotent: before moving the port, check the parking netns of `longName` for an interface with the ownership altname and, if found, skip the move and proceed with restore. This turns an interrupted migration into a resumable one with a small, local change.

### 4. Dead `LinkDeploymentStateSetter`/`SetDeploymentState` and a comment describing a nonexistent mechanism — P4

Location: [links/apply.go#L79-L84](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/apply.go#L79-L84), [links/link_veth.go#L156-L159](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/links/link_veth.go#L156-L159), [core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L89-L90](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L89-L90).

This PR introduces the `LinkDeploymentStateSetter` interface and `LinkVEth.SetDeploymentState`, but a repository-wide search finds no call sites (all other `DeploymentState` mutations are internal to each link type). Meanwhile the `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` comment claims "The corresponding live link is marked full-deployed so deployLinks skips pair re-creation for it" — no such marking exists; the actual mechanism is the `plan.addedLinks` filtering a few lines below ([core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L123-L145](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L123-L145)). The comment would send the next maintainer hunting for a mechanism that does not exist.

**Trigger/impact.** Read-only maintenance cost; dead exported interface and misleading documentation of the restore path.

**Correction.** Delete the interface and method, or wire them up if they were intended for something; reword the comment to describe the actual `plan.addedLinks` filtering.

### 5. `enslaveBridgePortsInNamespace` type-asserts `*netlink.Bridge` and can panic — P4

Location: [nodes/bridge/bridge.go#L308](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/192dec107ced8f608c230f6822578c3f5742037a/nodes/bridge/bridge.go#L308).

`netlink.LinkByName(bridgeName)` is type-asserted to `*netlink.Bridge`. `LinkByName` decodes by kernel kind, so if any other device (for example a leftover veth whose port name collides with the bridge name) currently holds `bridgeName`, the assertion panics inside the PostDeploy hook rather than producing an error.

**Trigger.** A device other than a bridge occupying the bridge's name in the parent's netns during `PostDeploy` — an edge case, but a panic aborts the whole apply with no diagnostics.

**Impact.** Crash instead of a clean error; low likelihood.

**Correction.** Compare `link.Attrs().MasterIndex != bridgeLink.Attrs().Index` on the `netlink.Link` interface — the assertion is not needed for the master check at all.

## Coverage notes

- All 21 changed paths from `manifest.json` were examined, including full reads of `core/apply.go`, `core/apply_bridge_migration.go`, `links/migration.go`, `links/ownership.go`, and the relevant sections of `core/topology_reconcile.go`, `nodes/bridge/bridge.go`, `utils/netlink.go`, `nodes/node.go`, and `core/config.go`; findings were traced through callers in both head and base.
- Tests were **not executed** (review is source-only); conclusions on runtime behavior are derived from code semantics, including Linux veth pair semantics and `netns.NewNamed` mount behavior.
- The new robot suite (`tests/01-smoke/34-bridge-ns-reconcile.*`) covers move-with-same-client, parent drift, add/remove clients, and idempotency; none of the finding-1 variants (client rewire/removal combined with a bridge move) is covered.
- Pre-existing issues deliberately excluded: the `CheckDeploymentConditions` unguarded slicing `b.Cfg.NetworkMode[10:]` / `b.GetShortName()[len(...)+1:]` exists identically in base ([base/nodes/bridge/bridge.go#L158-L168](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/6e94d1e5e7c0b2c3b328cfd9037e42fb98e55040/nodes/bridge/bridge.go#L158-L168)), and `bridge.Delete` being a noop (leaving a removed in-container bridge behind in the parent) is also pre-existing; the new migration flow depends on the latter but does not worsen it.
- Documentation check: the BridgeNS feature and its `<bridge>|<parent>` naming are already documented in `docs/manual/kinds/bridge.md` (unchanged in this PR); migration is an internal apply behavior, so no doc or schema update is required by this PR.
- `checkApplyNetworkModeTargets` guard behavior, the `rootNamespaceBased` BridgeNS grouping in `core/runtime_state.go`, and the `SetNodesMap` wiring in `core/config.go` were verified and are correct; no findings there.
